title: Algorithmic Marketing Intensity and Consumer Resistance in AI-Driven Advertising: A PLS-SEM Analysis of Social Media Users
affiliations: Independent University, Bangladesh (IUB)

detail.title: Algorithmic Marketing Intensity and Consumer Resistance in AI-Driven Advertising: A PLS-SEM Analysis of Social Media Users
detail.abstract: Introduction: The increased application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and algorithmic processes has changed the nature of digital advertising by creating very personalized marketing messages. Although algorithmic personalization could enhance advertising relevance and interactions, overly algorithmic targeting can also lead to adverse reaction among consumers. Objectives: This paper investigates the role of the intensity of algorithmic marketing in resisting consumers in the context of AI-driven advertising. Theoretical Framework: Based on psychological reactance theory and technology overload theory, our conceptual model is that the intensity of algorithmic marketing augments the feeling of personalization and cognitive overburden which, in turn, results in consumer resistance and avoidance behavior. Methodology: The data was gathered with 400 social media users who had been subjected to personalized digital advertising, and they were examined with the help of Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Moderating Variable: The model also examines how artificial intelligence moderates the negative consumer responses through the moderating role of trust. Key Findings: The findings suggest that perceived personalization and cognitive strain caused by the strength of the algorithmic marketing have great influence, leading to consumer resistance and avoidance of ads. In addition, consumer resistance decreases with trust in AI and undermines the connection between cognitive strain and resistance. Contribution/Significance: The results add to the literature on algorithmic marketing and consumer behavior by identifying the psychological processes underlying resistance to advertising by AI.

title: Royalty-free Licensing in Standards
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Royalty-free Licensing in Standards

declarations.funderStatement: Self Funded

detail.abstract: Royalty-free FRAND licensing has played an important role in the development and adoption of many successful technical standards. When used in a transparent, voluntary, and properly governed standards-development process, these commitments can reduce licensing friction, increase implementation certainty, and help markets scale around interoperable technology. That does not make a zero-royalty approach the right answer in every case. But the long record of successful royalty-free standards shows that properly structured policies can enable broad adoption, expand downstream markets, and support innovation without inherently creating the antitrust harms some have attributed to zero-royalty commitments.

title: Economics-informed Deep Learning for High-dimensional Dynamic Stochastic General Equilibrium Models
affiliations: University of Münster - Faculty of Economics

detail.title: Economics-informed Deep Learning for High-dimensional Dynamic Stochastic General Equilibrium Models
detail.abstract: Deep learning has been shown to enable global solutions to high-dimensional, complex economic models. However, although the need for global methods that can handle large shocks and nonlinearities, such as occasionally binding constraints, is evident, neural network solvers are still adopted only hesitantly in practice. This is partly due to a lack of stability and, more importantly, their substantial computational cost relative to inexpensive local approximation methods. In this paper, I propose a new method called Residual Equilibrium Function Learning (REFL), which aims to bridge the gap between local and global methods. By combining a local solution technique that serves as a reference baseline with a trainable neural network component that learns the residual from this baseline and by initializing the state distribution in an informed manner, the method can learn a global solution more accurately, quickly, and robustly. I test the new method using three different baseline functions with varying degrees of prior economic information in a high-dimensional, complex overlapping-generations model with portfolio choice and occasionally binding constraints. Given a feasible baseline function, the method is able to recover the functional rational expectations equilibrium without a homotopy schedule. I also find that the convergence speed and solution precision increase with the quality of the economics-informed baseline policy.

title: Costly Capital and Optimal Reinsurance
affiliations: Center for Finance and Insurance, University of Zurich - Department Finance and Leibniz University Hannover

detail.title: Costly Capital and Optimal Reinsurance
detail.abstract: We develop a theory of optimal reinsurance when holding capital is costly. Reinsurance creates value not by reducing risk but by lowering the cost of regulatory capital. Within a broad class of indemnity contracts, regulatory regimes and margins, an optimal layer contract always exists. Our normative benchmark is the frictional cost margin, which charges each contract the carry cost of the reinsurer's supporting capital. Costly capital drives the insurer to hold as little capital as possible: under V@R the optimal contract leaves shareholders no capital at risk, coverage stopping at the quantile beyond which V@R is blind, so the entire tail is retained, whereas a sufficiently stringent ES regime makes full cession optimal for any loss distribution. The expected value margin departs from this benchmark, creating a distortion that harms both parties: it enables transactions benefiting the insurer at the reinsurer's expense and blocks mutually beneficial ones.

title: Inside Information: Sorting, Screening, and Signaling Desistance in Correctional Settings
affiliations: , Vanderbilt University, University of Texas at Austin and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Inside Information: Sorting, Screening, and Signaling Desistance in Correctional Settings

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA
declarations.ethicsApproval: NA
declarations.funderStatement: NA

detail.abstract:
ABSTRACT
Research Summary
Correctional staff face an inference problem. They are legally required to support and recognize an incarcerated person's efforts at rehabilitation, but they cannot directly observe their true identity or the effort they are making to change. This paper applies the concepts of sorting, screening, and signaling from information economics to create an analytical framework to guide improved correctional practice. The paper first classifies the incarcerated population into three “types”: committed criminals, conformists, and desisters. Sorting at intake in the criminal justice system reliably separates out committed criminals using criminal history, but desisters are often pooled with conformists because intent to change is a dynamic, self-authored process that no risk-needs instrument, however refined, is designed to capture. Screening, whereby staff provide explicit rewards for behavioral compliance, fosters a safer environment, but likewise does not differentiate conformists from desisters, as desisters would comply even without incentives. Signaling solves this problem by shifting the initiative to the inmate, whereby desisters would be motivated to act without any guarantee of an explicit reward.
Policy Implications
Continued investment in ever more refined risk-prediction tools misdiagnoses the problem: risk instruments detect risk, not intent to change. Parole boards and correctional institutions should shift weight at reclassification and release away from risk scores and toward screens and primarily signals, including microsignals such as consistent attendance at a work assignment or willingness to accept added supervision. Correctional institutions should expand access to voluntary rehabilitative opportunities without layering on extrinsic rewards. They should also avoid the temptation to make programs mandatory, which dilutes their value as a signal. This framework for solving the inference problem generalizes beyond incarceration settings to any situation where decision makers need to identify desisters among a group of people with criminal history records.

title: Latent Fragility and Clustered Withdrawals in Dynamic Banks Runs
affiliations: University of Rome Tor Vergata, Bielefeld University - Center for Mathematical Economics, University of North Carolina (UNC) at Chapel Hill - Finance Area and Boston University - Questrom School of Business

detail.title: Latent Fragility and Clustered Withdrawals in Dynamic Banks Runs
detail.abstract: Using a mean-field game framework, we study a dynamic model of bank runs in which more withdrawals raise the risk of bank failure. Even though depositors receive gradual and idiosyncratic shocks, withdrawals occur in clusters. The main mechanism is latent fragility: run-prone depositors accumulate gradually over time and may prefer to wait individually, but they withdraw together once collective exit becomes self-fulfilling. We establish equilibrium existence and characterize earliest-run and latest-run equilibria. The clustering mechanism arises whether depositor heterogeneity is discrete or continuous. A common aggregate state coordinates withdrawal timing and leads to a unique threshold equilibrium.

title: Is Generative AI Destroying Edtech? A Two-Channel Test of Paid Demand

detail.title: Is Generative AI Destroying Edtech? A Two-Channel Test of Paid Demand

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence this work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study used only publicly available data (SEC filings, Google Trends, and published reports) and did not involve human-subjects research, so no ethics approval was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Generative-AI models now clear professional licensing and graduate-admissions examinations at near-zero marginal price, and the prevailing narrative holds that they will destroy paid education technology. We ask whether that destruction is visible in paid demand, testing its two channels, product substitution and search-based customer acquisition, on a panel of 16 U.S.-listed edtech firms from 2019 through early 2026, with registered effect-size tiers fixed before estimation. On the product-substitution channel we find a well-powered, tiered null: effects at the destruction-narrative tier are excluded in every specification and every exposure route, while material-shock effects are excluded within the specification family that controls the pandemic-reversion confound and cannot be resolved outside it. On the search channel the same machinery traces a different path: it exits its null band in 2024Q3, seven quarters after ChatGPT and one quarter after the search-regime change, and stays outside for six consecutive quarters. The magnitude, 0.07-0.09 log points per standard deviation of search dependence, is a specification-dependent upper bound, and the load-bearing fact is the contrast in path shape, not the point estimate. The two channels differ in evidential standing: the search finding is identified only up to a composite regime change. Non-significance is a feature of data resolution, not evidence of effect absence. The detectable harm thus ran through customer acquisition, upstream of the subscription decision, not through substitution for paid products, and the null survives dedicated checks against the leading alternative readings, save the fully offsetting hedge, which the design can bound but not exclude.

title: A Spearman-like Coefficient for Upper-tail Association Analysis
affiliations: University of Cádiz

detail.title: A Spearman-like Coefficient for Upper-tail Association Analysis
detail.abstract: Quantifying association during extreme events is of paramount importance in fields such as finance, insurance, and environmental sciences. Classical correlation measures often fail to capture co-movements in the tails of distributions, while traditional boundary tail coefficients collapse under asymptotic independence, rendering them blind to subasymptotic concentration. In this paper, we introduce a unified framework of Spearman-like, tail-sensitive indices constructed via the ranks and concomitants of the data to assess localized association conditional on large threshold exceedances. We establish two complementary families of measures: a discrete two-parameter family that encompasses Spearman's ρ as a special case, and a continuous single-parameter family obtained as its asymptotic limit. This threshold-defined framework offers a flexible, interpretable diagnostic tool that continuously tracks tail-association paths and successfully discriminates among fundamentally distinct subasymptotic structures where classical boundary indicators vanish. For both families, we investigate their theoretical properties-including their limiting behavior at the absolute boundary-propose empirical plug-in estimators, and derive their asymptotic distributions. The operational advantages of the indices are verified through analytical illustrations across diverse copula families and demonstrated via an empirical application to global catastrophic risk.

reference: Charles University in Prague Faculty of Law Research Paper No. 2026/II/4
title: The Law of the Sea in an Era of Strategic Chokepoint Disruption: The Case of Strait of Hormuz
affiliations: Charles University in Prague - Faculty of Law

detail.title: The Law of the Sea in an Era of Strategic Chokepoint Disruption: The Case of Strait of Hormuz

publicationDetails.detailsText: Charles University in Prague Faculty of Law Research Paper No. 2026/II/4
publicationDetails.journalName: Charles University in Prague Faculty of Law Legal Studies Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Global supply chains depend on secure maritime transport, yet instability in strategic chokepoints is now at its highest level in decades. Recent disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, the Red Sea, the Suez Canal, and the Panama Canal, have demonstrated how quickly regional crises can trigger global shocks to energy markets, container shipping, and industrial production. The 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis was the most severe example: after Iran threatened to target vessels, daily transits collapsed by roughly 95 %, leaving hundreds of ships stranded and causing sharp increases in oil prices, insurance costs, and shipping delays. These events expose structural weaknesses in the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). Although transit passage through major straits is protected under Articles 37–44, the convention lacks real‑time enforcement tools when coastal states employ coercive tactics such as threats, inspections, or selective interference. Dispute‑settlement mechanisms are retrospective and too slow to mitigate immediate supply‑chain impacts, allowing states to functionally suspend navigation without formal legal consequences. For highly trade‑dependent economies such as Taiwan, whose semiconductor sector relies heavily on maritime inputs, these vulnerabilities are acute. Strengthening chokepoint governance requires empowering the International Maritime Organization to improve monitoring and transparency while pursuing long‑term reforms to reinforce UNCLOS and protect global supply‑chain resilience.

title: Quantum-inspired Risk Portfolio Optimization via Exponential Tilting
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, , , , , Fondazione LINKS, Torino, Intesa Sanpaolo SpA, Fondazione LINKS, Torino, Fondazione LINKS, Torino, Fondazione LINKS, Torino, Intesa Sanpaolo SpA and

detail.title: Quantum-inspired Risk Portfolio Optimization via Exponential Tilting
detail.abstract:
Financial portfolio optimization is often framed through mean–variance objectives, yet real profit-and-loss (P&L)
scenario distributions are typically discrete and non-Gaussian. To explore realistic P&L distributions, we propose an objective function based on exponential tilting and certainty equivalent under constant absolute risk aversion. We then derive a second-order approximation, recovering a quadratic optimization problem solvable through mixed integer quadratic programming (MIQP) and quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO). Constraints in the QUBO formulation are incorporated via Lagrangian relaxation and slack variable approaches, enabling a direct comparison between classical constrained MIQP and quantum-inspired methods. In order to study how exponential tilting affects mean, standard deviation, and tail-risk measures such as Value at Risk and Conditional Value at Risk, we design an experimental protocol based on scanning a grid of tilt parameters and solving the associated optimization problems. The results on a realistic trading portfolio show how the tilts can be tuned to optimize different risk-return profiles while remaining competitive with those found using other state-ofthe-art approaches. Moreover, performance analysis suggests that, even using classical solvers, the QUBO formulation with Lagrangian relaxation scales better than the MIQP approach, providing the best constraint encoding strategy.

title: The Confidence Pill: The Causal Effect of Exposure to Police Social Media
affiliations: Newcastle University, Newcastle University and Newcastle University

detail.title: The Confidence Pill: The Causal Effect of Exposure to Police Social Media
detail.abstract: This paper studies how police communication on social media affects public confidence in the police and subjective well-being. We run a large-scale online experiment in which social media users are randomly exposed to real Instagram content posted by English police forces or to neutral content. We distinguish between three content types: enforcement outcomes, community engagement, and requests for public assistance. Exposure to police content increases confidence in the police and costly support for policing in an incentivised donation task. However, it also produces large immediate decreases in self-reported happiness and does not shift crime concern, perceived police effectiveness, reporting intentions, or Government spending preferences. Effects differ sharply by content type: community-engagement posts deliver confidence gains comparable to enforcement-focused posts while generating substantially smaller wellbeing costs. Overall, police communication on social media operates as a confidence pill-raising confidence but with considerable adverse effects on well-being.

title: When Does Risk-Managed Momentum Add Value? An Out-of-Sample, Regime-Conditional, and Statistically Tested Study of a Volatility-Targeted Dual-Momentum Strategy

detail.title: When Does Risk-Managed Momentum Add Value? An Out-of-Sample, Regime-Conditional, and Statistically Tested Study of a Volatility-Targeted Dual-Momentum Strategy

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests or financial relationships that could have influenced this study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study involves no human participants or patient data; it uses only publicly available market data.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this research; it was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: A defensive strategy is expected to trail passive equities across a sustained bull market, so "did it beat the market?" is the wrong question. This paper asks a conditional one: under what market conditions does risk-managed allocation add value, and are the differences statistically distinguishable from noise? I build a rules-based backtest combining dual-momentum asset selection with volatility targeting across four asset classes (Feb 2013–Jun 2026), correcting common backtest errors (lookahead bias, turnover-based transaction costs, a real time-varying risk-free rate), and subject it to out-of-sample and walk-forward validation, regime-conditional analysis, a 36-configuration sensitivity grid, and block-bootstrap significance tests. The results are instructive because they are mixed: the strategy reduces volatility and drawdown versus buy-and-hold but does not outperform a 60/40 benchmark in any configuration, and its full-sample risk-reduction benefits are not statistically significant. Its value is regime-dependent, strong in the slow 2022 bear market, worst in the fast COVID crash. Walk-forward re-optimization degrades out-of-sample performance, an empirical demonstration of the backtest-overfitting trap. An engineered daily crash-guard overlay delivers statistically significant downside protection but exposes a fundamental crash-protection-versus-whipsaw tradeoff. All results are reproducible from cached data and a fixed seed. Code, data, and interactive demo: github.com/aarivgoyal/quant-momentum-risk-targeting (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21444647).

title: Can Public Long-Term-Care Oversight Methods Travel Across States? A Two-County Oregon Cross-State Applicability Study

detail.title: Can Public Long-Term-Care Oversight Methods Travel Across States? A Two-County Oregon Cross-State Applicability Study

declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study did not involve human subjects research or protected health information. It uses exclusively publicly available, de-identified administrative and geospatial data (Oregon's long-term-care licensing portal, county- and Census-level population sources) and publicly available court and Department of Justice filings for the two enforcement matters discussed in the paper. No patients or participants were involved, and no ethics board approval or informed consent was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant or funding from any agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.
declarations.clinicalTrialRegistration: Not applicable. This study is not a clinical trial.

detail.abstract:
Background: A companion study developed and piloted a 20-indicator public-data review-priority framework, empirically applied in one state (Washington) and one facility type (Adult Family Homes), across three counties; such a framework has uncertain generalizability until tested elsewhere.

Objective: This cross-state applicability study asks which indicators are technically reproducible with the core analytic logic and original thresholds retained, which require facility-type-aware recalibration, which are supported by the new state's own enforcement or oversight record, and which remain dependent on internal claims data this study does not have.

Methods: The Washington pipeline's core merge, normalization, clustering, and threshold logic was retained after Oregon-specific schema harmonization, then applied to newly assembled data for Clackamas and Washington County across all four Oregon-licensed facility types (Adult Foster Homes, Assisted Living, Residential Care, Nursing Facilities; n = 792), drawing additionally on two Oregon licensing-unit evaluations and two official enforcement matters naming facilities in the study counties.

Results: Facility density and bed density were technically reproducible. Pooled county-level prevalence of facilities with at least one retained enforcement or investigation record was similar across counties (enforcement 18.8% both; investigation 27.2% vs. 28.4%), but this is descriptive only, not a common-observation-period rate, since facility-type-stratified prevalence varies widely (Adult Foster Home enforcement prevalence of 8 to 12% versus 38 to 60% or higher for the other three types). The shared-contact clustering computation was technically reproducible, but its three-license threshold was not interpretively portable across Oregon's mixed facility types, flagging a same-brand arrangement rather than an undisclosed common-control network; restricting the indicator to Adult Foster Homes recovered a comparable pair-level signal. A separate registry check of all 49 underlying clusters confirmed a real administrative or ownership relationship for 47, 11 of them recoverable only through registry evidence rather than facility naming. Of the 20 indicators, 1 operationalizes with recalibration, 3 are partially operationalized, 2 are case-supported, 3 are system-supported, 3 are contextually assessed, 4 are publicly testable but not completed here, 3 require internal data, and 1 was not established.

Conclusion: Public-data review-priority methods demonstrated second-state technical portability, but a structural proxy indicator's construct and its numeric threshold behaved differently under recalibration, and this precisely categorized accounting of a 20-indicator framework's cross-state evidentiary status is itself a reportable result.

title: How Fast Do Signatures Learn? Statistical Theory and Applications for Path Regression
affiliations: Mathematical Institute, University of Oxford and Oxford Man Institute, University of Oxford, Peking University, Peking University and

detail.title: How Fast Do Signatures Learn? Statistical Theory and Applications for Path Regression
detail.abstract: Many prediction and decision-making problems in operations research involve pathvalued covariates-data that evolve over time-for which path signatures have become a canonical feature representation. Their use is justified by a universal approximation theorem, but this is an existence result: it guarantees that a finite-level signature can approximate any continuous path functional, without quantifying how fast the approximation error decreases as the truncation level grows. This paper develops approximation and statistical theory for signature-based path regression. We establish an L2 approximation rate for smooth functionals of Itô diffusions and show that it is minimax optimal. We then propagate the truncation error through three statistical learning procedures-Signature-OLS, Signature-LASSO, and Signature-Logistic-and establish their consistency. Three real-data applications show that signatures provide informative finite-dimensional representations of path-valued covariates and can improve prediction relative to handcrafted features, in the context of finance-foreign exchange realized volatility forecasting from intraday price paths; energy-battery end-of-life prediction from early diagnostic current-voltage pulse paths; and medicine-epileptic seizure detection from short electroencephalogram windows.

title: Where Does Fertility Sit in the Macroeconomic Shock Network? Time-Varying Connectedness Evidence From Greece

detail.title: Where Does Fertility Sit in the Macroeconomic Shock Network? Time-Varying Connectedness Evidence From Greece
detail.abstract: Greek live births fell to 65,594 in 2025, the lowest count on record and about 19,000 below the 2020 level. Whether the link between the macroeconomy and fertility strengthens or weakens across successive crises is unknown, because existing studies assume it is constant. Using monthly data for 2001 to 2025 and a time-varying parameter vector autoregression, this paper measures the direction and the changing strength of the connection between births and macroeconomic conditions. Births are a net receiver of macroeconomic shocks: they absorb disturbances to unemployment, prices, and sentiment but transmit little in return. Inflation, rather than measured joblessness, has the largest positive net pairwise directional connectedness to births. The strength of the link is far from constant and rises sharply during the sovereigndebt crisis and at the onset of the pandemic. The net-receiver result also holds for Italy and Spain.

title: Direct Versus Risk-Stratified Endoscopic Screening for Upper Gastrointestinal Cancer in Non-High-Risk Areas of China: A Cost-Effectiveness Analysis with Decision Thresholds
affiliations: Fujian Medical University, Xuzhou Medical University, Fujian Medical University - Fujian Cancer Hospital and

detail.title: Direct Versus Risk-Stratified Endoscopic Screening for Upper Gastrointestinal Cancer in Non-High-Risk Areas of China: A Cost-Effectiveness Analysis with Decision Thresholds

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: The study followed the CHEERS 2022 reporting guideline and was approved by the Ethics Committee of Fujian Cancer Hospital (approval number: K2022‑136‑02).
declarations.funderStatement: Guiding Project of Fujian Science and Technology Plan (2022Y0055), Major Scientific Research Program for Young and Middle-aged Health Professionals of Fujian Province (2022ZQNZD008), and the Fujian Provincial Key Clinical Specialty Project.

detail.abstract:
Background: We aimed to determine whether the optimal endoscopic screening strategy for upper gastrointestinal cancer (UGIC) in non-high-risk areas of China is fixed or conditional, by comparing direct endoscopic screening (DES) and risk-stratified endoscopic screening (RSES) across frequencies and starting ages.

Methods: From the healthcare-system perspective, we developed a Markov model simulating 100,000 residents aged 40–69 years in Fujian Province, a representative non-high-risk area. Five frequencies and six starting ages were evaluated for both strategies, with no screening as comparator. Outcomes included costs, QALYs, and ICERs. The willingness-to-pay (WTP) threshold was set at China's 2024 per-capita GDP ($13,445).

Findings: Across all starting ages, both strategies were cost-effective versus no screening, with ICERs from $1,471 to $6,688 per QALY, all below the WTP threshold. The model was most sensitive to endoscopy adherence among RSES-positive individuals. DES every 2 years was preferred (ICERs $7,797–$9,147 per QALY vs biennial RSES; 74%–83% probability of being cost-effective at the WTP threshold). RSES became preferred when DES adherence fell below 29% or risk-stratification performance reached 65% to 75%.

Interpretation: Endoscopic screening is cost-effective in non-high-risk areas of China, but no single strategy is universally optimal. Biennial DES is favoured under base-case assumptions but reverses to RSES once local adherence or risk-stratification performance crosses the identified thresholds. Screening policy should therefore be guided by local conditions rather than a uniform recommendation.

title: Pricing Suffering in Animals
affiliations: University of San Diego School of Law, Duke University and Texas State University

detail.title: Pricing Suffering in Animals

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA
declarations.ethicsApproval: NA
declarations.funderStatement: NA

publicationDetails.detailsText: San Diego Legal Studies Paper No. 26-021
publicationDetails.journalName: University of San Diego Law School Legal Studies Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
Large majorities of Americans care about animal welfare, and federal regulations affect billions of animals. The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) promulgates rules affecting the extent to which show horses endure sores, cows contract diseases, and chickens have outdoor access. Yet no one has systematically examined whether agencies account for animal welfare in their decision-making. To investigate the government's treatment of animal welfare, this Article conducts the first systematic investigation of cost-benefit analysis (CBA) in 73 regulatory impact analyses published by the USDA and its subsidiary agencies over two decades. Fifty CBAs ignore effects on animal welfare altogether. When CBAs discuss impacts on animal welfare, such discussions are thin.  Only three CBAs monetize animal welfare effects. These findings reveal a systematic neglect of animal welfare that undermines rational decision-making. 

This Article argues that CBAs should incorporate Americans' willingness to pay for animal welfare. Because agencies are obligated to consider regulatory effects comprehensively, CBAs' current approach to animal welfare is irrational and likely illegal. To improve agencies' decision-making and compliance with law, the Article suggests a variety of technical tools agencies could use to account for the value that Americans place on animal welfare and demonstrates how such techniques would work in practice. Borrowing from agency precedent in other contexts—including monetizing effects on ecosystems and climate change—the Article also suggests organizational tools to improve CBAs, including valuing consumer preferences for animal welfare through agency guidance or an interagency working group. The Article's survey of agencies' consideration of animal welfare, together with its proposed solutions, constitutes the most comprehensive treatment to date of animal welfare as an administrative law problem.

title: Applying the GARCH Model to Measure Market Volatility and Predict Periods of Financial Instability

detail.title: Applying the GARCH Model to Measure Market Volatility and Predict Periods of Financial Instability
detail.abstract: This paper applies the Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity (GARCH(1,1)) model to evaluate market volatility in the S&P 500 during two periods of financial crisis: the 2007–2009 Global Financial Crisis and the 2019–2021 COVID-19 pandemic. After deriving the model's recursive structure, stationarity conditions, and mean-reversion properties, GARCH(1,1) is estimated via maximum likelihood on daily log returns across both windows. Results show that volatility during the 2008 crisis was driven primarily by high persistence (β₁ = 0.905), consistent with a prolonged, systemic credit crisis, while the COVID-19 crash exhibited substantially greater sensitivity to new shocks (α₁ = 0.280), consistent with a sudden, discrete market disruption. Both periods satisfy the stationarity condition (α₁ + β₁ < 1), though volatility decays more slowly following the 2008 crisis (half-life of 57.4 days) than the 2020 crash (22.0 days). These findings demonstrate GARCH(1,1)'s capacity to quantify meaningful differences in volatility dynamics across distinct types of financial crises, while also highlighting the model's core limitations, including its inability to capture asymmetric responses to positive and negative shocks.

title: The Surgeon Without a File

detail.title: The Surgeon Without a File
detail.abstract: The professional career of René Favaloro exhibits a discontinuity that the standard biographical reconstruction dissolves rather than explains: between the medical degree of 1949 and his integration into a high-complexity cardiovascular service in 1962, there is no documented formal surgical training. The lexicon of the sources is variable and inconsistent-concurrencia, practicantado, residenciaand Argentine institutional chronology renders it anachronistic: the germ of the country's first surgical residency dates from 1951 and the first university residency in surgery from 1957. The institutional curriculum adds "General Surgery, Postgraduate Courses, Hospital Rawson," but the only structured program of the Finochietto School began in May 1953, with Favaloro settled in La Pampa since 1950, a date not even the Foundation itself manages to fix: May according to its biography, November according to its curriculum vitae. This paper holds that Jacinto Aráuz constitutes the longest and least documented interval in which that acquisition of skill could have occurred-a "black box" of training on real patients, with no known clinical archive and no auditable material siteand that access to Cleveland operated, according to the available biographical reconstruction, through a chain of personal recommendations without a supporting file. The alleged lack of English on arrival, resting on a single autobiographical source, is treated as a self-interested claim, symmetrical and inverse to the surgical competence attributed in 1950: the myth grants surgery where documents are missing and removes English where humility needs to be manufactured. The nonexistence of an auditable documentary chain is not an obstacle to this investigation but one of its results: no public, continuous, and verifiable documentation is known today about how Favaloro acquired and validated his surgical competence, while the public biography asserts that competence as an established fact.

title:
Wired but Dark

Private Capital, Smart Grids, and the Architecture of Nigeria's Energy Future
affiliations: University of Benin

detail.title:
Wired but Dark

Private Capital, Smart Grids, and the Architecture of Nigeria's Energy Future
detail.abstract:
Nigeria is a paradox of abundance and deprivation. It sits atop proven gas reserves exceeding 200 trillion cubic 
feet, receives between 4,000 and 6,500 Wh/m² of solar irradiation daily across its territory, and hosts West Africa's 
largest economy. Yet it delivers an average of 4,300 megawatts (MW) of electricity to a population of 220 million 
a per-capita generation ratio so thin that the country ranks among the most under-electrified major economies on 
earth. By comparison, Poland, with 37 million people, generates over 46,000 MW. The United States generates 
roughly 3,900 MW per million people; Nigeria generates barely 20.
This report examines the structural causes of that failure, the private sector forces attempting to transcend it, and 
the policy architecture needed to translate isolated successes into systemic transformation. It interrogates 
Elektron Energy's 30 MW Victoria Island embedded power plant as a replicable commercial model; benchmarks
Nigeria's smart mini-grid sector against global peers; analyses the feasibility of former Power Minister Bayo 
Adelabu's $100 billion investment estimate; dissects the highly controversial #3.3 trillion debt settlement —
including the public debate it ignited between Arise TV anchor Rufai Oseni and presidential aide Tolu Ogunlesi on 
X — and proposes a coherent framework for deleveraging distribution companies (DisCos) while making them 
operationally viable.
The central argument is straightforward: Nigeria's electricity crisis is not primarily a generation capacity problem. 
It is a structural financing, institutional, and governance problem that has been consistently misdiagnosed. Private-
sector embedded generation, distributed renewable energy, and commercial mini-grids are proving that the 
economics of reliable power are achievable in Nigeria today but only in isolated pockets, not at national scale, 
because the transmission backbone and distribution architecture remain trapped in a debt cycle that no single 
settlement has ever conclusively resolved.

title: Augmented Structure Preserving Neural Networks for biomedical engineering applications in cell migration and mitosis prediction
affiliations: Universidad Politécnica de Madrid, Universidad Politécnica de Madrid, Universidad Politécnica de Madrid, Universidad Politécnica de Madrid and Universidad Politécnica de Madrid

detail.title: Augmented Structure Preserving Neural Networks for biomedical engineering applications in cell migration and mitosis prediction
detail.abstract: ​ Cell biomechanics involve a great number of complex phenomena that are fundamental to the evolution of life itself and other associated processes, ranging from the very early stages of embryo-genesis to the maintenance of damaged structures or the growth of tumors. Given the importance of such phenomena, increasing research has been dedicated to their understanding, but the many interactions between them and their influence on the decisions of cells as a collective network or cluster remain unclear. We present a new approach that combines Structure Preserving Neural Networks, which study cell movements as a purely mechanical system, with other Machine Learning tools (Artificial Neural Networks), which allow taking into consideration environmental factors that can be directly deduced from an experiment with Computer Vision techniques. This new model, tested on simulated and real cell migration cases, predicts complete cell trajectories following a roll-out policy with a high level of accuracy. This work also includes a mitosis evento prediction model based on Neural Networks architectures which makes use of the same observed features. The AI contribution is a structure-preserving neural framework for time-dependent prediction, while the engineering application is video-based modelling of cell migration and mitosis in biomedical engineering.

title: Hydroplaning and Wet-Road Crash Rules Mining using Autoencoder-Based Neurosymbolic (AERIAL) Association Rules
affiliations: Texas State University, Texas State University, Texas State University and Texas State University

detail.title: Hydroplaning and Wet-Road Crash Rules Mining using Autoencoder-Based Neurosymbolic (AERIAL) Association Rules
detail.abstract: This study distinguishes hydroplaning-related crashes from general wet-road crashes and identifies how their fatal and injury (KA) crashes and moderate/minor/no injury (BCO) crash patterns differ. The motivation is that hydroplaning-related crashes are often hidden within broader wet-road records, where narratives may describe rain, wet pavement, skidding, or loss of control without directly identifying hydroplaning. Texas CRIS crash data from 2017 to 2025 were analyzed using a narrative-informed and model-interpretable framework. Structural topic modeling was first applied to crash narratives to separate hydroplaning-related, wet-road, and mixed cases. Machine-learning and deep-learning models were then used to predict hydroplaning-related versus wet-road crashes using structured variables and to identify the factors that differentiated the two groups. Probability-thresholded samples were further analyzed using severity-specific Autoencoder-Based Neurosymbolic (AERIAL) association rules for hydroplaning-related KA crashes, hydroplaning-related BCO crashes, wet-road fatal and injury crashes, and wet-road moderate/minor/no injury crashes. The findings show that hydroplaning-related crashes are more control-loss centered, with fatal and injury crash patterns linked to rural two-lane roads, unsafe speed, skidding, overturning, and fixed-object involvement. Wet-road crashes are more conflict- and recovery-centered, with fatal and injury crash patterns linked to rural high-speed two-lane exposure, no-passing zones, unsafe speed, and opposite-direction conflicts. The findings support separate wet-weather safety strategies, including pavement grooving, drainage improvement, and roadway-departure treatments for hydroplaning-related crashes, speed management, wet-reflective markings, rumble strips, and curve-warning treatments for wet-road crashes.

title: Trends in HIV Mortality and Incidence in the League of Arab States from 2000 to 2023: A Comparative Analysis of Regional Progress and Emerging Challenges​
affiliations: Imperial College London, Imperial College London, Imperial College London and

detail.title: Trends in HIV Mortality and Incidence in the League of Arab States from 2000 to 2023: A Comparative Analysis of Regional Progress and Emerging Challenges​

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding was obtained for this study.

detail.abstract:
Background: Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) remains a major global public health challenge, with approximately 39 million people living with HIV (PLHIV) worldwide as of 2023. Regional disparities persist, and the 22 Arab League countries continue to face unique epidemiological, cultural, and structural challenges in addressing the HIV epidemic.

Methods: Data were extracted from the IHME Global Health Data Exchange Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 Results Tool. HIV burden was characterised using three key epidemiological metrics: mortality rate, Disability-Adjusted Life Years (DALYs), and Years of Life Lost (YLLs), all reported per 100,000 population. Age-standardised and all-ages values were analysed across five age groups (0–14, 15–49, 50–69, ≥70 years, and age-standardised) and by sex, from 2000 to 2023. Analysis was conducted in Microsoft Excel.

Findings: Between 2000 and 2023, age-standardised HIV mortality per 100,000 increased by an average of 95.1% across the 22 Arab League countries, with Djibouti (62.15), Mauritania (30.67), and Sudan (18.67) recording the highest rates in 2023. Age-standardised HIV prevalence rose in 18 of 22 countries between 2010 and 2023, averaging a 94.12% increase across the region. The Arab League average age-standardised HIV mortality rose from 3.07 to 5.99 per 100,000, representing a 95.1% increase. HIV incidence declined in only a subset of states.

Interpretation: The varying HIV trends across Arab countries demand tailored, evidence-based policies. Prioritising youth-centred education, engaging key populations, training healthcare providers, and integrating HIV services into universal health coverage frameworks are essential for sustainable HIV control.

title: A Vision-language Pre-trained Model for Breast MRI Interpretation: A Large-scale, Multicenter Model Development and Prospective Validation Study
affiliations: Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST), Chinese PLA General Hospital, Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST) and

detail.title: A Vision-language Pre-trained Model for Breast MRI Interpretation: A Large-scale, Multicenter Model Development and Prospective Validation Study

declarations.declarationOfInterest: We declare no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This project has been reviewed and approved by the Human and Artefacts Research Ethics Committee (HAREC). The protocol number is HREP-2025-0312. All data were de-identified before the development of the model.
declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by the Hong Kong Innovation and Technology Commission (Project No. GHP/006/22GD and ITCPD/17-9), HKUST (Project No. FS111), National Key R&D Program of China (Project No. 2023YFE0204000), the Health and Medical Research Fund (Ref: 20211021), the Health Bureau, The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and National Natural Science Foundation of China (Project No. 82102142).

detail.abstract:
Background: Interpreting multiparametric breast MRI is complex because it requires integration of information across multiple sequences to generate clinically meaningful reports. This process is time-consuming and expertise-dependent, potentially leading to workflow bottlenecks and diagnostic variability. To address these challenges, we developed and validated an artificial intelligence system for automated report generation and malignancy diagnosis.  

Methods: In this multicenter study, we assembled 10,753 breast MRI examinations from 10,664 patients across six hospitals in China. A unified vision-language framework was pre-trained on 3,664 image-report pairs from two internal centers and subsequently developed and validated for report generation and malignancy diagnosis using retrospective internal cohorts of 3,877 and 4,090 examinations, respectively. Prospective and external validation included 101 and 1,907 examinations for report generation and 113 and 5,637 for malignancy diagnosis, respectively. Clinical utility was assessed in two reader studies: a randomized crossover study of 60 cases comparing AI-assisted versus unassisted reporting by six radiologists, with report quality independently evaluated by three radiologists, and an independent diagnostic benchmark of 200 cases comparing the model with six radiologists.  

Findings: In the reporting reader study, final AI-assisted reports were judged equivalent to or preferred over unassisted reports by all three blinded reviewers in 83·9% of case-level comparisons, and reporting time was reduced by 27·3% per case, corresponding to a mean absolute reduction of 1·77 min (95% CI 1·54-1·98). Compared with the multimodal FeatureFuse baseline, the model improved BLEU-4 by 0·084-0·113, ROUGE-L by 0·084-0·121, and three-class BI-RADS accuracy by 0·094-0·145 across internal and prospective cohorts. Three-class BI-RADS accuracy improved from 0·523 to 0·688 in the external cohort. For malignancy diagnosis, the model achieved AUROCs of 0·920 and 0·929 in two internal cohorts, 0·936 in the prospective cohort, and 0·851-0·944 across four external centers. In the diagnostic benchmark, the model achieved higher accuracy than the least-experienced radiologist (89·5% vs 78·0%; p<0·001).  

Interpretation: This vision-language system showed consistent performance for both report generation and malignancy diagnosis across internal, prospective, and external cohorts. AI assistance improved reporting efficiency without an apparent reduction in the quality of the final radiologist-edited reports, while the diagnostic model achieved performance comparable to most participating radiologists. These findings support its potential as a practical decision-support tool for breast MRI interpretation, particularly in settings with limited specialist expertise.

title: Decentralized Equilibrium Search Under Central Governance Primal-Dual Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Large-Scale Inventory Coordination
affiliations: and College of William and Mary, Students

detail.title: Decentralized Equilibrium Search Under Central Governance Primal-Dual Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Large-Scale Inventory Coordination
detail.abstract: We study the problem of coordinating inventory replenishment decisions across thousands of retail stores sharing a common warehouse, under binding capacity constraints and contractual service-level commitments. Classical inventory theory-from the Newsvendor model to multi-echelon base-stock policies-assumes known demand distributions, optimizes each store independently or sequentially, and produces static ordering rules calibrated to historical statistics. These assumptions break down in largescale practice: demand is non-stationary, stores compete for scarce warehouse capacity, and service commitments must be honored dynamically. We propose a primal-dual multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework in which store-level PPO agents optimize local replenishment policies while a central planner enforces system-level constraints through Lagrangian dual variables. The dual variables admit direct economic interpretations as shadow prices: prices warehouse capacity scarcity, and prices the cost of the service-level commitment. Together with a bullwhip penalty coefficient , they constitute a three-lever governance system with provably orthogonal controls over fill rate, capacity feasibility, and order volatility. We validate the framework on 143 weeks of the Walmart public sales panel (store-department pairs). The system achieves an 89.9% demand fill rate under standard conditions. Under a 50% demand surge-a structural non-stationarity that no calibrated static policy can anticipate-PPO achieves 86.5% fill rate while the Newsvendor oracle falls to 39-47% regardless of whether its parameters are correctly recalibrated, a 1.83 performance gap. This result reveals that the adaptability advantage of MARL is structural rather than empirical: state-conditional ordering solves a real-time capacity allocation problem that static ordering rules cannot solve in principle.

title: Childhood Adversity And Early Natural Menopause Among Women: A Cross-National, Retrospective Cohort Study
affiliations: Peking University, Peking University, Peking University, Peking University - Department of Epidemiology and Biostatistics, Peking University, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College (CAMS & PUMC) - School of Population Medicine and Public Health and Peking University - Institute of Population Research

detail.title: Childhood Adversity And Early Natural Menopause Among Women: A Cross-National, Retrospective Cohort Study

declarations.funderStatement: This study was supported by the Top Young Talent Project of the National Special Support Program “Social Transformation, Life Course, and High-Quality Population Development”, the Cyrus Tang Foundation (Grant No. 050459) and the Peking University Digital Humanities Project, and the Fundamental Research Funds for the Central Universities (Grant No. 7101303989).

detail.abstract:
Background: Evidence on whether childhood adversity contributes to earlier reproductive ageing remains limited, particularly from cross-national studies. We investigated the association between childhood adversity and early menopause among women from the USA, England, and China.

Methods: A retrospective cohort study was conducted to explore the association of childhood adversity with the risk of early natural menopause among women aged 45 years or older. We analysed representative harmonised data from three nations, including the Health and Retirement Study, the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing, and the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. Early natural menopause, defined as natural menopause before age 45 years, indicated accelerated reproductive ageing. Childhood adversity was assessed as cumulative, subtype-specific, and categorical exposure. Modified Poisson regression with robust standard errors estimated associations; heterogeneity, mediation, prediction, and sensitivity analyses were performed.

Findings: Among 12402 women, 1262 (10·18%) experienced early menopause. In pooled analyses, each additional childhood adversity item was associated with a higher risk of early menopause (RR=1·08, 95% CI: 1·02-1·15). Deprivation-related adversity in early childhood increased the risk of early menopause by 12%. (RR=1·12, 95% CI: 1·04-1·20), whereas threat-related adversity was not clearly associated. Compared with no adversity, low-level adversity (RR 1·17, 95% CI: 1·04-1·32) and high-level adversity (RR 1·26, 95% CI: 1·07-1·47) were associated with an increased risk of early menopause, respectively,with a dose-response relationship across adversity categories. Associations varied by birth cohort (global p for interaction<0·001), with country heterogeneity for deprivation-related adversity (I²=65·2%; p for interaction =0·06). Educational attainment and pre-menopausal smoking mediated part of the association (RR 1·05, 95% CI: 1·02-1·09; 29·8% of the total effect), including a significant sequential pathway (1·9%). Prediction models showed moderate apparent discrimination but poor cross-country transportability.

Interpretation: Childhood adversity might be an important life-course determinant of accelerated reproductive ageing. The findings suggest that both early material disadvantage and downstream behavioural risk may contribute to the long-term reproductive consequences of childhood adversity, and the strength of association varies across national contexts and generations.

title: Private and Public Appeals in Promoting Impure Public Goods: Evidence from a Field Experiment with Farmers
affiliations: University of Guelph and

detail.title: Private and Public Appeals in Promoting Impure Public Goods: Evidence from a Field Experiment with Farmers
detail.abstract: Impure public goods present a unique challenge for policies aimed at encouraging their adoption. We examine the effectiveness of emphasizing key characteristics of these goods: private benefits, public local benefits, and public global benefits. To test these effects, we conduct a large-scale field experiment in which agricultural producers participate in cost-share bidding for nitrogen stabilizers, a critical impure public good. Our findings reveal that emphasizing private benefits significantly increases bids, followed by public local benefits, whereas public global benefits have an insignificant effect. Interestingly, combining private and public appeals results in lower bids than presenting the private appeal alone, suggesting that public appeals may diminish the effectiveness of private appeals.

title: Prediction Markets between the United States and the European Union: A Comparative Analysis of the Legal Classification of Event Contracts
affiliations: and Bocconi University

detail.title: Prediction Markets between the United States and the European Union: A Comparative Analysis of the Legal Classification of Event Contracts
detail.abstract: Over the past months, prediction markets — platforms enabling the trading of binary contracts whose value depends on the occurrence of a future event — have become a phenomenon of high significance across the world, and their legal status now lies at the centre of intense litigation and regulatory activity. The decision of the Third Circuit Court of Appeals in KalshiEX LLC v. Flaherty of 6 April 2026, the first appellate-level ruling on the matter in the United States (US), classified sports event contracts as swaps within the meaning of the Commodity Exchange Act and held that state gambling laws are accordingly preempted. Starting from a reconstruction of the US framework, this article offers a comparative analysis with the European Union (EU) system, which revolves primarily around the MiFID II regime. Although there is still no specific regulation on prediction markets in the Union, the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) has already expressed its first position on the matter, building from past positions on binary options and contracts for differences. The topic also involves the role of the Regulation on markets in crypto-assets (MiCAR), as well as the competence of Member States in matters of gambling. This paper suggests that the divergence between the two legal orders does not reflect a mere difference in regulatory intensity, but an inverted hierarchy between financial-markets law and gaming law: in the United States, federal derivatives law prevails by preemption over state gambling regulation; in the Union, conversely, national gambling law prevails by structural exclusion over harmonised financial-services law. The conclusions offer a critical reading of the implications of this divergence, also in light of the Savings and Investments Union and the debate on the review of financial legislation.

title: Transformation & Value Creation Engine: Impact of Synthetic Capital Stacks on Distressed Petrochemicals

detail.title: Transformation & Value Creation Engine: Impact of Synthetic Capital Stacks on Distressed Petrochemicals
detail.abstract: This paper develops a testable framework for evaluating whether synthetic capital stacks create value in distressed petrochemical restructurings. Using publicly listed petrochemical firms stressed during 2020-2026, the design links debt overhang, liquidity runway, creditor recovery, equity-option preservation, and downside-risk reduction to contingent claims embedded in restructuring packages. The paper provides a distress-screened sample, event-time design, valuation framework, and identification strategy. Because vendor-level bond, CDS, product-spread, and transaction-term data are not fully public, empirical result tables are specified but not estimated.

title: The Gendered Roles in Society and Women's Leadership in Higher Educational Institutions: The Graham Gender Equality Theory and Scale

detail.title: The Gendered Roles in Society and Women's Leadership in Higher Educational Institutions: The Graham Gender Equality Theory and Scale

declarations.ethicsApproval: NA

detail.abstract: Gender equality is a fundamental human right and a prerequisite for achieving equality of outcomes for both men and women in terms of education, labor markets, etc., At the same time, gender roles are barriers to women's career advancements and attainment of leadership positions. Gender disparity is a typical problem in higher education institutions. Women are still underrepresented in leadership in higher education institutions. This study employed an inductive approach in collecting data. This study followed the systematic literature review and the integrative literature review methods in developing knowledge about the sources of gender disparities in leadership in higher education institutions and the measures that are relevant in creating gender equality in leadership in higher education institutions. The findings from this study indicate that women face three main challenges in attaining leadership in higher education institutions. These are sociocultural elements, organizational and institutional elements, and individual elements. The findings also indicate that eradicating gender disparities in leadership can be achieved when organizational leaders have an accurate understanding of the root causes of gender disparities in leadership and implement measures to reduce or eliminate the problems. The measures include formulating and implementing policies, strategies, and interventions. This article presents new ideas about the paths to achieving gender equality in leadership; the Graham Gender Equality Theory, Model, and Scale. The gendered systems in society and in many organizations can be analyzed by using the Graham Gender Equality Scale. The level of gender disparities in the workplace and the key elements that lead to gender disparities can be evaluated using the scale. This study presents some practical implications for human resources managers and organizational leaders and some research focus, propositions, theories, and model to guide researchers in extending knowledge about gender disparities and gender equality in leadership.

title:
Citable by Construction 
An Evidence Model for Machine-Readable Comparative Law: Three Orthogonal Axes, an Enforced Citable Subset, and Computed-versus-Authored Reconciliation
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title:
Citable by Construction 
An Evidence Model for Machine-Readable Comparative Law: Three Orthogonal Axes, an Enforced Citable Subset, and Computed-versus-Authored Reconciliation
detail.abstract:
Machine-readable knowledge bases of comparative regulation are increasingly consumed not by readers who can weigh a caveat but by software, retrieval pipelines, language-model agents, automated compliance tools, that will treat whatever a field asserts as fact. In that setting three distinctions that a careful human reader keeps implicit must be made explicit, structured, andenforced,or the knowledge base will present a market report as binding law,a draft provision as in force, or an unverified transcription as confirmed. This paper sets out an evidence model that makes those three distinctions first-class and orthogonal: claim_class, the kind of claim(a proposition of lawversus a market or operational fact); evidence_tier, the provenance strength(confirmed against the official text, partly confirmed,or practitioner corroborated); and binding_status, thebinding status of the instrument the claim rests on (enacted and inforce, made but not commenced, finalized policy pending legislation,apend ing proposal, a prohibition, or no regime). The three axes compose without collision, and their intersection defines a lawyer-citable subset, the records a lawyer or supervisor can cite as current binding law, as the conjunction of tier1_legal, in_force, and resolution_ text. 

The paper then argues that a subset defined only by self-reported tags is not trustworthy, and sets out the build-time enforcement that makes the subsetreal:integrity gates that refuse a record asserting official-text confirmation without a locator, a purity gate that keeps a mar ket fact out of the instrument a lawyer is shown, a binding-status gate that refuses to treat a located-but-not-commenced instrument as current law, a signal-provenance gate that forbids any computed result to rest on an operational fact, and a ledger cross-check that catches drift, each demonstrated to bite by a negative test that breaks it on a throwaway copy. 

A second instrument, computed-versus-authored reconciliation, derives the knowledge base’s downstream conclusions from a rule engine and diffs them against the hand-authored analysis, treating disagreements as findings and shipping the derived layer as a labelled pre view rather than as asserted truth. A third discipline, the honest residual, publishes the back log of not-yet-verified records as queryable data and insists that the gates are defenses, not a cure: onlyprimary source  verification retires the liability. The method is presented as domain general; the cross-border stablecoin register is the demonstration, and the paper closes by separating what is portable (the three axes, the citable intersection, the enforcement gates, the computed-versus-authored stance, the backlog discipline) from what is domain-specific (the dimension set and the signal table).

title: The $LIBRA Case and the Limits of Investment Risk in Criminal Law: From the Digital Asset to the Architecture of Fraud

detail.title: The $LIBRA Case and the Limits of Investment Risk in Criminal Law: From the Digital Asset to the Architecture of Fraud
detail.abstract: The July 2026 ruling that removed all private complainants from Argentina's $LIBRA case rests on a methodological error: it treats the technological classification of the asset (a "memecoin") as excluding the possibility of fraud. Drawing on Argentine doctrine, German Risikogeschäfte dogmatics, and comparative case law (Howey, Shavers, Arbistar), this article argues that criminal analysis must shift from the investment object to the induced representation: market risk never purges an antecedent deception, and the architecture of the scheme (an investment platform bearing the government's slogan, presidential dissemination of the token's smart-contract link, and subsequent denial) is consistent with the typical structure of fraud.

title:
Cross-Border Stablecoin Feasibility Over Time 
A Trigger-Conditioned Forward Map of Pending Regulatory Transitions
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title:
Cross-Border Stablecoin Feasibility Over Time 
A Trigger-Conditioned Forward Map of Pending Regulatory Transitions
detail.abstract:
The companion works in this portfolio characterize cross-border stablecoin feasibility as it stands today: the Compliance Matrix as a twelve-jurisdiction node table, the Architecture working paper as an eight-constraint composition framework, and the Corridor Atlas as a onehundred-thirty-two-edge directed map. Each is a description of a single moment. This paper adds the missing dimension: feasibility is dated, and the public regulatory record already contains the changes in law that will move it. Its central instrument is the trigger, a change in law such as a commencement or an enactment, never a market event, and its central method is conditioning rather than forecasting: for each pending change the paper states which directed edges change feasibility class, which records the change rests on, and under what conditional status the change is contingent. 

Two contributions follow. The first is the conditioning method itself, applied to a deliberately sparse current instance that will densify as enactments land. The second is a typology of triggers by the kind of certainty each carries, separating the one kind that moves a dated horizon from the kinds that do not, and including a category a class-centric reading easily misses: the intra-regime gating change that moves accessibility within a live regime, with the European Union's 1 July 2026 MiCA transitional expiry as its worked example. 

From the register of changes in law visible on the public record as of 30 June 2026, set out in full in §3, the paper derives a corridor-sensitivity ordering. The forward map's classlevel motion is concentrated at the one remaining pre-regime origin, South Korea, and at the two regime-in-transition destinations: the United Kingdom, resolving to a clean Category I on a gazetted date in 2027, and Taiwan, whose Virtual Asset Service Act passed at third reading on the dateline of this draft and which resolves to a channelled Category II on an as-yet-ungazetted commencement; the prohibition destination, Mainland China, stays insensitive to any positive trigger. A second finding the register's structure makes legible is a cross-jurisdictional one: independent regimes converging on a single functional line between prohibited holder-yield and permitted activity-linked rewards, documented most fully for the United States and appearing as a sibling restriction elsewhere. 

A final and more interpretive section, resting on softer evidence as it says plainly, reads a structure the static map cannot express: the cross-border stablecoin stack is divided along one geopolitical fracture at three layers at once. The settlement substrate is split between rival bloc experiments rather than shared, with only Project Agorá led by the Bank for International Settlements, Project Ensemble led by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, and mBridge run since the Bank for International Settlements' 2024 withdrawal by a People's-Republic-of-China-and-Gulf group; the regulatory layer is open, channelled, or closed at each boundary by the availability of a recognition determination; and the issuance layer is fragmented per instrument. The paper advocates no outcome: the transitions it maps are analytical, and their operational viability depends on developments enumerated against the constraint framework, not asserted.
