detail.abstract: This paper addresses the systemic risks of autonomous machine-to-machine (M2M) commerce by formalizing the Agent-to-Agent Yield Paradox a phenomenon where individually rational pricing agents built on multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) produce compounding reliability decay and emergent tacit collusion in high-velocity inventory markets. To mitigate these operational and antitrust liabilities, we introduce the Detektor-Safe Harness, a governance protocol that isolates probabilistic inferential policies within a rigid, deterministic computational boundary. By enforcing velocity circuit breakers and an input-isolated Non-Collusion Boundary directly on the system's action space rather than its cognition, the harness functions as a capability-invariant safeguard. We demonstrate that as policy rationality scales toward perfect game-theoretic foresight, the protocol transitions from an operational volatility buffer into a verifiable, infrastructure-level alignment rollcage for artificial superintelligence (ASI) operating on the commercial grid.

title: Unified Boundary Field Theory of Interest Rates: An Empirical Study of Robin Short-Rate Boundary Coordinates and Low-Rank Covariance in the Yield Curve
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Unified Boundary Field Theory of Interest Rates: An Empirical Study of Robin Short-Rate Boundary Coordinates and Low-Rank Covariance in the Yield Curve
detail.abstract: This paper provides an empirical test of the Robin short-rate boundary-coordinate layer in Unified Boundary Field Theory (UBFT). The central claim is not merely that Treasury yield curves are low-dimensional. Rather, the paper asks whether a single short-rate boundary geometry can organise several empirical objects that are usually modelled separately: yieldcurve shape, maturity-dependent volatility, local boundary anchoring, covariance geometry, and phase-state behaviour. Using daily fitted U.S. Treasury zero-coupon yield curves from the Federal Reserve/Svensson data set over 1985-2026, I estimate a three-coordinate Robin short-rate boundary layer consisting of an amplitude coordinate, a local short-end slope, and a long-boundary anchor. The same maturity-loading geometry that represents the curve also governs variance transport across maturities through the interaction of the maturity loading vector with the boundary-coordinate covariance matrix. At the innovation level, the empirical correlation matrix of these boundary coordinates lies close to a signed rank-two manifold. Across broad regimes, blind five-year windows, rolling windows, holistic phase windows, human-selected windows, corrfine windows, random partitions, coordinate placebo tests, and targeted identification checks, the implied correlations reproduce observed correlations with high explanatory power and persistent branch selection. The evidence supports a segmentation-robust boundary-layer interpretation: the Robin short-rate boundary coordinates are not only a curve-fitting device, but a common empirical geometry linking shape, volatility transport, boundary anchoring, and innovation covariance. Placebo tests using Nelson-Siegel coordinates, Svensson subsets, endpoint-slope decompositions, and random rotations show that alternative representations can reproduce individual pieces of the evidence, but do not provide the same unified boundary interpretation. Additional identification checks show that the result is not explained by replacing the Robin amplitude with the raw fitted short-boundary level, and that the stable residual wedge is not materially generated by nonlinear transformation bias in the correlation estimator. The contribution is therefore a structural organisation result rather than a claim of exact rank reduction.

title: A Collaborative Autoethnography of Embodied Leadership Struggles: The Case of Leaderful Practices in a University Context
affiliations: , University of Turku, University of Turku and LUT University

detail.title: A Collaborative Autoethnography of Embodied Leadership Struggles: The Case of Leaderful Practices in a University Context

declarations.ethicsApproval: The authors declare no conflicts of interest regarding this manuscript

detail.abstract: This study explores embodied leadership struggles and the ongoing negotiation of leaderful practices in a university context. The empirical material is based on autoethnographic diary notes of two authors of this study. Through our collaborative analysis, we identify two themes of embodied leadership struggles as we attempted to create leaderful practices in the university setting: (1) moving between heroic and collective leadership expectations through bodily spaces and (2) while attempting to navigate our vulnerability in relation to our leadership expectations about the quest to find leaderful practices. Our study makes three contributions. First, our study contributes to the discussion of leadership-as-practice (L-A-P) by articulating the embodied struggles managers face when attempting to enact and promote leaderful practices. Second, the study contributes to the understanding of how these struggles can become a source of leadership learning through vulnerability. Rather than treating vulnerability as an inherently empowering personal condition, we show that vulnerability is a context-dependent, relationally shaped, and negotiated phenomenon. Finally, our study offers a methodological contribution by advancing collaborative autoethnography as a means for enacting leadership learning.

title: Hybrid Algorithmic Governance in U.S. Welfare Administration: State-and County-level AI as a Case of Support-control Convergence

detail.title: Hybrid Algorithmic Governance in U.S. Welfare Administration: State-and County-level AI as a Case of Support-control Convergence
detail.abstract: This article examines the institutional conditions under which artificial intelligence systems in U.S. welfare administration come to operate as instruments of support or as instruments of control. Rather than asking what welfare algorithms "really" are (tools of proactive assistance or infrastructures of surveillance) the article starts from the premise that support and control are co-present within the same system, while their relative balance shifts over time. This movement is conceptualized through the notion of support-control convergence and the model of an institutional ratchet. Routine budgetary and political pressures make control-oriented effects easily measurable and politically capitalizable, whereas a return toward support requires external intervention of disproportionate force, such as judicial compulsion, legislative prohibition, or public scandal. Empirically, the article draws on process tracing of six state-and county-level cases: NYSDOL fraud detection, Michigan MiDAS, Illinois Medicaid managed care, LA County homelessness prevention, the Allegheny Family Screening Tool, and Washington Foster Care. The findings show that the system's orientation is shaped by institutional design, with the decisive parameter being the side on which the costs of algorithmic error are placed. Drift toward control is routine, while reversal is exceptional and costly. In the MiDAS case, activation required a single administrative decision, whereas reversal took nine years and a $20 million settlement; even then, the system did not return to a support-oriented configuration.

title: Between Silicon Empires: The Philippines in the Age of Pax Silica

detail.title: Between Silicon Empires: The Philippines in the Age of Pax Silica

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper. This research received no external or institutional funding and was undertaken entirely independently. The views expressed in this working paper are solely those of the author and do not necessarily reflect those of any affiliated institution.

detail.abstract:
Purpose. This paper's principal contribution is conceptual rather than descriptive: it develops “Pax Silica,” a novel analytical framework for understanding an emerging international order in which semiconductor supply chains, artificial intelligence, data governance, platform capitalism, and digital infrastructure — rather than territory, industrial output, or military mass alone — constitute the principal sources of geopolitical power. The Philippines serves as the empirical case through which the framework's analytical value is demonstrated, not as the paper's primary object of interest.

Research Design. The paper combines conceptual theory-building with a structured, theory-informed case study, following the logic of case selection for concept refinement rather than statistical generalization. It synthesizes international relations and international political economy theory — including Nye, Strange, Farrell and Newman, Keohane and Nye, Zuboff, Castells, Stiglitz, Rodrik, Acharya, Kuik, Goh, Bremmer, Chen Weiss, and Khanna — with open-source evidence from 2024–2026 on semiconductor export-control policy, Philippine trade and diplomatic data, and cybersecurity threat reporting.

Findings. Pax Silica is distinct from adjacent frameworks — techno-nationalism, technopolarity, digital sovereignty, digital capitalism, geoeconomics, weaponized interdependence, network power, and platform capitalism — because it integrates five previously siloed dimensions of technological power into a single order-level concept capable of explaining middle-power strategy. Applied to the Philippines, the framework reveals a state of genuine but underexploited structural significance, constrained by chronic R&D underinvestment, a persistent digital divide, and an already-active cybersecurity threat environment.

Originality. Beyond the Philippine case, the paper demonstrates the framework's generalizability by extending it, in brief, to Vietnam, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Mexico, and Poland — middle powers whose divergent hedging strategies the Pax Silica framework can equally illuminate.

Policy Implications. The paper argues that “technological hedging” — an application of Kuik's general hedging concept to the technological domain specifically — combined with “digital sovereignty without technological autarky,” offers middle powers a theoretically grounded and practically viable alternative to the binary choice between alignment and autarky.

title: Introducing KAUC Cultural Index (KCI) for Measuring Culture
affiliations: Vietnam National University (VNU)

detail.title: Introducing KAUC Cultural Index (KCI) for Measuring Culture
detail.abstract: This method paper presents the KAUC Hybrid Cultural Index (KCI), a domain-adaptable procedure/method for measuring culture as a two-dimensional process of value maturation. The method converts domain-specific cultural indicators into four KAUC layer scores: Knowledge, Action, Utility, and Contribution. It then combines horizontal intensity, which measures weighted layer strength, with vertical maturity, which measures sequential progression through KAUC. Unlike simple additive scores, the KCI avoids overvaluing disconnected high-score profiles by requiring both layer strength and developmental coherence. The article provides formulas, decision rules, a worked example, validation and robustness checks, spreadsheet-ready formulas, and executable Python code. It operates the Culture Tower (KAUC Framework) for empirical and applied cultural measurement across environmental, digital, green, creative, clean, organizational, and other cultural domains.

title: Why Efficient Systems Fail Spectacularly: A Unified Theory of Systemic Risk
affiliations: UCLA Anderson

detail.title: Why Efficient Systems Fail Spectacularly: A Unified Theory of Systemic Risk
detail.abstract: I develop a unified model of resource and risk sharing in which N agents pool against a common crisis threshold subject to transaction costs. Three results follow. As transaction costs fall: the welfare-optimal pool expands and individual buffers shrink; average welfare improves strictly; and expected crisis scale-the number of agents simultaneously unable to access the shared resource-grows, even if crisis probability falls. The mechanism is identical across financial risk pooling, supply-chain management, and transportation networks. Large systemic crises are the necessary consequence of welfare-optimal pooling. The correct policy response is a Pigouvian charge on each participant's marginal contribution to expected crisis scale.

title: Spec-Driven AI for Empirical Research: A Scoping Review and an Architecture of Epistemic Control

detail.title: Spec-Driven AI for Empirical Research: A Scoping Review and an Architecture of Epistemic Control
detail.abstract: AI-assisted research systems increasingly automate literature search, coding, statistical analysis, visualization, and manuscript drafting. Automation alone, however, does not resolve the underlying methodological problem of empirical research: how to distinguish exploration from confirmation, preserve provenance, control the latitude of analytical decisions, and ensure that claims do not outrun the evidentiary status of the data and the study design. This article is a scoping review of six approaches bearing on this challenge-preregistration and registered reports, pre-analysis plans in economics, multiverse analysis and specification curve, reproducible research and research compendia, FAIR and provenance standards, and emerging AI-for-science workflows. We synthesize these approaches into a spec-driven AI methodology for empirical research (FSAIM), announced separately as a position note [10.2139/ssrn.6853581], in which hypotheses, data, code, artifacts, claims, and AI actions are treated as auditable objects within a staged workflow featuring human gates for approval. The proposed framework casts AI not as a shortcut for writing but as a component of an epistemically bounded research engine. We discuss implications for empirical economics and finance, where secondary data, look-ahead bias, specification multiplicity, and publication incentives create persistent risks to credibility.

reference: Faiza Ismail, 'Islamic financing in Europe: recent developments in Ireland' (2017) 38(2) Company Lawyer 48
title: Islamic Financing in Europe: Recent Developments in Ireland

detail.title: Islamic Financing in Europe: Recent Developments in Ireland

publicationDetails.detailsText: Faiza Ismail, 'Islamic financing in Europe: recent developments in Ireland' (2017) 38(2) Company Lawyer 48

detail.abstract: This article examines the development of Islamic finance (IF) across Europe, with a particular focus on Ireland's position within this landscape. It surveys IF developments in France, Germany, and the UK—identifying the UK as the most developed and sophisticated European market—before turning to Ireland's specific opportunities for growth. The article argues that three factors are driving IF's emergence as an alternative financing source in Europe: the 2008 financial crisis, liquidity generated by rising oil prices, and demand from Europe's growing Muslim population. Building on the author's earlier work comparing Irish and UK Islamic finance strategies, this article identifies four Irish industries with strong potential to attract Islamic investment: the fund industry, the aviation finance industry, the special purpose vehicle (SPV) industry, and trade finance. It highlights Ireland's competitive advantages—including its low corporate tax rate, common law tradition, English-speaking status, extensive double taxation treaty network, and world-leading position in aviation leasing—as key assets for positioning Dublin as a hub for Sharia-compliant investment. The article explains how Sukuk (Islamic bonds) can serve as a practical channel for directing Islamic investment into these sectors, using the East Cameron Sukuk as a case study of successful Islamic financing in a non-Islamic jurisdiction. It concludes with concrete recommendations for Ireland to develop a coordinated public-private strategy—including a dedicated working group, expanded use of existing trade networks with the Gulf and Malaysia, and targeted marketing efforts—to position Ireland as a Eurozone centre for Islamic finance.

title: Joint Physical Custody Laws and Maternal Mental Health: Evidence from Modern U.S. State Reforms
affiliations: Capital University of Economics and Business and University of West Georgia

detail.title: Joint Physical Custody Laws and Maternal Mental Health: Evidence from Modern U.S. State Reforms

declarations.funderStatement: Guo acknowledges financial support from the National Natural Science Foundation of China, Grant 72103038.

detail.abstract: This study presents the first causal evidence on how U.S. pro-joint physical custody laws (PJPCLs) affect mothers' mental health. Exploiting the staggered adoption of state reforms during the 2010s, we apply the Gardner (2022) difference-indifferences estimator to multiple large-scale survey and administrative datasets. Our first-stage analysis provides descriptive evidence that court-ordered joint physical custody increases by 17.8 percent following the reforms. Using the 2010-2024 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS), we find that PJPCLs increase the number of poor mental health days among mothers aged 18-44 by 12.6 percent, with the effects emerging gradually over the post-reform period. Our estimates are robust to inference procedures designed for a small number of treated clusters and are similar under triple-difference specifications comparing mothers to childless women within the same state. We also find little evidence that the estimated mental health effects are driven by selection into parenthood or interstate migration. Additional analyses reveal that mothers increase childcare time and reduce labor supply, alongside declines in marital dissolution and intimate partner violence. These patterns are consistent with heavier childcare constraints and weakened intra-household bargaining power. Overall, these results suggest that reforms intended to equalize parental involvement impose unintended psychological costs on the parent who had traditionally been the primary caregiver.

detail.abstract: Microplastic (MP) contamination in agricultural soils has emerged as a pervasive environmental challenge, driven by extensive plastic production and inadequate waste management practices. Since the mid-twentieth century, global plastic output has exceeded 8,000 million tonnes, a substantial fraction of which has fragmented into microplastics (<5 mm), enabling their widespread distribution across agroecosystems. This chapter critically examines the sources, environmental pathways, and mechanistic impacts of MPs within the agro-pedospheric system, with particular emphasis on soil structure, microbial dynamics, and crop productivity. Microplastics enter agricultural soils through diverse anthropogenic routes, including plastic mulch degradation, biosolid application, wastewater irrigation, atmospheric deposition, and organic amendments. Once incorporated, MPs induce multifaceted alterations in soil physical, chemical, and biological properties. Structural disruptions include reductions in bulk density, porosity, and aggregate stability, which collectively impair water retention and nutrient cycling processes. At the biological level, MP exposure alters soil microbial community composition, reduces microbial biomass and enzymatic activity, and disrupts key functions such as nitrogen fixation and carbon mineralisation. These changes adversely affect plant growth by inhibiting seed germination, root development, nutrient acquisition, and overall crop performance, thereby posing a significant risk to agricultural sustainability and food security. The chapter further evaluates emerging remediation strategies, including biochar application, microbial bioaugmentation, phytoremediation, and the adoption of biodegradable lignocellulosic bioplastics as sustainable alternatives to conventional plastics. While these approaches demonstrate promising potential, their Agricultural Sciences: Techniques and Innovations Vol. 9 Microplastic-Induced Perturbations in Agro-Pedospheric Microbial Networks and Crop Homeodynamics 17 large-scale applicability and long-term effectiveness require further validation under field conditions. Overall, this chapter provides a comprehensive synthesis of current knowledge, identifies critical research gaps, and highlights the need for integrated management strategies and policy interventions to mitigate microplastic pollution and ensure resilient agroecosystems.

title: Beyond Recognition: Belonging as a Scientific, Evolutionary, and Post-Essentialist Foundation for Social Philosophy

detail.title: Beyond Recognition: Belonging as a Scientific, Evolutionary, and Post-Essentialist Foundation for Social Philosophy
detail.abstract: Theories of recognition have transformed contemporary social and political philosophy by demonstrating that identity, dignity, and justice are fundamentally relational achievements. Charles Taylor emphasized the dialogical constitution of identity, Axel Honneth reconstructed moral development through relations of love, rights, and solidarity, and Nancy Fraser connected recognition to redistribution and participatory parity. Together, these approaches established recognition as one of the central paradigms of modern social theory. This article argues, however, that recognition remains philosophically incomplete because it begins too late. Recognition explains how individuals become morally visible to one another, but it does not explain the deeper relational structures that make recognition itself possible. Human beings do not first exist as isolated individuals and subsequently enter relations of recognition. They emerge within pre-existing structures of belonging that sustain life, cooperation, identity, institutions, recognition, and civilization. The Philosophy of Belonging proposes an alternative foundation for social philosophy. Rather than beginning with ethical concerns, it begins from contemporary science. Physics, evolutionary biology, neuroscience, psychology, institutional theory, economics, and complexity science converge upon a common insight: existence is relationally embedded, temporally structured, and historically conditioned. Human beings survive, cooperate, and develop because they belong before they recognize. The argument is developed through four principles of the Philosophy of Belonging: being is belonging; reality possesses synchronic and diachronic dimensions; belonging is necessarily imperfect; and reality is stratified into material, biological, and institutionalhuman levels. Particular emphasis is placed upon the third principle. Imperfect belonging is not a social failure but an evolutionary necessity. The tension between individuality and belonging constitutes one of the principal mechanisms through which societies adapt, innovate, and survive. This perspective leads to a reinterpretation of institutions, capitalism, and globalization. Historically, capitalism expanded with remarkable speed because it proved uniquely successful at institutionalizing competition within structures of belonging. Contemporary crises emerge because globalization has expanded competition, mobility, and interdependence faster than institutions capable of sustaining belonging. The article concludes that recognition explains dignity, while belonging explains existence. Recognition remains indispensable for contemporary moral life, but belonging constitutes the deeper ontological condition of cooperation, institutional continuity, economic development, and civilizational survival. If the twentieth century in the Western societies was shaped by recognition, the twenty-first century may increasingly become the century of global belonging.

title: Policy Orchestration and Entrepreneurial Ecosystem Performance in the UAE: A Multi-Level Framework for SDG 8-Oriented Economic Development

detail.title: Policy Orchestration and Entrepreneurial Ecosystem Performance in the UAE: A Multi-Level Framework for SDG 8-Oriented Economic Development

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA
declarations.ethicsApproval: NA
declarations.funderStatement: NA

detail.abstract: Purpose: In this paper, a UAE-oriented framework is developed which explains how policy orchestration transforms entrepreneurial ecosystem assets into startup scaling, non-oil economic upgrading and SDG 8 oriented decent work impacts. The paper addresses a contemporary issue in entrepreneurial ecosystem literature whereby despite advancement in the theoretical discourse from single-factor models of success, there is limited understanding of how policy ambition can be translated to ecosystem performance in state-led and internationalised economies. Design/methodology/approach: An integrative literature review and policy synthesis approach is used in this paper. Recent entrepreneurial ecosystem, innovation cluster, institutional and sustainable development literature is combined with publicly available UAE policy and ecosystem information such as the We the UAE 2031, Dubai Economic Agenda D33, Operation 300bn, National Agenda for Entrepreneurship and SMEs, Hub71 and DIFC Innovation Hub. Findings: Five propositions are put forward showing that entrepreneurial ecosystems deliver more impact if there is coherent orchestration of national strategies, regulatory experimentation, finance, talent, clustering specialisation and market access. Impact is made through a proposed Policy Orchestration-Cluster Conversion-Impact framework. Originality/value: The paper uses the UAE to explain the entrepreneurial ecosystems of diversifying economies. It provides a practical dashboard of governance for policy makers and ecosystem builders to move from mere activity metrics to productivity, decent work and sustainable economic development.

title: The Mediation of Lack: The Feminine Position and the Structure of the Subject in Lacan

detail.title: The Mediation of Lack: The Feminine Position and the Structure of the Subject in Lacan
detail.abstract: Psychoanalysis has met, since its inception, a structural obstacle at the question of the feminine. Taking Lacan's assertion that the woman does not exist as its point of departure, this paper reconstructs the generative mechanism of the feminine position within his theory of the symbolic order, and argues that the defining character of that position is captured precisely by the term the mediation of lack. The argument falls into two parts of equal weight. The first proceeds within Lacanian theory. The self-referential structure of the symbolic system, which can never exhaust the real, makes lack something that must be mediated rather than confronted or abolished, and the objet petit a is on this account a structural necessity. Against this background the masculine position secures a closable location through the having and not-having distinction organized by a central signifier, while the feminine position stands in an unclosed zone between the symbolic and the real, its stability resting instead on the persistence of a relational dynamics. There arises from this a mechanism by which the subject internalizes the persistence of lack as a function of itself, becoming the site at which lack is kept relatable, accessible, and open to continued questioning. The second part does not rest in exposition. It passes first through the feminist and post-structuralist critique, which discloses that what is confining in this position issues from the historical construction of a particular symbolic order rather than from structural necessity, and then reframes the position within the framework of Generative Relational Being, under which the mediation of lack is not a defect but the site at which relational value is generated. On this basis the ethics of the position is set out through five ordered principles, which specify the conditions under which the mediation of lack is just rather than exploited. The account issues in an ethic and closes, in the manner it requires of itself, on the questions that ethic opens.

title: Empirical Likelihood Tests for Pairwise Stochastic Dominance
affiliations: Athens University of Economics and Business - Department of Economics, University College Dublin (UCD) - Michael Smurfit Graduate School of Business and Nazarbayev University - Graduate School of Business

detail.title: Empirical Likelihood Tests for Pairwise Stochastic Dominance
detail.abstract: We develop an empirical likelihood test for pairwise stochastic dominance in weakly dependent time series. The procedure localizes candidate binding constraints as local minima of the empirical integrated distribution gap, then computes a multivariate empirical likelihood ratio over the resulting contact set. Critical values use re-centered pseudo-samples, implemented blockwise for dependence. The statistic is self-normalizing and covariance-adaptive, aggregating joint evidence from localized contacts rather than relying on a supremum or integrated support-wide distance. We prove first-order asymptotic validity and show that the null limit is a Gaussian-cone, or chi-bar-square, projection governed by the covariance of binding moments. Local-power results show equivalence between empirical likelihood and benchmark distance tests with one binding constraint, but possible power gains with multiple bindings because empirical likelihood exploits contact-set covariance geometry. Monte Carlo designs calibrated to option-enhanced indexation show accurate, stable size, robustness to the localization threshold, feasible calibration, and high power relative to Linton--Maasoumi--Whang and Linton--Song--Whang tests, especially when local violations align with covariance features captured by the statistic. An application to option-strategy indices rejects more economically implausible pairwise dominance relations, consistent with strategies trading off upside participation, option income, and downside protection rather than dominating each other.

title: Forecasting: Returns or Prices?
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Forecasting: Returns or Prices?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest.

detail.abstract: This paper validates the Expectations hypothesis for the stock market using Futures data. It explains that price forecasts are reasonably accurate but returns forecasts are not because prices are level variables whereas returns are ratios and an economic relationship that might exist between levels may not extend to their ratios. This drawback is somewhat resolved by considering average returns since these incorporate the economic relationship between the levels into its ratios by considering multiple past prices. Further, it is found that forecasted average returns generate higher profits for daily and weekly frequencies than forecasted plain or traditional returns.

title: The Logical Framework of Human Behavior and Economics

detail.title: The Logical Framework of Human Behavior and Economics
detail.abstract: Human behavior is highly complex, and its underlying logic has long resisted systematic explanation. This paper advances four axioms as a general logical foundation for the analysis of human behavior and economics, from which ten corollaries are derived to form a unified theoretical framework. The framework provides a common basis for addressing major questions in economics and political economy, including the instability of extractive political institutions and the rise of sustained modern economic growth. More broadly, the paper highlights the possibility of explaining important phenomena in human behavior and economics through a small set of general principles rather than only through fragmented, case-specific accounts.

title: Intra-Annual Timing of Discretionary Agricultural Trade Interventions
affiliations: University of Colorado at Boulder, University of Colorado Boulder, University of Nebraska at Lincoln and University of Nebraska at Lincoln - Department of Economics

detail.title: Intra-Annual Timing of Discretionary Agricultural Trade Interventions
detail.abstract: We examine the intra-annual timing of discretionary agricultural trade interventions for maize, rice, and wheat. Relating intervention timing to production cycles reveals that many interventions occur during growing seasons when policymakers lack complete harvest information. Based on this observation, we ask whether hypothesized drivers of intervention-international price and domestic yield-are more strongly related to intervention probability during different parts of the production cycle. We find strong associations between intervention and two yield signals at different times: realized yield with some delay after harvest and satellite-derived proxies for crop conditions during the season. Prices are consistently associated with intervention throughout the year.

title: South Africa's Road Fatalities and the Insolvent Road Accident Fund: How Did We End Up Here?
affiliations: Stellenbosch University

detail.title: South Africa's Road Fatalities and the Insolvent Road Accident Fund: How Did We End Up Here?
detail.abstract: South Africa's road fatality rate remains among the worst globally, exceeding 24 deaths per 100,000 population, far above the world average of 15 and the EU average of 6.1. Despite the UN's Decade of Action for Road Safety (2021–2030) targeting a 50% reduction in deaths, South Africa has shown no meaningful improvement since 2000, unlike EU counterparts, which have seen dramatic declines. This editorial traces the history of South Africa's road accident compensation system, from voluntary insurance before 1942 through successive legislative reforms, from the Motor Vehicle Insurance Act (1942), the Motor Vehicle Accident Fund (1965), the shift to a fuel-levy model (1986), and the establishment of the current Road Accident Fund (RAF) in 1997.  Today, the RAF is deeply insolvent, with liabilities exceeding R450 billion against R50 billion in annual revenue, spending more on legal fees than on road safety campaigns. The editorial argues that South Africa's policy focus has misplaced priorities, emphasising the Fund's financial viability rather than reducing fatalities. It calls for proven international interventions, including lower speed limits, demerit-point licensing systems, and risk-based insurance tied to driving behaviour and concludes that saving lives, not sustaining the RAF, should be the true measure of success.

title: Welfare Observability: A Cost-Coverage Frontier for AI Oversight Under Evasion

detail.title: Welfare Observability: A Cost-Coverage Frontier for AI Oversight Under Evasion
detail.abstract: AI oversight has been framed as certification: prove the deployment is safe, or prove its agent is aligned. That question is impossible from inside-only signals under the companion non-identifiability premise; exogenous probes are the intended escape, not a contradiction. This paper changes the question. Let welfare coverage 𝐶(𝐵) be the share of a deployment's welfare-relevant behavior that an instrument actually observes at probe budget 𝐵. We model a deployment as welfare slices with heterogeneous welfare-damage density, behavior mass, probe cost, and an adversary detection parameter, and we characterize the cost-coverage frontier: in the passive case it is a separable concave allocation solved exactly by welfare-damage-weighted water-filling, increasing and concave in 𝐵, asymptoting to a ceiling 𝐶 max < 1 when a positive share of welfare mass has no valid exogenous probe. A strategic model can flatten finite-budget coverage by relocating or masking welfare-damaging behavior in slices the auditor covers weakly; this version does not claim that evasion lowers the infinite-budget ceiling beyond the unprobeable floor. The concavity and the water-filling are standard once the problem is posed; what is new is the object: welfare coverage as a measured quantity and, under a separate unprobeable-mass assumption, a coverage ceiling that persists at infinite budget. A construction, the cryptographically committed, distribution-embedded known-answer probe, builds one cheap, trustworthy atom under stationarity and exogenous-traffic assumptions, and we plot a synthetic frontier: welfare-weighted allocation reaches ninety percent of the passive ceiling roughly three times cheaper than uniform in this instance, while an adversarial allocation flattens the finite-budget curve by concentrating evasion on heavy welfare-weight slices. Welfare observability, not certification, is the governable quantity.

title: Mentorship And Belonging as Drivers of Retention: An Improvement Science Approach to Supporting Black Male Educators in Specialized School Settings

detail.title: Mentorship And Belonging as Drivers of Retention: An Improvement Science Approach to Supporting Black Male Educators in Specialized School Settings

keywords: Educational Leadership Education Policy Black Male Educators Teacher Retention Educator Workforce Diversity Improvement Science Mentorship Organizational Belonging Antiracist Leadership Equity in Education Teacher Diversity Educator Retention Leadership Development Organizational Change Culturally Responsive Leadership Critical Race Theory Affinity Spaces Professional Development School Improvement Human Resource Management in Education

detail.abstract: The underrepresentation and high attrition of Black male educators in U.S. schools remain persistent challenges with implications for equity, student outcomes, and organizational stability. This Dissertation of Practice addressed the problem of limited retention and professional growth of Black male educators at Rivermont Alexandria, a specialized school for students with autism, where foundational staff supports were present but did not adequately meet the identity-affirming needs of this group. The guiding research questions examined how intentional mentorship and structured affinity spaces could improve Black male educators’ sense of belonging, professional efficacy, and intent to remain in the organization. Using a mixed-methods, improvement science design, the study implemented a 6-week pilot intervention—Mentor Mondays—that paired Black male educators with strengths-based mentors and created biweekly peer-led affinity sessions. Data were collected through pre- and post-intervention surveys, reflection logs, focus groups, and attendance tracking. Analysis revealed that participants reported stronger perceptions of mentorship quality, increased belonging within peer groups, and greater professional affirmation. However, outcomes also showed persistent gaps in organizational belonging and clarity of career advancement pathways. Importantly, the intervention highlighted a leadership lesson: Retention efforts must prioritize the retention of quality and committed Black male educators, not indiscriminate retention based on identity alone. The findings supported theoretical insights from organizational support theory, relationalcultural theory, and critical race theory, demonstrating that mentorship and belonging structures are critical but insufficient without systems of accountability and transparent career development. The researcher concluded that schools can strengthen Black male educator retention by embedding culturally affirming mentorship and affinity spaces into existing structures, while simultaneously maintaining professional standards. Limitations included the short pilot timeframe and single-site scope. Recommendations for practice included codifying mentorship systems, institutionalizing affinity spaces with trained facilitators, and developing clear advancement pathways for Black male educators across the network.

title: NYC's Ride-Hailing Cordons (2019, 2025): A Modern-DiD Replication and Re-examination

detail.title: NYC's Ride-Hailing Cordons (2019, 2025): A Modern-DiD Replication and Re-examination
detail.abstract: Li and Vignon (2024) estimate that NYC's 2019 ride-hailing surcharge reduced trip volume inside the cordon by 9.4 percent. This number anchors how policymakers and analysts discuss congestion-targeting fees on ride-hailing. This paper revisits the estimate using modern difference-indifferences diagnostics that postdate the original publication, and applies the same identification framework to NYC's January 2025 Congestion Relief Zone. Using public Taxi and Limousine Commission trip records, we reconstruct the 2019 surcharge zone (the published paper does not list its zones) and reproduce the headline coefficient within 0.2 percentage points under the original's preferred specification. Honest difference-indifferences bounds (Rambachan and Roth 2023) show the 2019 anchor surviving small deviations from parallel trends past M = 0.5, with the partial-identification interval re-including zero between M = 0.5 and M = 1.0; the 2025 specifications are more fragile, with the interval re-including zero between M = 0.25 and M = 0.5, where M governs the maximum admissible relative magnitude between pre-trend and post-period slope changes. A triple-difference revision that absorbs pre-existing Manhattan central business district drift places the policy-attributable share of the 2019 effect at-3.6 percent (95-percent CI [-6.6,-0.5]), roughly one-third of the published headline. This estimate is our least robust: its confidence interval approaches zero, and the Honest-DiD bounds on the underlying anchor re-include zero at moderate departures from parallel trends (M = 0.5-1.0), so the-3.6-percent figure is best read as "materially smaller than the published 9.4 percent, and plausibly consistent with a small effect" rather than a sharp point estimate. Three months after the 2025 cordon launched, analogous specifications place its effect on inside-cordon ride-hailing volume between-4 and-8 percent, with the November 2024 reinstatement-announcement window explaining most of the within-range variation. Both cordons reduced ride-hailing trip volume, but by less than the published 9.4-percent benchmark suggests. Two ancillary findings reinforce the recalibration: (i) a SUTVA-by-outcome contamination-Li and Vignon (2024)'s preferred outcome variable counts only trips ending in the cordon for control zones, and substituting it into the triple-difference flips the sign positive, a clean demonstration that outcome definitions that shift mechanically with the treatment in the control group leak policy effects into the control baseline; and (ii) on a geographic apples-to-apples basis (restricting the 2019 sample to the 38 zones inside both cordons), the 2019 estimate falls to approximately-4 percent, comparable in magnitude to the 2025 range under like-for-like geography. The methodological contribution is identifying pre-existing CBD drift as a confounder that the original TWFE design absorbs into the policy coefficient.

title: Elbows Up: Economic Coercion and U.S. Border Labor Markets in the 2025 Trade War

detail.title: Elbows Up: Economic Coercion and U.S. Border Labor Markets in the 2025 Trade War
detail.abstract: In early 2025 the United States imposed tariffs on Canada and paired them with public statements questioning Canadian sovereignty, an act of economic coercion against a close ally. This paper asks what such coercion costs and where the burden falls. Canadians responded, amid widely reported anger, by sharply curtailing travel to the United States; we trace where that redirection-whatever mix of boycott sentiment and other U.S.-specific deterrents drove itlanded inside the coercing country, at the local-labor-market level. Pairing predetermined (2024) cross-border-visitor exposure with monthly employment across 390 metropolitan areas, we find leisure and hospitality employment associated with land-crossing exposure at roughly-0.57% per standard deviation after onset. The association is descriptive, but stable in sign and magnitude across randomization and spatially clustered inference, explicit seasonal adjustment, and within-Census-division comparison. Falsification tests tie the decline to the U.S.-Canada episode rather than to the tariffs the two countries shared: the tariffed southern border, where crossings never fell, shows no gradient; controlling for a metro's own tariff exposure does not attenuate the decline; and Canadian trips overseas rose even as trips to the United States collapsed. The incidence differs by travel mode because the dose does: Canadians were only a few percent of arrivals even at large airports, so air destinations lost nothing detectable, while land day-trip economies lost on the order of ten to thirty thousand jobs. We read that range as an upper bound on gross local losses, worth several hundred million to a billion dollars a year in earnings. A February 2026 ruling struck the tariffs down; neither travel nor jobs returned within our window. Part of the cost of the coercion fell inside the country that imposed it, concentrated in border communities that leaned against the party whose policy provoked the backlash.

title: Does Free Trade Favor Dynastic Business Families?
affiliations: Thammasat Business School

detail.title: Does Free Trade Favor Dynastic Business Families?
detail.abstract: Free-trade and economic-integration agreements (FTEIAs) create new opportunities for firms to expand. While these agreements may foster entrepreneurial wealth through creative destruction, they may also favor dynastic business families that are better positioned to capture the gains through privileged access to capital. Using a stacked difference-indifferences design around 36 FTEIAs from 1986-2020, together with handcollected billionaire data distinguishing dynastic from entrepreneurial wealth, I find that FTEIAs increase wealth controlled by dynastic business families. Following an agreement, dynastic wealth-to-GDP rises by 0.27 percentage points annually (15% of its standard deviation), while entrepreneurial wealth-to-GDP shows no significant change. Further evidence is consistent with a privileged-access-to-capital mechanism: the effect is stronger in financially underdeveloped countries, and post-agreement increases in dynastic wealth-to-GDP are associated with slower productivity growth. These findings suggest that, without strong financial systems, trade liberalization may reinforce the dominance of dynastic families rather than promote entrepreneurial wealth creation.

title: A Reluctant Stakeholder: Russia's Position on Traditional Medicine in BRICS Health Cooperation

detail.title: A Reluctant Stakeholder: Russia's Position on Traditional Medicine in BRICS Health Cooperation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No competing interests.
declarations.funderStatement: None.

detail.abstract: Russia's engagement with BRICS health cooperation under India's 2026 presidency is cooperative but uneven: Moscow has invested in high-technology, security-adjacent tracks — nuclear medicine, tuberculosis research, early-warning systems — while remaining conspicuously absent from the bloc's growing consensus around traditional, complementary, and integrative medicine (TCIM). This brief argues that Russia's distance from the TCIM agenda reflects a structural gap, not a judgment of its worth: unlike India's Ministry of AYUSH or China's institutionalized Traditional Chinese Medicine framework, Russia has no comparable domestic apparatus, and its existing folk-medicine provisions sit outside mainstream clinical care and state insurance. That gap is closeable, and closing it serves Russia's own interests: prevention-oriented, lower-cost care is a rational fiscal choice for a country managing sustained defense expenditure elsewhere in its budget, not a symbolic gesture toward its BRICS partners. The brief recommends BRICS build a dedicated mechanism for sharing implementation knowledge between institutionally mature and institutionally thin members, fund independent TCIM research rather than relying on Western validation, and treat India's AYUSH rollout as a shared, ongoing laboratory rather than a finished model — positioning Russia as a future contributor to this agenda rather than a permanent bystander.

title: Natural disasters and fiscal shelters
affiliations: and Universidad Carlos III de Madrid

detail.title: Natural disasters and fiscal shelters

publicationDetails.detailsText: Banco de Espana Working Paper No. 2612
publicationDetails.journalName: Banco de Espana Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Using a novel dataset on U.S. natural disasters and high-frequency measures of economic activity, we evaluate the effectiveness of federal disaster assistance. Exploiting quasi-random variation in whether aid from the Federal Emergency Management Agency is granted or denied, we compare otherwise similar events. States receiving aid recover within 20 weeks, whereas denied states face deeper and more persistent contractions. Recovery is stronger when aid is timely and generous, and includes direct transfers. Pre-disaster mitigation lowers future disaster frequency and costs, while stronger fiscal capacity enhances resilience by enabling governments to sustain post-disaster recovery.
