title: Issuance Yield of MREL-Eligible Bank Debt: A Benchmarking Model
affiliations: Universidad de Oviedo - Department of Business Administration, ,  and

detail.title: Issuance Yield of MREL-Eligible Bank Debt: A Benchmarking Model

publicationDetails.detailsText: Banco de Espana Working Paper No. 2607
publicationDetails.journalName: Banco de Espana Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper develops a benchmarking framework to assess the cost of issuing MREL-eligible debt, enabling structured comparisons across banks, instruments and jurisdictions. Using data on 12,075 securities issued by 206 banks in the banking union from 2019 Q3 to 2024 Q3, we quantify how bank characteristics, macroeconomic conditions and instrument features affect issuance costs. Compared with banks with assets below €100 billion, global systemically important institutions benefit from significantly lower costs, down by 92 basis points, while other systemically important institutions and top-tier banks benefit by 88 basis points. Higher credit ratings are associated with up to an 86 basis point reduction in issuance spreads; greater efficiency, proxied by a lower cost-to-income ratio, also narrows spreads. The overnight index swap rate is the most influential macroeconomic factor, with each percentage point increase associated with a 97 basis point rise in costs. Longer maturities and greater subordination significantly increase funding costs. Lastly, we apply the model to decompose issuance costs for seven Spanish banks, identifying key cost drivers across institutions, and to simulate the impact of issuing senior non-preferred versus senior debt for four European banks near the €100 billion size threshold, documenting the implications of subordination requirements for banks’ net income.

title: Severe Class Imbalance versus Near-Balanced Regimes in Seismic Hazard Classification: A Comparative Machine Learning and Explainable AI Study of Explosion Discrimination and Tsunami Risk Assessment
affiliations: Macquarie University

detail.title: Severe Class Imbalance versus Near-Balanced Regimes in Seismic Hazard Classification: A Comparative Machine Learning and Explainable AI Study of Explosion Discrimination and Tsunami Risk Assessment
detail.abstract: Machine learning is increasingly used to triage seismic hazard data streams, yet published pipelines rarely examine how the same modelling recipe behaves under two very different label distributions. This study reports two parallel classification experiments built on an identical extended model zoo, cross-validation protocol, and explainability toolkit, applied to (i) a severely imbalanced task discriminating man-made explosive events (quarry blasts, mining and chemical explosions) from natural earthquakes in a rolling 30-day United States Geological Survey (USGS) feed (10,505 events, 1.85% positive rate), and (ii) a near-balanced task predicting tsunami potential from 782 globally catalogued significant earthquakes (2001-2022, 38.9% positive rate). Twelve classifiers spanning linear, instancebased, kernel, tree-ensemble, boosting, neural, stacking, and attention-based tabular (TabNet) families were benchmarked with 10-fold stratified cross-validation, Friedman omnibus and Holm-Bonferroni-corrected pairwise Wilcoxon significance testing, and a four-method explainability suite (SHAP, LIME, permutation importance, partial dependence/ICE). On the explosion-discrimination task, gradient-boosted trees dominated (LightGBM: mean crossvalidated PR-AUC = 0.989, hold-out F1 = 0.974 on the minority class), with depth-related features driving predictions consistent with the near-surface seismic signature of blasting. On the tsunami-risk task, GradientBoosting was the best-ranked model by mean AUC (0.948, hold-out AUC = 0.954, F1 = 0.887), a materially harder ceiling than the explosion task despite the more balanced labels, reflecting genuine geophysical ambiguity in tsunami genesis rather than an artefact of class skew. In both experiments, the Friedman test rejected the null of equal classifier performance (p < 10⁻⁶), yet none of the 66 pairwise Holm-corrected comparisons per dataset reached significance a pattern we discuss as a caution against over-interpreting narrow leaderboard rankings from 10-fold designs. We contribute a reproducible, side-by-side comparative framework, a full multi-method explainability audit for both tasks, and an explicit leakage-sensitivity check demonstrating the explosion classifier's performance is not an artefact of reportingnetwork identity. Results suggest that classical gradient boosting remains competitive with, or superior to, more recent attention-based tabular architectures at the sample sizes typical of curated seismic hazard datasets, and that PR-AUCfirst reporting under severe imbalance yields more defensible headline metrics than ROC-AUC alone.

title:
The Dual Dollar System 
A New Framework for the Functional Separation of Financial and Trade Currencies in the International Monetary System
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title:
The Dual Dollar System 
A New Framework for the Functional Separation of Financial and Trade Currencies in the International Monetary System
detail.abstract:
The U.S. dollar currently serves two fundamentally different functions within the international monetary system. It functions both as the principal currency for international trade settlement and as the dominant currency supporting global financial markets. While this dual role has contributed to the stability and development of the postwar international monetary order, it also creates structural interactions between international trade and international finance, making it difficult to pursue independent policy objectives for each.

This paper proposes the Dual Dollar System (DDS), a new institutional framework that functionally separates these two roles into distinct currencies: the Trade Dollar, used exclusively for international trade settlement, and the Financial Dollar, used for domestic economic activity and international capital markets.

Rather than replacing the existing dollar-based international monetary system, the proposed framework seeks to strengthen its long-term stability by separating two fundamentally different economic functions currently concentrated within a single reserve currency.

The proposed system introduces three independent policy instruments: the policy interest rate, the supply of each currency, and the exchange rate between the Financial Dollar and the Trade Dollar. These instruments may provide policymakers with greater flexibility in managing monetary policy, international trade, financial stability, and economic competitiveness.

This paper presents the conceptual design of the Dual Dollar System, discusses its potential advantages and institutional challenges, and identifies important directions for future theoretical, empirical, and policy-oriented research.

title: "Over-Modeling" in Economics: Behavioral Postulates, Institutional Frameworks, and Empirical Discipline
affiliations: Nankai University

detail.title: "Over-Modeling" in Economics: Behavioral Postulates, Institutional Frameworks, and Empirical Discipline
detail.abstract: Recent Chinese academic discussions have brought methodological questions in economic research back into view. Lu (2026) characterizes one tendency as "over-modeling": model construction may fail to incorporate real-world context, so that researchers "ignore reality in order to make the model work," while the pursuit of methodological complexity and precision may lead researchers to "sacrifice the question in order to make the method work." This paper acknowledges this observation, but argues that the problem is not peculiar to recent Chinese economic research. The issue is not modeling itself, but how to judge when modeling becomes "over." To make this judgment more concrete, I propose a three-part account: economic explanation needs to state how actors form goals, beliefs, and modes of choice (Behavioral Postulates); under what rules and payoff consequences they act (Institutional Frameworks); and what evidence disciplines claims about the magnitude and scope of the proposed mechanisms (Empirical Discipline). Over-modeling can be understood as an imbalance or disconnection among these three elements. The paper develops this argument through Ricardo's abstraction and Schumpeter's critique of the "Ricardian vice," the Menger-Historical School debate, and the Mises-Friedman disagreement over a priori deduction and empirical testing. The same account is then used to understand recent controversies over econometric identification in historical research. Finally, I use auction theory and option pricing as examples to argue that complex models need not constitute over-modeling when their behavioral logic, institutional conditions, and channels of empirical feedback are clear.

title: No Free Universality: A Pre-Registered Null for Asset-Invariant Microstructure Representations in an Off-the-Shelf LLM
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: No Free Universality: A Pre-Registered Null for Asset-Invariant Microstructure Representations in an Off-the-Shelf LLM

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests. This is independent research conducted without institutional or commercial affiliation. No external party had any role in the study's design, execution, analysis, or the decision to publish.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study involves no human participants, animal subjects, or personal data. All data are derived from publicly available cryptocurrency exchange market-data streams (order-book and trade events), which contain no personally identifiable information.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. All compute and data-collection costs were borne by the author using personal resources.

detail.abstract: Do neural representations of market microstructure converge across assets? We test the Platonic Representation Hypothesis in a domain it has not visited: numeric, human-generated, high-frequency order-book state. Five spot pairs on one venue are sampled contemporaneously at 5 Hz (21,950 matched windows); each window is rendered into an identical, asset-blind nine-feature line and read by a frozen Mistral-7B-Instruct encoder; a pre-registered criterion requires representational excess over the cross-asset alignment already present in the inputs, increasing with depth. The hypothesis is not supported: at the peak layer, time-matched cross-asset CKA (mean 0.025) sits below the z-scored input floor (mean 0.048), 0/10 pairs pass, and alignment decreases with depth (Spearman-0.30)-the inverse of the abstraction signature. The representations are nonetheless not orthogonal: all 10 pairs exceed shuffle (≈ 0.001) and dimensionality (≈ 0.0005) floors-small structure transmitted from the inputs, not amplified. Two standalone observations follow. Contemporaneous cross-asset co-movement of order-book states is tiny at 5 Hz (input CKA 0.03-0.08 z-scored): crypto beta is a returns-level phenomenon, not a microstructure-state one at this sampling. And state-matched cross-asset alignment reaches ≈88% of the within-asset ceiling for a shared encoder-high partly by construction, formalizing why asset-blind probes cannot test asset-invariance of learning. We further document a numerical failure mode-catastrophic cancellation in fp32 unbiased-HSIC on uncentered LLM Gram matrices, producing CKA values above 1-and the validation protocol that repairs it. A discriminating from-scratch follow-up is pre-registered.

title: Sunset Provisions
affiliations: Charles III University of Madrid and University of Chicago

detail.title: Sunset Provisions

declarations.funderStatement: Antoine Loeper gratefully acknowledges the financial support of MICIN/AEI/10.13039/501100011033, grants CEX2021-001181-M, CNS2022-135957, and PID2022-142153NB-I00, and of Fundación Ramon Areces, grant CSIP17A5892.

detail.abstract: A temporary law is a law that is enacted with a pre-specified expiration date. The clause that sets that date is commonly called a sunset provision. The standard argument for sunset provisions is that they counteract legislative inertia and prevent capture by special interest: they force policymakers to revisit laws, programs, or regulations after a fixed period and to preserve only those that remain justified considering new information, changed circumstances, or demonstrated performance. This paper reviews the existing literature on the presumed benefits of sunset provisions and puts it to the test of empirical evidence and of recent development in the legislative bargaining literature.

title: From Knowledge to Capability: Why Digital Financial Literacy Does Not Translate into Entrepreneurial Capital Access

detail.title: From Knowledge to Capability: Why Digital Financial Literacy Does Not Translate into Entrepreneurial Capital Access

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study involved survey-based research with entrepreneur participants. Participation was voluntary, informed consent was obtained from all respondents, and responses were analyzed anonymously and used only for academic research purposes.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: The expansion of digital financial systems has significantly improved access to financial services for entrepreneurs, particularly in emerging markets. A central assumption underlying these developments is that increasing financial literacy will enhance entrepreneurial outcomes, including access to capital. However, the extent to which financial knowledge translates into effective financial decision-making remains unclear. This study examines the relationship between digital financial literacy, financial self-efficacy, and entrepreneurial outcomes using a two-study design. In Study 1, survey data from 226 entrepreneurs show that digital financial literacy does not have a significant direct effect on capital access, while financial self-efficacy is a strong and consistent predictor. Study 2 complements these findings using a scenario-based decision experiment with 96 entrepreneurs. The results indicate that decision quality is negatively affected by behavioral bias and positively influenced by self-efficacy. Importantly, the effect of financial literacy is conditional and depends on the level of cognitive bias. Together, the findings suggest that financial knowledge alone is insufficient. Its effectiveness depends on both psychological capability and behavioral constraints, highlighting the need to rethink knowledge-based approaches to entrepreneurial finance.

title: Visual Recovery
affiliations: City University of Hong Kong and City University of Hong Kong

detail.title: Visual Recovery
detail.abstract:
This paper introduces visual recovery, an empirical approach that treats the implied volatility surface as the object of interest rather than reducing it to a few option characteristics. We map the full maturity-delta geometry of individual stock and S&P 500 implied volatility surfaces into a predictive distribution of future stock returns. Each surface is observed on a 10 × 18 grid. A channel-separate Vision Transformer preserves this grid, combines stock-level and aggregate option-market information, and outputs a 100-bin forecast of the next 21-trading-day stock return. From the fitted distribution we extract the probability of a-20% monthly crash, predicted variance, and predicted mean return. 
The surface contains its strongest information about downside risk and variance. The crash probability forecasts realized crashes with a panel coefficient of 0.97 (𝑡 = 16.38) and remains informative against the Martin-Shi lower bound. Predicted variance forecasts realized variance with a coefficient of 1.28 (𝑡 = 23.53), falling to 0.77 (𝑡 = 6.42) with the full set of controls. Expected-return information is also present: sorting on predicted mean returns generates an equal-weighted decile spread of 1.76% per month (𝑡 = 4.21). Surface ablations show that level carries much of the mean-return signal, while residual smile and term-structure shape continue to predict crash risk and variance. The evidence indicates that the full visual geometry of option prices contains economically meaningful distributional information beyond standard scalar summaries.

title: Pay Now, Regret Later? When Disclosure Fails to Deter: Choice Persistence and Post-Purchase Satisfaction in Installment Payments
affiliations: Bank of Israel

detail.title: Pay Now, Regret Later? When Disclosure Fails to Deter: Choice Persistence and Post-Purchase Satisfaction in Installment Payments

declarations.declarationOfInterest: non
declarations.ethicsApproval: The research has ethic approval and has been pre- registered

detail.abstract: Risk disclosures are widely used in credit markets, yet their effectiveness remains unclear. We study this where all spending is already deferred, so installment splitting adds a further layer of deferral on everyday purchases. In a preregistered experiment (N = 1,000), a risk prompt does not significantly reduce take-up. Yet it leaves a welfare trace: installment users told that a prompt had once been required and was now removed report lower satisfaction, consistent with disclosure-induced regret. Those most likely to split are already financially stretched-precisely the group the prompt fails to reach. Effective protection may require tailoring disclosure to borrower characteristics.

title: Cluster-Respecting Shrinkage for Streaming Covariance Estimation: A Clustering-Free Block Target from Hadamard Squares of the Correlation Matrix

detail.title: Cluster-Respecting Shrinkage for Streaming Covariance Estimation: A Clustering-Free Block Target from Hadamard Squares of the Correlation Matrix
detail.abstract: Streaming covariance estimators for large panels of daily financial returns require shrinkage as the number of assets approaches the effective sample size, and the standard streamingcompatible target-the equicorrelation matrix-imposes a single uniform factor on a crosssection that in reality carries block (cluster) structure. Explicit clustering would recover that structure but breaks the streaming contract. We show that no clustering is needed: the Hadamard square of the estimator's own correlation matrix is a cluster-respecting shrinkage target by construction-positive semi-definite by the Schur product theorem, unit-diagonal for free, and O(n 2)-whose entries retain within-cluster structure while suppressing noise correlations quadratically. Because the naive version underweights the market direction when shrinkage is light, we let the target morph with the shrinkage intensity itself, governed by a parameter-free level-matching rule. The construction adds no tuned parameters, preserves the guarantees of the base estimator, and reduces exactly to the published estimator whenever shrinkage is inactive. On a 30-year S&P 500 panel the morphing target leaves the moderate-concentration benchmark unchanged and delivers large, highly significant held-out gains where shrinkage is load-bearing-up to 25 NLL at n=300. All results are reproducible with the open-source reference implementation.

title: The Impact of Ambient Air Pollution on Outcomes of Single Vitrified-Warmed Blastocyst Transfer
affiliations: Ojinmed IVF Centre, Mongolian National University of Medical Sciences, Ojinmed IVF Centre, Ojinmed IVF Centre, Ojinmed IVF Centre, Ojinmed IVF Centre, Ojinmed IVF Centre, Ojinmed IVF Centre, Ojinmed IVF Centre, Harvard University - Liver Center, Ojinmed IVF Centre, Ojinmed IVF Centre, Ojinmed IVF Centre, Ojinmed IVF Centre and Ojinmed IVF Centre

detail.title: The Impact of Ambient Air Pollution on Outcomes of Single Vitrified-Warmed Blastocyst Transfer

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: The study protocol received approval from the Ojinmed IVF Centre Institutional Ethics Committee (reference: EA2024111201). Written informed consent for the use of anonymised clinical data in retrospective research was obtained from all participants.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract:
Background: Ambient air pollution is associated with impaired reproductive and adverse perinatal outcomes, yet evidence from extreme-exposure settings across the assisted reproductive technology (ART) continuum is limited. Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, records particulate matter far exceeding WHO thresholds. We investigated associations between six criteria air pollutants and ART outcomes.

Methods: This retrospective cohort study included 5,021 SVBT cycles from 2,978 patients at the Ojinmed IVF Centre, Ulaanbaatar (May 2015–August 2025). Monthly SO2, NO2, CO, PM10, PM2·5, and O3 from 14 stations were assigned across seven pre-specified exposure windows. Multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aOR, 95% CI) for clinical pregnancy, live birth, pregnancy loss, preterm birth, and low birth weight.

Findings: PM2·5 in the embryo-transfer month was associated with decreased clinical pregnancy (linear trend p-value=0·004), and exposure 90 days before oocyte pick-up with decreased live birth (linear trend p-value=0·03). PM10 within 30 days after blastocyst transfer was associated with a 43% reduction in live birth (highest vs lowest quartile: aOR 0·57, 95% CI 0·34–0·94; linear trend p-value=0·02), and third-trimester exposure with low birth weight (linear trend p-value=0·049). Higher third-trimester O3 was associated with an 81% increase in preterm birth (aOR 1·81, 95% CI 1·01–3·22; linear trend p-value=0·02); all p-values denote the linear trend across quartiles.

Interpretation: Ambient pollutant exposure was associated with outcome-specific perinatal harm across distinct phases of IVF and pregnancy in an extreme-pollution setting. These findings support counselling couples preparing for and undergoing ART to reduce exposure—through indoor air filtration, personal protection, and avoiding peak-pollution periods—before conception and throughout pregnancy, and reinforce the need for urgent air-quality improvement.

title: Beyond Implied Probability: Risk-Adjusted Implied Probability and Risk-Scores for Merger Arbitrage

detail.title: Beyond Implied Probability: Risk-Adjusted Implied Probability and Risk-Scores for Merger Arbitrage

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No outside interest.

detail.abstract: This paper seeks to outline a risk-score heuristic which investors can deploy quickly to assess the varying risk profiles of binary-event risk arbitrage trades in a more consistent manner. In instances where constant risk exposure is mandated but positive EV trades are infrequent, utilising a risk-score aids investors in identifying the trades that impose the least risk in fulfilling their mandate. A more negative risk-score indicates a higher risk trade, reflecting the potential gain or loss from pursuing a trade and associated market implied probabilities of each outcome, scaled to an investor’s risk aversion. This is accompanied by the explanation of risk-adjusted implied probability, which serves as another heuristic to assess the requisite level of conviction an investor must have for current market pricing to be appealing, given their baseline appetite for risk.

title: The Pyramidal Effect

detail.title: The Pyramidal Effect

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract:
Abstract

Why do some well-resourced development interventions collapse despite ample capital, while comparatively leaner, sequenced efforts succeed? Why do some political candidates spend years seeking the highest office in the land when they should invest in building ground up? This working paper develops the Pyramidal Effect - also termed Base-Apex Sequencing Theory (BAST) - a unified formal theory holding that apex-level outcomes are structurally bounded by, and lag, accumulated base capacity, in the same way a pyramid's apex is bounded by, and structurally dependent on, its base. The theory is stated as six axioms and formalized through three complementary mathematical models: a geometric stability condition adapted from structural mechanics, a lagged and concave capability-accumulation dynamic in the spirit of economic complexity theory, and a bottleneck constraint following Liebig's Law of the Minimum and Goldratt's Theory of Constraints. These are unified into a single diagnostic statistic: the stability ratio Σ(t), and a critical-mass threshold Bᴄ, enabling ex-ante policy diagnosis rather than only ex-post explanation. We test the framework across four cases spanning economics and electoral politics: Nigeria's Anchor Borrowers' Programme (Σ between 2 and 8; self-sufficiency stalled near 57–70 percent after a decade), Indonesia's BIMAS rice intensification programme (Σ falling from 1.9 in 1968 to approximately 1.0 by 1984–85, corroborated out-of-sample by a 1986 pest-outbreak the model independently flags), Sri Lanka's Mattala Rajapaksa International Airport (Σ from 29 to 651, the starkest case), and prior experience among United States Senators, 1953–2023 (which reveals two stacked apexes: winning and governing; each requiring a domain-specific extension). The three economic cases confirm the theory's core predictions; the political case extends it, via a stock-flow reconciliation generating a falsifiable prediction for the 2030s and two new formal extensions (a synthetic base substitute and a proximity-weighted base index). A companion spreadsheet reproducing every Σ(t) calculation is available from the author. The paper closes with the “Pyramidal Check”, a practical five-question ex-ante audit for development-finance design, infrastructure appraisal, and political party recruitment. AI disclosure: generative AI tools were used in preparation under the author's direction; the author takes full responsibility for all content.

title: New Constitutionalism and Property
affiliations: National Law School of India University

detail.title: New Constitutionalism and Property
detail.abstract:
This paper examines the moral foundations of liberal constitutional protections of property by moving beyond standard justifications based on natural rights and utility. It argues that property regimesespecially those governing land-are shaped by competing moral virtues embedded in two distinct forces: constituent forces, rooted in democratic will and social claims, and constitutive forces, embedded in legal, institutional, and market-oriented frameworks. While constituent forces emphasize fairness, reciprocity, and social responsibility, constitutive forces prioritize stability, predictability, and the protection of entitlements. Under conditions of new constitutionalism, the latter increasingly dominate, reorienting property regimes toward the imperatives of global capital. 

Legal and institutional arrangements are no longer neutral mediators but instruments that entrench neoliberal economic policies through transnational regimes such as trade agreements and investment protections. This produces a structural conditioning of states, compelling them to prioritize capital accumulation while marginalizing livelihood concerns. The paper demonstrates how this transformation reshapes land relations. First, it shows how land use is increasingly driven by investment logics, leading to dispossession and conflict in agrarian contexts, particularly in the Global South. Second, it analyzes how global trade regimes generate "deterritorialized" forms of value-such as virtual water and financial instruments-that weaken the coherence of constituent claims. Third, it examines how land, once detached from identity and community, is reconstituted as an abstract asset, a process legitimized through law and institutional discourse.

title: Spillover Impacts of Long-lasting Insecticidal Nets on Childhood Malaria Acrossendemic African Countries: An Analysis of Demographic Health Survey Data
affiliations: Karolinska Institutet, Keio University - Department of Health Policy and Management, Mount Kenya University, Nagasaki University, Karolinska Institutet and National Institute of Infectious Diseases - Center for Surveillance, Immunization, and Epidemiologic Research

detail.title: Spillover Impacts of Long-lasting Insecticidal Nets on Childhood Malaria Acrossendemic African Countries: An Analysis of Demographic Health Survey Data

declarations.declarationOfInterest: We declare no competing interests.
declarations.funderStatement: Y.K.K. was supported by a Research Fellowship for Young Scientists from the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS) (JP26KJ0187), JSPS KAKENHI (JP25K20618), and Karolinska Institutet (KI) Research Grants (2024-02402). DY was supported by JSPS KAKENHI (JP26K02664)

detail.abstract:
Background: Long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs) reduce malaria risk through direct protection of users and potential community-level protection that may extend to non-users. The magnitude of these spillover impacts across African settings remains poorly characterised. 

Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of the latest Demographic and Health Survey (DHS) and Malaria Indicator Survey (MIS) data from malaria-endemic countries in Africa. Using the g-formula under a partial interference framework, we estimated spillover impacts of increasing community LLIN coverage from 50% to 70% on childhood malaria prevalence. The primary pooled analysis included 19 countries and was restricted to clusters with observed LLIN coverage of at least 50%. 

Findings: The pooled overall spillover estimate was protective but did not reach statistical significance (overall risk ratio [RR] 0·925, 95% CI 0·840–1·019; users 0·946, 0·853–1·049; non-users 0·934, 0·824–1·059). In a sensitivity analysis restricted to 13 countries with sufficient high-coverage clusters, spillover impacts were stronger and statistically significant (overall RR 0·885, 0·797–0·983; non-users RR 0·839, 0·761–0·926). Significant protection was also observed among socioeconomically vulnerable populations and in high-transmission settings. 

Interpretation: Community LLIN coverage showed a consistent protective association with childhood malaria prevalence. These findings support efforts to achieve high LLIN coverage and highlight the importance of accounting for spillover benefits in programme evaluation.

title: The "Vulnerable Buffer-city" Paradigm: Structural Asymmetry, Demographic Absorbency, and Socio-ecological Strains in Peri-Urban Spaces

detail.title: The "Vulnerable Buffer-city" Paradigm: Structural Asymmetry, Demographic Absorbency, and Socio-ecological Strains in Peri-Urban Spaces
detail.abstract: Vulnerability research has produced two dominant explanatory traditions: a compositional tradition, which locates vulnerability in the internal characteristics of a place (its housing stock, its demographic profile, its exposure to hazard), and a systemic tradition, which locates it in a settlement's position within a national or global economic hierarchy. These two traditions rarely meet at the scale that matters most for a growing class of Global South settlements: cities that sit in the immediate functional shadow of a national metropolitan core, absorbing its demographic overspill while remaining administratively and fiscally subordinate to it. This article proposes the Vulnerable Buffer City (VBC) model to fill that gap. A buffer city is defined as a settlement occupying a specific structural positionfunctional absorption of a core city's population pressure, combined with resource and planning-authority asymmetry relative to that core-which generates a distinct form of positional vulnerability, irreducible to the compositional vulnerability captured by existing place-based indices. The article situates this claim against primate-city theory, urban-bias theory, and the hazards-of-place and socio-environmental fragmentation literatures, derives five testable propositions, and proposes a Buffer Vulnerability Index combining positional and compositional indicators, to be applied to Témara using Morocco's 2024 General Population and Housing Census (RGPH) and regional planning and budgetary data.

title: SmartFSQCA: A Free, Browser-Based Platform for Fuzzy-Set Qualitative Comparative Analysis

detail.title: SmartFSQCA: A Free, Browser-Based Platform for Fuzzy-Set Qualitative Comparative Analysis

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable; this study describes a software tool and involves no human participants or personal data.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA) has become a mainstream method across management, human resource management, information systems, political science, education and health, because it models the causal complexity-conjunction, equifinality and asymmetry-that correlational methods obscure. Yet the software that supports it remains fragmented and, for many researchers, difficult to access: the reference programs are desktop applications or R packages that require installation and, in the R case, programming skill, while calibration, the truth table, the three solutions, and the visual and robustness diagnostics needed for credible reporting are spread across separate tools and manual steps. This paper introduces SmartFSQCA, a free, single-page web application that runs a complete fsQCA workflow entirely in the user's browser, so that data never leave the machine. From an uploaded spreadsheet it detects repeated Likert items and helps group them into constructs; calibrates raw variables into fuzzy or crisp setmembership scores by the direct (logistic) method, a crisp threshold, or pass-through, with a calibrationquality diagnostic; computes the analysis of necessary conditions with consistency, coverage and the Relevance of Necessity; constructs the truth table under user-set frequency, consistency and PRI thresholds, flags contradictory rows, and minimises it by the Quine-McCluskey algorithm to produce the complex, parsimonious and intermediate solutions with core/peripheral condition marking; and reports raw and unique coverage, solution consistency and coverage, XY sufficiency plots, typicality/deviance classification, bootstrap confidence intervals, a threshold-robustness grid, Venn overlap of paths, and analysis of the negated outcome for asymmetry. An optional, key-free AI layer drafts a publication-ready interpretation, proposes theoretical names for configurations, and appraises robustness, always constrained to the computed numbers. Every set-theoretic measure and the Boolean minimiser were validated against an independent implementation of the published formulae and against data with a known generating recipe, with exact agreement. SmartFSQCA lowers the barrier to rigorous, reproducible, privacy-preserving fsQCA and is offered with a citable version and an open licence.

title: Efficacy and Outcomes of Clinical Trials in Anesthesiology With Nonstatistically Significant Results: A Cross-Sectional Study
affiliations: Universidad Nacional de Colombia, CES University and CES University

detail.title: Efficacy and Outcomes of Clinical Trials in Anesthesiology With Nonstatistically Significant Results: A Cross-Sectional Study

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No Interests to disclose.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received.

detail.abstract:
Introduction: Randomized clinical trials (RCTs) are the gold standard for evaluating healthcare interventions. However, the traditional interpretation based on a P value < .05 has been increasingly questioned, particularly when study findings do not reach statistical significance. Such results may still conceal clinically meaningful effects. The likelihood ratio (LR) has been proposed as an alternative statistical measure because it quantifies the extent to which the observed data support the null or the alternative hypothesis.

Objective: To evaluate whether the likelihood ratio (LR) provides additional evidence beyond the P value for interpreting nonstatistically significant primary outcomes in randomized clinical trials in anesthesiology.

Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional study of randomized clinical trials published through December 2024 in Q1 and Q2 anesthesiology journals. Trials with nonstatistically significant primary outcomes (P > .05) and sufficient data to calculate the LR were included. We evaluated the distribution of LR values, their association with P values, and their impact on posttest probabilities across different pretest probability scenarios.

Results: Of 642 randomized clinical trials initially identified, 117 met the inclusion criteria. Overall, 26.5% had an LR less than 1, indicating evidence favoring the alternative hypothesis, whereas 35.1% had an LR of 100 or greater, indicating strong evidence favoring the null hypothesis. Across pretest probability scenarios of 10%, 25%, and 50%, an LR of 100 or greater increased the posttest probability of the null hypothesis to more than 96%. The correlation between the LR and the P value was weak (Spearman ρ = 0.076), suggesting that the two measures provide complementary rather than redundant information.

Conclusions: The likelihood ratio provides a more nuanced interpretation of nonstatistically significant findings in randomized clinical trials in anesthesiology. By complementing the P value, the LR may improve the interpretation of clinical trial results and support more informed decision-making in clinical research.

title: Policy Uncertainty and Asset Volatility: A Systematic Review of GARCH-Family Approaches (2015-2026)

detail.title: Policy Uncertainty and Asset Volatility: A Systematic Review of GARCH-Family Approaches (2015-2026)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: The past decade has witnessed a proliferation of text-based and news-derived uncertainty indices-economic policy uncertainty (EPU), geopolitical risk (GPR), climate policy uncertainty (CPU), and equity market volatility (EMV) trackers-that are now routinely deployed as exogenous drivers of conditional variance in empirical finance. Despite this proliferation, no systematic taxonomy exists of how these indices are structurally embedded into GARCH-family volatility models, leaving researchers, editors, and practitioners without a shared vocabulary for comparing competing specifications. This paper addresses that gap through a PRISMA-based systematic review of the peer-reviewed literature linking uncertainty indices to GARCH-family models across equity, foreign exchange, commodity, energy, carbon, cryptocurrency, and green-asset markets published between 2015 and 2026. Screening Web of Science and Scopus records against explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria yields a final analytic sample drawn from the empirical literature, from which we derive a three-paradigm taxonomy: Paradigm A, high-frequency direct embedding, in which an uncertainty proxy enters linearly into the conditional variance equation (GARCH-X); Paradigm B, mixedfrequency decomposition, in which the GARCH-MIDAS framework separates short-run and 2 long-run volatility components and admits low-frequency macro and policy variables without temporal aggregation loss; and Paradigm C, regime-dependent transmission, in which Markov-switching GARCH models allow the strength and even the sign of uncertainty transmission to vary across latent volatility regimes. The review finds that each paradigm occupies a distinct niche: Paradigm A is best suited to short-horizon shock identification, Paradigm B dominates long-horizon forecasting and energy/carbon market applications, and Paradigm C is best suited to tail-risk and crisis-period analysis. The findings carry direct implications for volatility forecasting practice in energy and environmental economics, for regulatory value-at-risk frameworks, and for the design of next-generation multilingual and multi-uncertainty GARCH specifications.

title:
The Counterfeit Toggle: 
Deceptive Health Feature Design as Disability Discrimination under ADA Title III and Section 5 of the FTC Act

detail.title:
The Counterfeit Toggle: 
Deceptive Health Feature Design as Disability Discrimination under ADA Title III and Section 5 of the FTC Act
detail.abstract:
Consumer artificial intelligence platforms now ship dedicated, gated "health" features whose name, branding, and gating toggle signal a special, protected clinical environment. The signal is false. The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act is defined by the actor holding the data rather than by its sensitivity, so it cannot attach to a relationship between a company and an individual consumer at all: an individual is not a covered entity, and no business associate agreement is possible. What the consumer receives is a revocable privacy policy commitment, not the enforceable regime the same company gives its enterprise customers.
 
This article argues that the resulting design is a single fact pattern reachable through two doctrines at once: the reasonable modification and equal access obligations of Title III of the Americans with Disabilities Act, and the unfair and deceptive practices prohibition of Section 5 of the Federal Trade Commission Act. The disability injury is not incidental; the false reassurance operates through the very trait that defines anxiety and paranoia disabilities, and the resulting clinical decompensation is disability specific and severe. Meaningful access, not a freestanding disparate impact rule, carries the discrimination claim; the eggshell skull rule, already extended to psychological fragility, answers the objection that a resilient user would not have been harmed; the defendant's own illegality bounds an otherwise unbounded accommodation duty; and the fundamental alteration and undue burden defenses fail three ways. 

The contributions are three: distinguishing a HIPAA compliant product from a product to which HIPAA applies, and naming the deception trust laundering; locating the disability wrong in meaningful access under Title III rather than an overstated disparate impact rule, measured through the eggshell skull rule; and identifying the antecedent illegality that converts an idiosyncratic reliance into a cognizable harm, with an injunctive menu that closes the burden defense. The argument turns on one contested premise, that Title III reaches a purely digital service, defended in a companion work.

title: ENSO-Driven Correlation Dynamics in Agricultural and Energy Markets: A DCC-MIDAS Approach

detail.title: ENSO-Driven Correlation Dynamics in Agricultural and Energy Markets: A DCC-MIDAS Approach

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding was received for this research.

keywords: asymmetric climate risk JEL Classification: G13

detail.abstract: This paper embeds the Oceanic Niño Index (ONI) into a two-stage DCC-MIDAS model to examine how ENSO drives long-run correlation between soybean futures and WTI crude oil over September 2000 to June 2026 (N = 6,465 daily observations). The estimated long-run ENSO slope is negative and significant (θρ =-0.145, p<0.05), indicating that El Niño episodes reduce soybean-oil correlation while La Niña episodes raise it. An asymmetric decomposition confirms this pattern is driven entirely by La Niña (θ-= +0.284, p<0.05), with El Niño having no significant effect (θ+ =-0.031); a Wald test rejects symmetry at the 1% level (χ²(1) = 7.459, p = 0.006). The mechanism operates through opposing variance channels: ENSO lowers soybean long-run variance (θsoybean =-0.541) but raises oil long-run variance (θoil = +0.421), mechanically decoupling the two markets under El Niño. Estimated MIDAS effective lags reveal that correlation integrates climate information (2.8 months) far more rapidly than individual market volatilities (11.2 months for soybean, 15.2 months for oil). These findings have direct implications for commodity portfolio diversification and dynamic hedging strategies conditioned on ENSO forecasts.

title: Rent without Labour: AI Infrastructure and the Labour Test of Gulf Diversification

detail.title: Rent without Labour: AI Infrastructure and the Labour Test of Gulf Diversification

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required because the paper uses only publicly available documents and does not involve human participants, interviews, or personal data.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Gulf states present their AI investments as economic diversification, and the scale of those investments is not in question. This paper asks a prior question: whether the AI transition changes the relation that defines a rentier state-the separation between state income and citizen labour. It separates the AI economy into three layers (compute infrastructure, AI operations, productive use) and argues that the transition risks reproducing the rentier gap if it is measured by installed capacity rather than by national labour absorbed into productive use. Applying this labour test to Saudi Arabia and the UAE shows a consistent asymmetry in the public record: capacity is measured in detail, workforce composition rarely, and labour absorption into sectoral AI work barely at all. The fragments that are visible point toward an internationalised operating layer and partly outsourced implementation signals. The scarcity of absorption data is read not only as a research limitation, but as evidence of what current diversification metrics measure and what they leave out.

title: Public Moral Agreement can Overstate Shared Values: Intrinsic and Strategic Conformity
affiliations: University of Konstanz - Faculty of Economics and Statistics, University of Konstanz - Faculty of Economics and Statistics,  and

detail.title: Public Moral Agreement can Overstate Shared Values: Intrinsic and Strategic Conformity
detail.abstract: When members of a group agree publicly on controversial moral and political questions, this is widely taken as evidence of genuine consensus. However, publicly expressed judgments may not faithfully reflect private views, but arise from three sources: shared values, intrinsic conformity with prevailing views, and strategic conformity driven by public evaluation. To separate these mechanisms, we introduce a new moral-trilemma paradigm and adapt a transitivity-based experimental approach that allows us to infer participants' private judgments before social exposure and compare them with judgments made after observing majority views, with or without peer reward or punishment. Across twelve moral domains, participants shift toward majority views even when responses remain private, demonstrating intrinsic conformity. When judgments are evaluated and can elicit peer reward or punishment, conformity nearly doubles. Consequently, a substantial share of visible agreement reflects strategic preference falsification rather than genuine convergence. Observed consensus thus often overstates underlying agreement within groups, which may also amplify perceived polarization.

title: Institutional Design and Legal Authority in Post-Crisis Financial Regulation: A Comparative Study of the United States, United Kingdom, and India (2008-2019)
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Institutional Design and Legal Authority in Post-Crisis Financial Regulation: A Comparative Study of the United States, United Kingdom, and India (2008-2019)

detail.abstract: The 2008 financial crisis exposed regulatory failures across advanced and emerging economies around the globe. This paper presents a comparative analysis of responses to the unique economic conditions created by the 2008 global financial crisis across the United States, United Kingdom and India between 2007 and 2019. It argues that the effectiveness of these regulatory measures depended more on whether the changes introduced under these regulatory efforts were entrenched in a resilient legal framework rather than on the scale of implementation through government intervention. The United States was the fastest to respond, through the launch of the Troubled Asset Relief Program (TARP) and the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act; however, these initiatives were undermined by their political vulnerability, demonstrated by the subsequent partial rollback of the Dodd-Frank Act in 2018. The United Kingdom was the next to follow, with the abolition of the Financial Services Authority and the creation of a twin-peaks regulatory structure under the Financial Services Act 2012, followed by the isolation of retail banking under the Financial Services (Banking Reform) Act 2013, producing the most structurally enduring reform of the three jurisdictions. In contrast to the others, India experienced a delayed domestic banking crisis, which it addressed through the implementation of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code 2016, fundamentally altering insolvency law by shifting from an approach which allocated control to debtors to one which favored creditors. Furthermore, this paper analyzes the constitutional legitimacy of TARP through an examination of the compatibility between broad executive control over $700 billion in public funds and core rule-of-law principles. The paper concludes that financial regulation is ultimately a legal design problem, in which the durability of economic interventions is determined over the long term by the legal architecture in which they are embedded.

title: Pricing the Physical Gray Rhino: Extreme Climate Shocks and Long-Run Volatility Dynamics in Soft Commodities
affiliations: and

detail.title: Pricing the Physical Gray Rhino: Extreme Climate Shocks and Long-Run Volatility Dynamics in Soft Commodities

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no competing interests.

detail.abstract: Against the backdrop of intensifying global climate variability, extreme weather events are increasingly inflicting physical disruptions on agricultural supply chains; yet traditional financial asset pricing models predominantly neglect these long-term physical constraints. This paper investigates the transmission mechanism of physical climate risks into financial markets by employing a GJR-GARCH-MIDAS (Mixed Data Sampling) framework, utilising daily returns of soft commodity futures-cocoa and coffee-alongside the monthly Oceanic Niño Index (ONI) released by NOAA, over the period January 2000 to June 2026. Empirical results reveal that low-frequency ENSO climate anomalies significantly and positively elevate the long-run secular volatility of tree-based soft commodity futures (θ = 0.233, p < 0.01 for cocoa; θ = 0.105, p < 0.10 for coffee), while exerting no statistically significant effect on annual crop futures such as soybeans (θ =-0.417, p < 0.01 in the opposite direction). This striking heterogeneity is rooted in the divergent biological supply elasticities between perennial tree crops and short-cycle annual crops. Our findings offer a robust empirical foundation for correcting long-run volatility estimates in derivative pricing, and provide forward-looking risk management insights for multinational food corporations and central banks navigating agricultural inflation.

reference: Theoretical Inquiries (forthcoming); Stanford Law Review, Forthcoming
title: Quantum Bureaucracies
affiliations: University of Washington - School of Law

detail.title: Quantum Bureaucracies
detail.abstract:
This essay amounts to a thought experiment: what if anticipated developments in computing — quantum simulation, machine learning, or some combination — eventually allow governments to model the effects of policy interventions on human behavior with exquisite precision? 

Assuming away, contrary to the weight of present evidence, the inaccuracy and bias that plague algorithmic governance today. A century of public policy scholarship, from Hayek and Lindblom to Diver and Collingridge, identifies poor information as among the greatest obstacles to effective policy-making. The prospect of achieving societal goals while avoiding unintended consequences would seem, on these assumptions, an unalloyed good. Yet the arrival of the "quantum bureaucracies" would also place within reach certain contested projects of contemporary legal theory, from personalized law and micro-directives, to perfect enforcement and impossibility structures. Familiar objections to these projects, sounding in privacy, legibility, ossification, and autonomy, would be correspondingly magnified.

Drawing on science fiction, philosophy, and legal scholarship, the essay argues for a deeper problem still. Even a restrained and well-intentioned quantum bureaucracy may amount to a tacit endorsement of determinism by the state. Law and liberal democracy rest on conceptions of free will, moral deliberation, and room for play. A decisive swing of the epistemic pendulum back toward determinism would represent a sea change in governance and perhaps in our understanding of what it is to be human. Faced with this prospect, a quantum bureaucracy must choose between concealing its capabilities, at the cost of transparency, and exercising them openly, at the cost of unsettling the premises on which legal legitimacy depends. Because these questions turn on the government's worldview, and because the public deserves a say in that worldview, society should take an active and existential interest in impeccable prediction technology now, while its trajectory remains open.

title: An Experimental Study of Coarse Correlated Equilibrium for Delegation to Connected Autonomous Systems
affiliations: and Purdue University - Krannert School of Management

detail.title: An Experimental Study of Coarse Correlated Equilibrium for Delegation to Connected Autonomous Systems

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None to declare.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Approval from the Purdue IRB.
declarations.funderStatement: National Science Foundation (award #2333487)

detail.abstract: In a coarse correlated equilibrium, individuals have an incentive to delegate to a device that selects outcomes according to a known probability distribution. This delegation is made before the specific outcome is selected, analogous to a commitment to allow an autonomous vehicle to take actions on the human driver's behalf. This experiment studies individuals' willingness to delegate to such correlating devices across a range of payoff and correlating device treatments. These include games with multiple Pareto-rankable pure strategy equilibria that differ in their associated risk, as well as games without a pure strategy equilibrium in which a correlating device can raise expected payoffs relative to the unique mixed strategy equilibrium. We find that subjects seldom delegate their decision-making authority, and the rate of committing to the device decreases over time. Average earnings are significantly higher when both parties commit to it than in cases without a device. However, in games we study with multiple pure strategy Nash equilibria, one-sided commitment yields substantially lower average earnings.

title: Exchange Rate Regimes and Green Capital Inflows: Evidence from Staggered Regime Transitions in Developing Countries
affiliations: and Mohammed V University of Rabat

detail.title: Exchange Rate Regimes and Green Capital Inflows: Evidence from Staggered Regime Transitions in Developing Countries
detail.abstract: Integrating into the green global production network requires developing countries to attract substantial green capital inflows, a process heavily dependent on domestic exchange rate policies. We analyze how transitioning to a floating regime affects international renewable energy investments using a staggered difference-indifferences approach for causal inference. Our findings reveal that transitioning to a floating exchange rate regime can significantly boost international renewable energy investments. These benefits are highly conditional to credible transitions sustained for at least three years, while transient policy shifts fail to attract investments and instead induce green capital flight. Ultimately, our findings underscore that credible and durable exchange rate flexibility can serve as a mechanism for scaling up green capital inflow.

title: Data-Centre Power Demand and Southeast Asia's Digital-Infrastructure FDI

detail.title: Data-Centre Power Demand and Southeast Asia's Digital-Infrastructure FDI
detail.abstract: We document that data-centre investment in Southeast Asia has become an electricity allocation problem before it is a capital allocation problem, and we assemble the evidence in three layers: a thirty-project ledger of announced investments worth roughly USD 57 billion in greenfield pledges plus the USD 16 billion AirTrunk platform acquisition; a register of thirty policy instruments across six countries that ration, reprice or green-condition data-centre power; and a comparative set of energy-system parameters (tariffs, connection times, grid carbon intensity) that govern where the capital can actually land. Three findings organise the paper. First, projected demand growth is steeper in this region than almost anywhere else: the IEA expects global data-centre electricity to roughly double to about 945 TWh by 2030, while Ember's country series has Malaysia growing eight-fold from 8.5 TWh to 68 TWh, by which point data centres would take close to a third of Peninsular Malaysia's electricity. Second, the binding constraint has already shifted from capital to infrastructure: as of December 2024, data-centre operators in Malaysia had contracted 5.9 GW of electricity supply while drawing only 405 MW, Johor was rejecting roughly 30% of applications on power and water grounds, and Singapore allocates megawatts administratively through competitive calls rather than through a connection queue at all. Third, the region's hosts have converged, by visibly different routes, on the same instrument: conditional access to electricity has replaced tax incentives as the operative screen on digital-infrastructure FDI. We argue this makes the megawatt, not the dollar, the natural unit of account for this investment wave, and we show what that implies for how announced figures should be read against balance-of-payments data.

title: Professionalism as Stewardship
affiliations: Australian Council of Professions

detail.title: Professionalism as Stewardship

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I have funded the work myself
declarations.ethicsApproval: n/a
declarations.funderStatement: I have funded the work myself

detail.abstract:
This paper advances a new argument in the evolving discussion of professionalism: that experienced professionals have a moral duty of stewardship. Building on earlier work that established the continuing relevance of professionalism and its growing importance in a complex and uncertain world, the paper argues that professionalism does not sustain itself automatically. Rather, it survives only when established practitioners consciously transmit professional judgement, ethical standards, and professional identity to those who follow.

Drawing on the sociological tradition of professionalism, particularly the concept of professions as custodians of specialised expertise exercised in the service of society, the paper demonstrates that professionalism is fundamentally a social inheritance. While technical knowledge can be taught formally, professional judgement is largely acquired through observation, mentorship, reflection, and guided experience. The paper identifies five stewardship obligations for experienced professionals: making tacit judgement visible, modelling professional conduct, explaining ethical reasoning, creating psychologically safe learning environments, and encouraging reflective practice.

Using legal practice and nursing as contrasting case studies, the paper shows that stewardship is a universal professional responsibility regardless of sector or institutional context. The argument is made more urgent by contemporary pressures, including artificial intelligence, remote work, declining institutional trust, and the earlier assumption of responsibility by younger professionals. The paper concludes that professionalism endures only when individuals and institutions deliberately cultivate and transmit the standards, values, and judgment upon which professional legitimacy depends.

title: Anatomy of a Shadow Ledger: Statutory Bypass and Legacy Unit Economics A Forensic Audit of the Ratanpol Cloth Market

detail.title: Anatomy of a Shadow Ledger: Statutory Bypass and Legacy Unit Economics A Forensic Audit of the Ratanpol Cloth Market

declarations.ethicsApproval: All primary research participants were fully anonymized to protect confidentiality and legal privacy, and informed consent was obtained prior to all ethnographic interviews.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates the microeconomic resilience and statutory bypass mechanisms of legacy retail ecosystems within emerging, rapidly formalizing economies. Focusing on the historic Ratanpol Cloth Market in Ahmedabad, India, this forensic audit examines how traditional merchants maintain structural competitive advantages over heavily capitalized corporate retail. Utilizing primary ethnographic fieldwork and secondary statutory analysis, the research isolates three core operational moats: the capitalization of zero-rent generational real estate, the utilization of informal Angadia micro-logistics, and the aggressive cost-engineering of "consensual replicas" that exploit intellectual property without triggering consumer fraud statutes. Furthermore, the study explores the macroeconomic friction generated by the Goods and Services Tax (GST) and the Unified Payments Interface (UPI). The findings demonstrate that while digitalization has forced consumer-facing transactions into formal compliance, wholesale supply chains have retreated into an unrecorded cash economy, mathematically shielded by the presumptive taxation loopholes of Section 44AD of the Income Tax Act. Ultimately, this paper argues that the traditional market is not an economic anachronism, but a highly optimized, hyper-rational ecosystem that systematically navigates and neutralizes top-down regulatory frameworks, exposing its participants to severe but rarely enforced criminal liabilities under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).

title: Specific Performance of Oral Agreements: Certainty, Consensus ad idem and the Burden of Proof under the Specific Relief Act, 1963
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Specific Performance of Oral Agreements: Certainty, Consensus ad idem and the Burden of Proof under the Specific Relief Act, 1963
detail.abstract: Indian law, alone among the major common-law systems, admits an oral agreement for the sale of immovable property to full contractual validity, having deliberately declined to enact any analogue of the Statute of Frauds 1677. This article examines how the Indian courts have answered the danger which that choice creates, namely the ease with which oral claims to valuable property may be fabricated, and defends a single thesis: that the rigorous law of proof developed by the Supreme Court, requiring the plaintiff who seeks specific performance of an oral agreement to plead and establish with exceptional certainty a concluded bargain and consensus ad idem upon every vital term, precisely as pleaded and not otherwise, is the functional equivalent of the formality statutes of the common-law world, and that this evidentiary rigour survives the Specific Relief (Amendment) Act, 2018 untouched, because that Act removed the discretion to refuse a proved contract, not the burden of proving one. The method is doctrinal: the leading authorities, from Kollipara Sriramulu and Ouseph Varghese through Mayawanti, Brij Mohan and Ganesh Shet to Kamal Kumar and the current position after the review in the Katta Sujatha Reddy litigation, are analysed in the courts' own words with paragraph pinpoints, alongside the English equitable inheritance through Fry and Pomeroy. The article concludes by distilling the doctrine into crisp propositions of immediate utility to the bench and the bar.

title: Two Audiences, One Screen: Reading Mustang (2015) Through Western and Turkish Receptions"

detail.title: Two Audiences, One Screen: Reading Mustang (2015) Through Western and Turkish Receptions"
detail.abstract: This paper examines the opposing Western and Turkish receptions of Deniz Gamze Ergüven's Mustang (2015) to argue that the film is both a genuine feminist exposure of patriarchal violence and a work shaped by an inherited Orientalist visual structure. Drawing on Edward Said's theory of Orientalism alongside close readings of the film's cinematography, production history, and critical reception, the paper shows how Western critics celebrated the film's aesthetic and political content. In contrast, Turkish critics questioned its authenticity, pointing to the sisters' urban accents, Western-coded gestures, and a camera gaze inherited from nineteenth-century Orientalist painting. Rather than resolving this contradiction in either direction, the paper argues that holding both readings together is the more rigorous critical position, revealing how institutional funding, festival certification, and market demand shape which version of a "true" story gets told, and whose resistance remains too local to be recognized.

title: Towards a Theory of Socio-ecological Urban Disarticulation: Rethinking Fragmented Growth in Dependent Intermediate Cities of the Global South

detail.title: Towards a Theory of Socio-ecological Urban Disarticulation: Rethinking Fragmented Growth in Dependent Intermediate Cities of the Global South
detail.abstract: The literature on Southern urbanization has produced powerful partial theories-the right to the city, urban political ecology, planetary urbanization, urban informality-yet none adequately accounts for a recurrent and increasingly consequential settlement type: the dependent intermediate city that absorbs metropolitan overspill without acquiring metropolitan capacity. This article proposes Socio-Ecological Urban Disarticulation (SEUD) as a dedicated theoretical framework for this condition. SEUD is defined as the structural decoupling of three co-constitutive registers of urban life-the spatial, the social, and the ecological-under conditions of rapid, externally-driven demographic growth and asynchronous institutional capacity. Unlike fragmentation theories, which describe spatial discontinuity, or metabolic-rift theories, which describe ecological extraction, SEUD specifies the interaction among all three registers as a self-reinforcing cycle rather than three parallel deficits. The article situates this proposition within existing critical urban theory, formalizes five testable propositions, and outlines an empirical strategy-built on Morocco's 2024 General Population and Housing Census (Recensement Général de la Population et de l'Habitat, RGPH) and GIS-based spatial indicators-for testing the framework against the city of Témara. The intention is not merely descriptive; it is to offer urban studies a portable analytical vocabulary for a settlement pattern that is widespread across the peripheries of Global South metropolitan regions but remains theoretically under-specified.

title: BNPL as an Early-Warning Indicator of Household Liquidity Stress Constructing and Testing a High-Frequency Composite Index

detail.title: BNPL as an Early-Warning Indicator of Household Liquidity Stress Constructing and Testing a High-Frequency Composite Index

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no financial, commercial, or personal conflicts of interest that could have influenced the research presented in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study uses publicly available data, publicly available company disclosures, and published survey results. It does not involve human participants, identifiable personal data, or animal subjects. Accordingly, institutional ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was independently conducted and supported by the author.

detail.abstract: Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) credit has grown from a niche checkout feature into a mainstream form of short-term consumer credit, yet it remains largely invisible to the data infrastructure that regulators and researchers use to monitor household financial health. This paper proposes and partially motivates a Household Liquidity Stress Index (HLSI) that incorporates BNPL activity and performance metrics-loan frequency, average balances, late-fee incidence, and charge-offs-alongside conventional indicators of household stress: credit-card utilization and delinquency, the personal saving rate, real wage growth, initial unemployment claims, and consumer sentiment. We describe a mixed-frequency, dynamic-factor approach to combining these series at weekly-to-monthly frequency, and we lay out an empirical strategy for testing whether BNPL-inclusive indices improve short-horizon (4-to 12-week) nowcasts of consumer-stress outcomes relative to benchmarks that exclude BNPL. Using data available through mid-2026, we document a motivating stylized fact: self-reported BNPL late payment has risen sharply even as realized delinquency and charge-off rates at major issuers have stayed flat or improved-a divergence consistent with BNPL soft-signal variables leading hard-default variables. We discuss data limitations, identification strategy, and policy relevance, and lay out the concrete next steps required to move from research design to full estimation.

title: Crises Reveal the Truth: Financial Depth, Openness, and Macroeconomic Stability

detail.title: Crises Reveal the Truth: Financial Depth, Openness, and Macroeconomic Stability

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author received no specific funding for this work
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study relies exclusively on secondary data obtained from publicly accessible sources, including the World Bank World Development Indicators (WDI) and the Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) database. As the analysis does not involve human participants, personal data, or direct interactions with individuals, institutional ethics approval and informed consent were not required.
declarations.funderStatement: NIL

detail.abstract: Why do trade openness, foreign investment, and financial depth support growth in some periods but fail during economic crises? This study examines the statedependent effects of trade openness, foreign direct investment (FDI), and domestic credit on U.S. output using cointegration analysis, ARDL estimation, Granger causality tests, and crisis-interacted local projections. The results suggest that domestic credit has the strongest long-run association with output, while trade and FDI exhibit weaker and more condition-dependent relationships. During crises, trade and FDI shocks become more contractionary, whereas the growthsupporting role of domestic credit weakens but remains comparatively more resilient. Overall, the findings show that the benefits of openness and financial development depend on macroeconomic conditions and institutional capacity. The policy implication is that trade and investment liberalization should be complemented by stronger financial intermediation and crisis-resilient institutions capable of sustaining economic activity when external conditions deteriorate.

title: Unlocking Tangible Benefits from Intangible Collaterals: Patent Pledgeability and Bond Pricing
affiliations: University of International Business and Economics, University of International Business and Economics (UIBE) - School of Banking and Finance,  and Xiamen University - Wang Yanan Institute for Studies in Economics (WISE)

detail.title: Unlocking Tangible Benefits from Intangible Collaterals: Patent Pledgeability and Bond Pricing
detail.abstract: Empirically gauging the pledgeability value of assets is among the key challenges in finance, especially for intangible assets. In this paper, we show that unlocking intangibles' pledgeability creates tangible pricing benefits for corporate debt financing. By exploiting unique quasiexogenous shocks in China which improves the practical use of patents as collateral without directly changing the technological/ legal contents and value of patents per se, we find a decline of 11.1 bps in corporate bond issuance spreads among firms headquartered in pilot cities. The effect is more pronounced for firms whose value is more closely tied to patents and other intangible assets, and in cities with stronger patent-related activity and intellectual-property enforcement. The evidence suggests that intangibles' collateral value, distinct from their productivity value, plays an independent and economically meaningful role in debt pricing.

title: Does Fintech Expansion Lead to Banking Deserts?
affiliations: Goethe University Frankfurt

detail.title: Does Fintech Expansion Lead to Banking Deserts?
detail.abstract: This paper examines whether fintech adoption contributes to the closure of physical bank branches. Using social connectedness to the most prominent fintech lender's headquarters and a shift-share instrument exploiting state-level fintech adoption trends, I show that rising fintech market shares lead to branch closures. These closures concentrate in metropolitan counties, where the marginal effect is 41% larger than in rural areas. Counties most at risk of becoming a banking deserts, whether by limited branch access, high poverty or minority shares, show smaller closure rates. Instead, closures reflect large banks' strategic network consolidation moderated by bank profitability and deposit market power.
