title: The Role of Judiciary in Advancing Environmental Governance and Justice
affiliations: PES University and PES University

detail.title: The Role of Judiciary in Advancing Environmental Governance and Justice

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No influence from anyone

detail.abstract:
Environmental degradation has appeared to be among the toughest problems of the current century, as climate change is growing direly faster, leading to the loss of the biosphere and ecological catastrophes, which demand urgent and unanimous response by legislation to avoid any further damage to the environment. This paper discusses how judicial activism is one of the tools that have played a critical role in the realization of environmental justice and sustainable development, not only in India, but also in the rest of the countries. In submission to the necessity of underlining the importance of judicial activism using PIL in the establishment of international obligations in the domestic legal system, as an effective activity is essential. 

The paper presents the history of environmental jurisprudence in India and how it has unfolded in recent decades, particularly the path that the Supreme Court of India has taken steps regarding the new concept of climate litigation after the world witnessed environmental degradation. These developments are illustrated through important judicial precedents from the 1980s onward. The paper further addresses how the Supreme Court has contributed to the energy transition process in the country through sustainable development and advancement of renewable energy sources, such as wind energy, solar energy and other clean energy, and has shed light on the rights to access a clean environment.

Judicial activism in India provides a viable climate governance in the global south. On this note, the writer proposes some viable suggestions that could help in achieving the judicial activism dream in India. It also includes more integrated actions between the judiciary and the executive arm with environmental laws and regulations.

title: Temperature and Real-World Low-Stakes Cognitive Performance: Evidence from the Driver's License Theory Exam
affiliations: , Capital University of Economics and Business, Capital University of Economics and Business, Tsinghua University and Tsinghua University

detail.title: Temperature and Real-World Low-Stakes Cognitive Performance: Evidence from the Driver's License Theory Exam
detail.abstract: This paper provides the first real-world evidence on the effects of temperature on low-stakes cognitive performance in a standardized testing setting. We study driver's license theory exam in China, a consequential but non-competitive licensing exam with extremely low difficulty and retake costs, clear incentives to pass, and objectively measured performance. We link administrative exam records to hourly weather and air pollution, and instrument local PM2.5 with pollution transported from upwind cities to address bias in the temperature estimates arising from endogenous pollution. We find that outdoor exam-time temperature has a non-negligible adverse effect on exam performance. A comprehensive comparison with existing studies shows that the magnitude of this effect lies between those documented for high-stakes exams and those estimated from survey-based low-stakes cognitive assessments. The adverse effects are stronger for the lower-stakes Subject 1, more difficult question types, cognitively disadvantaged candidates, and male candidates. We find little evidence of interday adaptation, but document within-day timing adjustments toward more moderate temperatures. Among retake-required candidates, heat has a larger effect on repeated attempts. Finally, we show that exam scores predict traffic violations nearly a decade later, especially alcohol-related driving violations, while they have little predictive power for more severe traffic crimes. Our results suggest that low-stakes cognitive outcomes are relevant to individual welfare and may also involve social externalities. Ignoring the effects of heat on everyday lower-stakes cognitive performance could substantially understate the social costs of climate change.

title: The Role of Exchange Rate Regimes in Driving Startup Ecosystem: Evidence from the Financial Infrastructure Channel
affiliations: and Mohammed V University of Rabat

detail.title: The Role of Exchange Rate Regimes in Driving Startup Ecosystem: Evidence from the Financial Infrastructure Channel
detail.abstract: Exchange rate regime choices introduce structural trade-offs between financial stability and innovation incentives that shape the startup ecosystem. Utilizing a panel of 40 emerging economies from 2010 to 2024, we overcome data sparsity by deploying non-parametric Machine Learning imputation before constructing customized indices for financial infrastructure, depth, and openness channels. We employ Double Machine Learning Local Projections (DML-LP) to execute a nonlinear causal inference strategy. To prevent traditional fixed effects from mechanically absorbing the treatment variance of sticky exchange rate regimes, we embed the Hybrid-Mundlak controls directly within the DML-LP nuisance equations. Our findings reveal that unexpected transitions toward floating regimes catalyze a creative destruction process that expands financial infrastructure, whereas peg defenses reinforce structural stagnation. Paradoxically, startup depth responds positively to both financial infrastructure expansions and contractions. These dynamics highlight systemic reductions in financial frictions and powerful technological leapfrogging effects. Ultimately, we demonstrate that financial infrastructure serves as the underlying transmission mechanism through which floating regime shifts enhance private capital absorption and mobilization within startup ecosystems.

title: Beyond the Goal: How Tactical Metrics and Betting Discourse Shape Modern Football
affiliations: Graduate School of Business

detail.title: Beyond the Goal: How Tactical Metrics and Betting Discourse Shape Modern Football
detail.abstract: This paper synthesizes the evolution of contemporary football through three critical lenses: the adoption of advanced predictive metrics, specifically Expected Goals (xG); the digital transformation of fan engagement; and the escalating tension between commercial gambling interests and sporting integrity. Drawing on a mixed-methods approach that integrates historical match-day performance data-sourced via Opta and API-Football-with longitudinal social media analysis spanning the 2020/21 season, the study demonstrates that xG provides a superior framework for tactical performance evaluation compared to traditional outcome-based measures. Furthermore, this research empirically maps the intersection of on-pitch performance and digital discourse. Quantitative analysis of social media engagement reveals a moderate negative correlation (r approx =-0.54) between team tactical efficiency and the density of betting-related content. This finding suggests that while high-performing teams generate discourse centered on tactical analysis, lower-performing clubs face a 'systemic crisis' characterized by disproportionate wagering speculation. The study concludes that the digital fan experience is increasingly stratified by performance-driven volatility, underscoring the urgent need for robust governance frameworks to mitigate the impact of gambling saturation on sporting integrity.

title: Scaling Sustainable Aviation Fuel: Cost-Effective Pathways and Regional Economic Impacts
affiliations: , Georgia Institute of Technology and Georgia  Institute  of  Technology

detail.title: Scaling Sustainable Aviation Fuel: Cost-Effective Pathways and Regional Economic Impacts

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: This research is funded by UPS Foundation.

detail.abstract: Scaling sustainable aviation fuel production is central to aviation decarbonization, yet policymakers and investors face uncertainty over which conversion pathways can deliver economically viable fuel while generating meaningful regional economic benefits. Holding total sustainable aviation fuel fixed at one hundred million gallons, we evaluate the techno-economic feasibility and regional economic impacts three technology pathways, Hydro-processed Esters and Fatty Acids, Fischer Tropsch, and Alcohol to Jet, in the southern US under both single-technology and mixed-portfolio deployment scenarios. We show that technology pathway choice alone fundamentally reshapes cost structures, co-product revenues, employment intensity, and tax generation. AtJ achieves lowest minimum selling prices, FT generates larger co-product streams and stronger regional economic spillovers. HEFA’s commercial maturity is constrained by high feedstock cost, low co-product production efficiency, and mediocre economic impact at the regional scale. Mixed-pathway portfolios mitigate trade-offs between cost competitiveness and regional economic impacts, providing an alternative solution to single-pathway deployment by building feedstock resiliency, diversifying economic impacts, and broadening employment opportunities. These findings demonstrate that SAF deployment strategy—not only production volume—plays a key role in determining economic outcomes, providing actionable guidance for regional planners and policymakers designing scalable, economically resilient SAF supply systems.

title: Sport Stadiums and Urban Economic Development: Evidence from Nightlight Data in Europe
affiliations: University of Oviedo, , University of Lausanne and University of Lausanne

detail.title: Sport Stadiums and Urban Economic Development: Evidence from Nightlight Data in Europe
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the local economic impact of new sports stadiums using high- frequency, high-resolution nighttime light (NTL) satellite imagery. Unlike previous studies relying almost exclusively on annual aggregated outcomes over broad spatial units, we exploit monthly and daily NTL data matched to census-level administrative units to distinguish persistent changes in local activity from episodic fluctuations. We examine four newly constructed stadiums in Spain, France, and England, all built on entirely new sites between 2015 and 2020. Our Difference-in-differences and event-study estimates show a consistent and statistically significant increase in localized NTL intensity following stadium inaugurations, characterized by a pronounced spatial decay. Notably, this increase is not driven by match-day activity; rather, it reflects a structural revitalization of the immediate urban vicinity. These patterns are robust to a series of checks using daily data, including controls for match-day activity, alternative buffer definitions, the exclusion of extreme luminosity values, and alternative event-day measures. Overall, the results suggest that stadiums function as localized, multi-purpose urban nodes that generate intermittent economic activation rather than broad- based urban regeneration. More generally, the results highlight the value of fine temporal and spatial data for identifying infrastructure externalities that aggregated measures may overlook.

title: Uncertain Information Advantage and Price Discovery: Evidence from Data Vendor Dissemination Differences
affiliations: INSEAD, London Business School and Rice University - Jesse H. Jones Graduate School of Business

detail.title: Uncertain Information Advantage and Price Discovery: Evidence from Data Vendor Dissemination Differences
detail.abstract: We examine how investors' uncertainty about whether their private signals have already been received and traded upon by other investors influences price discovery. In a near-lab setting, we compare intraday price discovery surrounding unpredictable releases of identical analyst information by IBES and FactSet. We first document significant and largely unpredictable differences in the timing and dissemination of a particular analyst’s forecast estimates to their subscribers by IBES and FactSet. We argue that this creates uncertainty for investors about the novelty and trading value of the forecast news. We predict and find that this uncertainty leads to (i) stock prices responding independently to each vendor’s dissemination, (ii) price discovery at the second release being negatively related to the time elapsed since the first release, (iii) the price impact at the second release being lower than that at the first release,  (iv) the price discovery as well as the price impact at second release being negatively related to past returns, but only when these returns potentially signal prior trading on the news.

title:
Artificial Intelligence in Uk Higher Educational Policy and Institutional Decision Making 

AI And Critical Issues in Uk He Policy Organisation

detail.title:
Artificial Intelligence in Uk Higher Educational Policy and Institutional Decision Making 

AI And Critical Issues in Uk He Policy Organisation
detail.abstract:
This systematic literature review examines how Artificial Intelligence (AI) is positioned within UK higher education (HE) policy and its influence on institutional pedagogical decision making. Drawing on peer reviewed studies, grey literature, theoretical models and policy reports, the review explores institutional responses, readiness and barriers to AI adoption for teaching and learning.

Three research questions guide the review: (1) How is AI framed in UK HE policy and institutional strategies? (2) What evidence demonstrates AI’s influence on pedagogical decision-making? (3) What challenges exist in current UK AI policy for higher education?

Findings indicate that AI integration in UK HE is accelerating but remains fragmented, revealing a gap between policy ambitions and institutional capacity. Difference between teaching-led and research-intensive universities highlight disparities in infrastructure and staff preparedness. Key policy concerns include ethics, equity exclusion and learner efficacy, compounded by limited theoretical coherence and participatory governance.

The review proposes a layered, inclusive framework linking national policy, institutional infrastructure, governance, ethics and pedagogy. It argues that effective AI adoption requires an evidence-led and collaborative approach rather than reliance on technological tools alone. Future research should empirically test the framework to inform ethical and resilient AI ecosystem in higher education.

title: Global GDP growth (1961–2025) and solar activity (1960–2024): R2=0.90
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Global GDP growth (1961–2025) and solar activity (1960–2024): R2=0.90
detail.abstract: The article uses the methodological approach developed by W.S. Jevons and A.L. Chizhevsky. The years of the solar cycles were numbered in the order established in solar astrophysics, grouped, and compared with average global GDP values with a one-year lag. Using the superposition method, a model with a determination coefficient of 0.9368 was obtained. The value of this coefficient in the diagram average Wolf number (independent variable)-average annual growth of global GDP with a lag of 1 year (dependent variable) was 0.9044. To explain the results, the author developed a three-zone astrophysical-biochemical model of the helioeconomic relationship with a one-year lag. The model demonstrates that solar activity extremes-zones of "biological depression" (Wolf number below 16) and "biological stress" (Wolf number above 156)-suppress global economic growth through hormonal imbalances (decreased serotonin and melatonin production) and subsequent pessimism. Stable global GDP growth is ensured exclusively in the "biological optimum" zone (Wolf number between 16 and 156). With a 2025 Wolf number of 123.2, the annual growth rate of global GDP in 2026 will be 3.25%. With a projected 2026 Wolf number of 91.4, global GDP growth in 2027 is projected to be 4.1%. With a projected 2030 Wolf number of 10.7, annual global GDP growth in 2031 would be 1.3%.

title: Constructing Exchange Rate Panels from the BIS Data Portal: A Python Teaching Note for Empirical Finance Research

detail.title: Constructing Exchange Rate Panels from the BIS Data Portal: A Python Teaching Note for Empirical Finance Research
detail.abstract: This teaching note explains how to retrieve bilateral exchange rate data from the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) Data Portal using Python. The note is motivated by a common problem in empirical finance: students often start with convenient free data vendors such as Yahoo! Finance, but final research projects require data sources with clear provenance, stable documentation, and transparent metadata. In the absence of professional paid terminals such as Bloomberg, Refinitiv, or Datastream, official or quasi-official sources such as the BIS provide a more credible foundation for exchange-rate research. The empirical example uses daily spot exchange rates against the U.S. dollar for a set of advanced-economy currencies commonly used in the exchange-rate predictability literature, together with the Taiwan dollar as an additional case of personal research interest.

title: Routing at Temperature: Boltzmann Priors on Transportation Fibres
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business and George Mason University

detail.title: Routing at Temperature: Boltzmann Priors on Transportation Fibres
detail.abstract: Estimating origin-destination (OD) travel from link or margin counts is an ill-posed inverse problem. The data leave the latent integer flows on a high-dimensional lattice fibre, and the prior is what selects a solution from it. Our motivating application is transit route OD estimation from automatic passenger counts: boardings and alightings at each stop fix the margins of an upper-triangular trip table, and the interior is latent. We show that the interpretable transport priors, maximum entropy and gravity, together with the integer-programming point estimate, are one object viewed at three temperatures. The device is the representation of Pincus (1970), which writes a constrained optimum as the low-temperature limit of a Boltzmann measure. Placed on Hazelton's integer fibre it yields a single family π λ (x) ∝ p(x) exp{λf (x)} in which λ = 0 is Bayesian tomography and the iterative-proportional-fitting estimator used in practice, λ → ∞ is the transportation optimum, and intermediate λ is the gravity model with deterrence equal to the temperature. We give the geometry of the fibre as an affine lattice, prove the temperature limits and their exponential rate, connect the λ = 0 end to the Gibbs conditioning principle, identify iterative proportional fitting as the mode of the family, and establish rapid mixing of the sampler through a Poincaré inequality and the conductance of the Markov-basis graph. On real route structure we find that automatic-counter margins pin down the on-board load profile exactly while leaving the trip composition uncertain, and we report that uncertainty with calibrated credible intervals that current practice discards. Three further studies, a controlled OD table, a route-flow network, and a back-calculation of latent counts, confirm that the temperature dial interpolates the two schools exactly.

title: Carbon Trading and Emissions Trading: Legal Mechanisms from Climate Change

detail.title: Carbon Trading and Emissions Trading: Legal Mechanisms from Climate Change
detail.abstract:
Climate change stands as one of the most pressing global challenges of our time, with far-reaching consequences for the planet's ecosystems, weather patterns, and human societies. As the international community grapples with the urgent need for effective solutions, the role of legal mechanisms in mitigating climate change has gained prominence. This dissertation delves into the intricate web of carbon trading and emission trading, exploring the legal frameworks that underpin these mechanisms and their critical significance in addressing climate change.

Achieving large greenhouse gas (GHG) emission cuts at the pace necessary to avoid the worst consequences of climate change has become a pressing challenge for policymakers and has reignited the debate about appropriate climate policy responses. Carbon pricing is often seen as an important instrument to accelerate a low-carbon transition by incentivizing firms and individuals to reduce their carbon emissions or pay for their carbon emissions.

This chapter explores the features, challenges and trade implications of carbon pricing. It reviews the trade relevance of a global carbon pricing scheme as a means of preventing a patchwork of uncoordinated carbon pricing policies. A proliferation of different carbon pricing policies could lead to high transaction costs and the introduction of border carbon adjustment (BCA) mechanisms, which could, in turn, lead to trade tensions. The chapter concludes by discussing the importance of international cooperation to address the fragmentation of carbon pricing schemes and support ambitious climate mitigation actions.

title: Relational Understanding in Intimate Relations: The Generative Relational Epistemology in the Domain of Intimacy

detail.title: Relational Understanding in Intimate Relations: The Generative Relational Epistemology in the Domain of Intimacy

keywords: The Throwing of a Generative Thing

detail.abstract:
A companion work developed a generative relational epistemology, on which a concept becomes observable through the relations among the several symbolic systems that render it, and knowing takes the form of a generative observation that is historically and dialectically produced. That work observed, near its end, that a person is the bearer of a symbolic system, so that the meeting of two persons is a crossing of symbolic worlds. This paper takes up that observation in the domain of intimacy, where the crossing is deepest and its stakes are highest. It asks what relational understanding, so conceived, does in an intimate bond, whether it is good, and how the capacities it requires might be cultivated. The paper builds two cases and then a practice. The functional case sets the potential work of relational understanding, in the generation of trust, the recognition of shared value, the easing of a certain class of conflict, and the quality of a shared life, beside the established theories and findings that treat these same matters, and it locates the distinctive contribution in two characters of the account, the relational and the generative.

The normative case then argues that a functional defense is not sufficient, since an efficient possession of the other can counterfeit the functions of understanding, and it grounds a normative distinction in ethical legitimacy, observed across several ethical traditions and not rested on a single one. Consequentialist, Kantian, care-ethical, and Aristotelian renderings each supply an aspect that the others leave, and non-possession, with generative justice, stands among them. Consistent with the dialectical and materialist conception of truth the companion work develops, the paper does not claim the correctness of a given understanding, and holds instead that understanding, like truth, is generated in historical and contradictory movement, while what can be asked of it is that it be ethically legitimate, a legitimacy whose own criteria are themselves historically generated and set as no final guarantee.

The paper then states the special problem of intimacy, that the bond is a site where these capacities are wagered and not rehearsed, since the value of what is given may return only after a long passage of time and cannot be tried again, so that the field in which a capacity is cultivated and the field in which it is exercised come apart. From this it proposes a model, a set of capacities and not a procedure, divided into those that admit near practice and those that can only be cultivated as a standing disposition, among the latter the throwing of a generative thing into the other's own generative repertoire, the non-intervention that lets a shared dynamic unfold, and the preservation of a relational experience against the day its value is recognized. Non-possession runs throughout as the condition without which the capacities decline into a refined extraction. The paper then turns dialectically upon its own argument, and holds that a full crossing of the other's world would end the bond it was meant to perfect, since the other's unsymbolizable remainder is the core around which desire moves and the reservoir from which the bond's further generation is drawn, so that understanding rightly aimed seeks the other and honors, in the same motion, what in the other it will not reach. The paper offers no final synthesis, and its form keeps the openness its account of understanding requires.

title: Debottlenecking the Coal-to-Dimethyl-Ether Roadmap in Indonesia: A Dynamic Backstop and Mixed-Complementarity Analysis of LPG Substitution, Fiscal Space, and Energy Security
affiliations: Padjadjaran University - Faculty of Economics and Business

detail.title: Debottlenecking the Coal-to-Dimethyl-Ether Roadmap in Indonesia: A Dynamic Backstop and Mixed-Complementarity Analysis of LPG Substitution, Fiscal Space, and Energy Security

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Not available
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not available
declarations.funderStatement: Not available

detail.abstract: Indonesia's flagship coal-to-dimethyl-ether (DME) program was designed to convert abundant low-rank lignite into a domestic substitute for imported liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), yet the 2023 withdrawal of its principal international partner exposed a structural gap between the cost of producing DME and the price of imported LPG. This paper develops a dynamic mixed complementarity problem (MCP) in GAMS-a partial-equilibrium "backstop" framework in the tradition of Nordhaus and Hotelling-to evaluate whether, when, and under which configuration DME can replace LPG while improving fiscal space, energy affordability, and energy security over the 2024-2045 horizon. The model is solved to a globally consistent equilibrium (PATH solver; Inf-Norm of complementarity = 4.7 × 10-3) across three pathways: pure substitution (Scenario A), a 15% drop-in blend (Scenario B), and integrated polygeneration (Scenario C). We find that the recurrent fiscal burden of remaining on imported LPG rises from about 29800 to 47400 rupiah per 3-kg cylinder by 2045, whereas the 15% drop-in blend-the "low-hanging-fruit" (LHF) pathway-turns fiscally positive earliest (by 2028), requires no household-stove retrofit, and delivers the largest per-cylinder saving (about 16700 rupiah) by 2045. Pure substitution and polygeneration eliminate LPG imports entirely (by 2033 and 2032 respectively) but break even later. The seven debottlenecking strategies are translated into model parameters and shown to be jointly sufficient to cross the Nordhaus switching point. The contribution is a transparent, policy-legible dynamic model that reframes DME not as an immediately profitable commodity but as a sequenced, backstop technology whose viability is unlocked by blending, cogeneration, and dynamic pricing rather than by perpetual subsidy.

title: Indigenous Land Rights and Firm Behavior
affiliations: Ahmedabad University and University of Minnesota - Minneapolis

detail.title: Indigenous Land Rights and Firm Behavior
detail.abstract: Indigenous communities often inhabit ecologically sensitive land without enjoying formal property rights, leaving these areas vulnerable to commercial overreach. Whether formalizing land rights for tribal communities can deter industrial exploitation is an open question. We develop a model of firms seeking land-use permits which predicts that tribal forest rights reduce overall land demand near tribal areas, but shift the composition of economic activity toward larger firms. This occurs because land rights raise land acquisition costs, which constrain smaller firms more, while the general equilibrium reduction in permit applications benefits all firms equally. We test these predictions using India's Forest Rights Act (FRA), which granted nationwide tribal forest rights in 2008. New data on deforestation permits and a firm panel confirm that land demand declines in districts with higher tribal forest-dependent populations, driven by longer permit processing times. The decline is strongest for smaller projects and firms, and weaker or absent for larger ones. Firm inputs and productivity mimic this pattern. Consequently, land conflicts and population displacement intensify post-reform, especially around large projects. Our findings point to a resorting rather than retreat of development pressure on indigenous land.

title: Rethinking Energy in Displacement Contexts
affiliations: and

detail.title: Rethinking Energy in Displacement Contexts
detail.abstract: Displaced persons in resource-constrained contexts experience a lack of access to energy, with consequences for health, safety, livelihoods and wellbeing. Existing research and implementation measures addressing energy in displacement contexts remain shaped by recurring shortcomings, in particular limited attention to displaced persons' needs, a focus on technology provision, and a linear framing of change processes. These shortcomings point to a broader conceptual gap in how energy access in displacement contexts is understood, supported by evidence and translated into action. Drawing on academic and grey literature from various disciplines and on insights from practice, this article proposes an alternative point of departure for research and implementation. We argue that improving energy access requires placing displaced persons' perspectives at the centre of how energy services are understood and shaped. We conceptualise enhancing access to energy services as a non-linear, locally grounded transformation process in which priorities, pathways and arrangements are progressively shaped through the inclusion of diverse perspectives. To advance conceptual clarity, we propose an integrative approach that identifies core areas of inquiry for transforming access to energy services and integrating diverse perspectives, while linking them to relevant research fields and methodological entry points. The article contributes to strengthening conceptual clarity, evidence generation and practical engagement towards equitable and sustainable access to energy services in displacement contexts.

title: Financial Resilience and Energy Security:An Imperfect-Competition Model of PLN's Coal Supply Chain and Financing Constraints
affiliations: Padjadjaran University - Faculty of Economics and Business

detail.title: Financial Resilience and Energy Security:An Imperfect-Competition Model of PLN's Coal Supply Chain and Financing Constraints

declarations.declarationOfInterest: not available
declarations.ethicsApproval: not available
declarations.funderStatement: not available

detail.abstract: Indonesia's state electricity company, PT PLN (Persero), holds a constitutionally entrenched, vertically integrated legal monopoly over electricity supply. In 2026 this monopoly came under visible strain: a national coal-supply shortfall of roughly 13 million tonnes triggered rolling blackouts on Java, an unrelated transmission failure blacked out all of Sumatra, retail taris remained frozen for a fourth consecutive quarter, and government receivables owed to PLN more than doubled, from Rp43.29 trillion to Rp110.74 trillion, in a single year. This paper develops a partial-equilibrium model of PLN's coal-red generation segment that embeds PLN's nancing constraint directly into the physical dispatch problem, in the spirit of the imperfect-competition and soft-budget-constraint literatures. The model is calibrated to PLN's FY2025 audited consolidated nancial statements and to real July 2026 market data (coal reference prices, the national coal supply-contract gap, installed capacity, and Bank Indonesia's policy rate). We show, rst, that a large share of the model's headline nancing-stress nding is conditional on an unsourced assumption about PLN's opening short-term debt stock, and is not a robust feature of the underlying seasonal cash-ow cycle. Second, once monthly emergency nancing is realistically capped rather than treated as unlimited, tightening credit access and deepening the physical coal shortage push unserved energy and unfunded cash shortfalls in the same direction across a systematic 30-point stress grid, conrming a direct, quantiable channel from nancial resilience to blackout risk. We conclude with policy recommendations on tari-adjustment credibility, arrears settlement, and the design of PLN's emergency nancing facilities.

title: Closed Minds, Unmoored Ambition, Relational Contempt: How a Psychological Triad Produces Authoritarian Outcomes in Competitive and Dominant-Party Democracies

detail.title: Closed Minds, Unmoored Ambition, Relational Contempt: How a Psychological Triad Produces Authoritarian Outcomes in Competitive and Dominant-Party Democracies
detail.abstract: Why do similarly authoritarian political actors self-destruct while others build durable authoritarian systems? This paper advances a mechanism-based theory: the authoritarian lock, a self-reinforcing psychological configuration comprising epistemic closure, unmoored ambition, and relational contempt. The lock's outcome-self-destruction versus durable rule-is conditioned by the structure of the elite cartel. Through a structured comparison of Miriam Defensor Santiago, Rodrigo Duterte, Lee Kuan Yew, and Franklin Drilon, the analysis shows that Santiago's rationalised hybrid lock led to self-destruction in a fractious Philippine Senate; Duterte's intuitive closure bypassed the same environment through populist appeal, producing durable rule; Lee's principled ambition prevented the lock, and a cohesive cartel channelled his contempt into state-building; Drilon, lacking the lock, succeeded through coalition-building. The framework integrates psychology and institutions, explaining divergent trajectories where pure personality or structural accounts cannot.

title: Global Business and Local Struggle: Chapter 8, 'Towards More Responsive Redress?'
affiliations: , University of Newcastle (Australia) - Newcastle Law School, University of Melbourne School of Social and Political Sciences, University of Melbourne and

detail.title: Global Business and Local Struggle: Chapter 8, 'Towards More Responsive Redress?'

declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was gained for the study
declarations.funderStatement: Australian Research Council Linkage Grant

detail.abstract:
This chapter is Chapter 8 of  'Global Business and Local Struggle, Reimagining Non-Judicial Remedy for Human Rights'. This chapter considers the practical implications of our analysis for those seeking redress and for NJMs themselves? And what are the implications for those advocating, and those involved in negotiating, the Draft UN Treaty on Business and Human Rights, an instrument that is often characterised as a preferred alternative to NJMs? Through our ten case studies we have shown considerable diversity in whether and how transnational non-judicial mechanisms for business and human rights (BHR) have provided opportunities for workers and communities to exert pressure on companies to respond to their grievances. Occasionally, NJMs played a significant role in augmenting such pressure (for example in Wilmar), and often they played a more peripheral one (Vedanta). Non-judicial mechanisms could fail to provide support (Weda Bay, POSCO) or could provide limited support in a way that reflected the NJM's own internal political dynamics, while ignoring constructive proposals from well-respected local civil society actors (Sumangali). They could provide a crucial source of leverage in building relationships on the ground to assist workers but could themselves be hampered by a lack of resources or shifts in the priorities of allies (Sportswear). Each of our ten cases provides stark evidence that approaching an NJM should never be the only strategy pursued by communities and workers to gain recognition and redress. But it can be an important part of that strategy, provided those seeking redress, and their allies, possess the necessary capacities, skills and support to realise potential gains.

This chapter is from a book published by Cambridge University Press (‘CUP’): Global Business and Local Struggle, Reimagining Non-Judicial Remedy for Human Rights by Tim Connor, Annie Delaney, Fiona Haines, Kate Macdonald and Shelley Marshall [https://doi.org/10.1017/9781009529389]. The book's Introduction is available open access on the Cambridge Core website and several other chapters are available on SSRN in accordance with CUP’s Green Open Access Policy. This chapter is free to view and download for private research and study only. Not for re-distribution or re-use. © Cambridge University Press.

title: Does a Non-Binding Agreement Move Trade? A Falsification Test from Entry into and Exit from the Belt and Road Initiative

detail.title: Does a Non-Binding Agreement Move Trade? A Falsification Test from Entry into and Exit from the Belt and Road Initiative

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study uses aggregate country-level trade data and does not involve human participants.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Do non-binding international commitments-memoranda of understanding, framework declarations, and other soft-law instruments-move real trade, or do they merely label commercial relationships already under way? We test this for the content-free limiting case, the Belt and Road Initiative, whose memoranda carry no tariff, no quota, and no enforceable obligation, and we treat entry into and exit from the agreement as a two-sided natural experiment. We bring three designs that share neither data nor estimator: staggered difference-indifferences , synthetic control, and a 166-country China-versus-donor gravity panel. In all three, a signatory's exports to China are a bounded zero at entry, and they show no detectable loss at the one estimable exit; the interval rules out an entry gain above roughly 40 percent. The import side does rise, but its trajectory passes through the signing date without a structural break: the agreement ratifies a pre-existing trend rather than creating it. A memorandum with no policy core leaves no falsifiable trade footprint we can detect, as with the null long debated for the binding WTO.

reference: SAFE Working Paper No. 490
title: One Advisor for the Whole World? Cross-Country Evidence on Financial Advice from Large Language Models
affiliations: Leibniz Institute for Financial Research SAFE

detail.title: One Advisor for the Whole World? Cross-Country Evidence on Financial Advice from Large Language Models

publicationDetails.journalName: Leibniz Institute for Financial Research SAFE Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: Households around the world increasingly take portfolio advice from the same handful of large language models. Does that advice adjust to what local circumstances warrant? I pose the same portfolio problem to leading models across twenty-one countries, each in its own language. Advice is nearly uniform across countries, even though the explanations invoke local context. What moves the advice instead is the model a household consults, not the country it lives in. The models follow retail financial advice rather than what academic finance would prescribe, and fail to incorporate the household's balance sheet even when it is stated. While automated advice once held out the promise of tailoring guidance to everyone, large language models encode the same advice for everyone.

title: Accounting For Model Uncertainty in Fiscal Multiplier Estimation: A Model-Averaging Local Projection Approach
affiliations: University of Zaragoza - Department of Economic Analysis and Universidad de Zaragoza

detail.title: Accounting For Model Uncertainty in Fiscal Multiplier Estimation: A Model-Averaging Local Projection Approach

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The opinions are those of the authors and do not necessarily reflect the views of the AIReF
declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by the Ministerio de Ciencia e Innovación/Agencia Estatal de Investigación under Grant PID2024-157255NB-I00.

detail.abstract: Government spending multipliers estimated using local projections and external instruments vary substantially across empirical studies, partly reflecting model uncertainty. We propose a model-averaging local projection instrumental variables (MA-LP-IV) framework that formally accounts for model uncertainty when estimating cumulative fiscal multipliers. Applying the method to a panel of 17 OECD countries over the period 1980-2020, and using narrative fiscal shocks as external instruments, we estimate multipliers exceeding one at short-and medium-term horizons. Although the estimated multipliers decline at longer horizons, they remain positive on average, while estimation uncertainty increases considerably. Posterior inclusion probabilities indicate that monetary conditions are consistently important covariates for explaining multiplier dynamics, whereas taxes and public debt become increasingly relevant at longer horizons.

title: On Hilbert's 8th Problem: II
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: On Hilbert's 8th Problem: II
detail.abstract: We study the zeros of the Riemann zeta function through the theory of generalized gamma convolutions (GGC) and Thorin measures, applied to a Hadamard factorisation of the Riemann ξ-function. For α > 1, Riemann's reciprocal ξ-function is expressed as the Laplace transform of a GGC, with an explicit Lévy form and a reciprocal Thorin measure obtained from the primal Lévy density by a sine-squared transform. The construction is then carried to the centre α = 1 2. There, through Riemann's incomplete-gamma continuation of ξ, we prove our main result: the primal Pólya kernel unfolds, cell by cell, into positive Γ(2) mixtures, and the assembled mixing measure M is positive (Theorem 5). Two facts single out this representation. First, by the SteutelKristiansen theorem a positive mixture of Γ(α) laws is innitely divisible exactly when α ∈ (0, 2], so Γ(2) is the threshold shape at which positivity of the mixing measure alone secures innite divisibility. Second, the mixing measure M is positive, which we prove cell by cell through an average-of-powers identity that turns an apparently signed alternating series into a monotone Leibniz series. Positivity of M makes the cell mixtures and the shiftcollapsed positive proxy they assemble infinitely divisible, xing the cellwise amplitudes. The completed ratio ξ(1/2 + s)/ξ(1 2) is not this proxy but a phase-weighted reassembly of the cells, in which arithmetic phases at log-frequencies log π + 2 log n carry the zeros. We emphasise that the present note does not prove RH: positivity of M controls the amplitudes unconditionally, whereas RH is the statement that the accompanying phases produce only real nulls equivalently the non-negativity of ξ's reciprocal Thorin measure, a total-positivity condition strictly stronger than infinite divisibility, and it is left open. This amplitude/phase split is the common wall behind the classical real-zeros criteria of Pólya-Cardon (Hermite-Biehler), de Bruijn (the Gaussian ow), and Walker (monotonicity): each holds at the level of a single Γ(2) cell but not across the positive mixture.

title: Complexity in Monetary Policy Communications

detail.title: Complexity in Monetary Policy Communications
detail.abstract: How does linguistic complexity affect the transmission of monetary policy communication? I provide new RCT evidence from about 2000 U.S. respondents randomly exposed to FOMC statements that differ only in language complexity. Simpler language increases understanding and moves inflation and GDP growth expectations more strongly, but it does not increase trust or confidence in the Federal Reserve, relative to more complex communication. Complementary financial market evidence suggests that complexity attenuates asset price responses to monetary policy shocks.

title: Industrial AI Resilience Framework (IARF): Cyber-Physical Architecture and Causal Mechanism for Critical Operations

detail.title: Industrial AI Resilience Framework (IARF): Cyber-Physical Architecture and Causal Mechanism for Critical Operations

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known financial or personal relationships that could have influenced the work reported in this paper. The research is conceptual in nature and does not involve any commercial funding or institutional bias.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethical approval was not required for this study as it does not involve human participants, patient data, or experimental procedures. The work is conceptual and focuses on system-level architectural design for industrial AI resilience.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. It was developed as an independent academic research initiative.

detail.abstract: Industrial artificial intelligence (AI) can be statistically accurate and, at the same time, operationally fragile: a high-performing model may induce physical consequences when it lacks bounds, traceability, and recoverability within operational technology (OT). The literature addresses partial facets of the problem-anomaly detection, predictive maintenance, OT cybersecurity, secure machine-learning operations (MLOps), digital twins, resilience engineering, functional safety, and adversarial learning-but offers no integrated architecture that explains how to detect, contain, safely degrade, and recover an OT-AI system when algorithmic failure, data degradation, or adversarial manipulation threaten to propagate into cyber-physical consequences. This work proposes the Industrial AI Resilience Framework (IARF), a design-science-research (DSR) artifact composed of five structural layers and two transversal capabilities, articulated by a causal mechanism formalized as a hybrid supervisory automaton. The formalization specifies state variables, a race condition that determines system failure, and balancing and reinforcing feedback loops. Six core constructs are operationalized with their measurement nature and causal role, and the framework undergoes an analytical structural validation-performed without datagrounded in logical consistency, ablation-based completeness, and coverage-based sufficiency. The IARF is presented not as validated theory but as an artifact with ten testable propositions (P1-P10) and a three-level empirical validation plan. Boundary conditions, contribution, and limitations are discussed.

title: Authoritarian Antitrust
affiliations: University of Sao Paulo - Faculdade de Direito

detail.title: Authoritarian Antitrust
detail.abstract:
Presidents have never merely watched antitrust from the sidelines. They have used it both to intensify and to restrain enforcement, translating their governing agendas into antitrust policy. But the familiar story of presidential antitrust remains incomplete. Alongside it lies a less noble one: presidents have also used enforcement power to discipline adversaries, shield allies, extract personal political support, displace rival regulatory agendas, and turn antitrust into a lever of presidential control.
This Article brings that hidden history into view by naming a distinct and undertheorized phenomenon: authoritarian antitrust. Authoritarian antitrust is the use of antitrust policy through the deliberate sabotage of the legal, administrative, and political accountability systems that are supposed to keep enforcement democratically contestable. Recovering episodes dating back to Franklin D. Roosevelt, the Article shows that authoritarian antitrust is not simply ordinary politicization, illiberal policy, illegality, or corruption. It is a technique of democratic erosion: the conversion of enforcement discretion into a means of closing democratic contestation and consolidating presidential power. Although authoritarian antitrust became more frequent and systematic under Donald J. Trump, the longer history reconstructed here shows that the recent pattern reflects more than the conduct of any single president. It arises from deeper structural conditions: the expansion of presidential power, the concentration of private economic power, and the erosion of state capacity.
The Article makes four contributions. First, it connects episodes that have usually been treated as isolated abuses and reveals a recurring pattern in presidential antitrust. Second, it explains why antitrust is especially useful to would-be autocrats. Antitrust’s normative elasticity allows presidents to stretch or narrow enforcement in the name of competing public values, while its institutional flexibility gives officials broad discretion over theories, investigations, settlements, merger review, and enforcement priorities. Together, these features allow presidents to govern through selective pressure while preserving the appearance of legality. Third, the Article offers a democratic barometer for antitrust governance, rejecting both the technocratic claim that politics has no place in enforcement and the politicalagnostic view that all presidential direction is equally legitimate. Fourth, it points toward reforms that can keep antitrust institutions open to democratic contestation, including information-forcing and conflict-enabling measures that strengthen executive, legislative, and judicial checks.

title: The Crypto Promise Unfulfilled: Performance Analysis of Digital Assets from January 2024 through June 2026
affiliations: Marquette University

detail.title: The Crypto Promise Unfulfilled: Performance Analysis of Digital Assets from January 2024 through June 2026
detail.abstract: This paper examines the performance of major cryptocurrencies relative to traditional and emerging asset classes from January 2024 through June 2026. The analysis begins with the landmark SEC approval of spot Bitcoin ETFs in January 2024, widely viewed as the institutionalization moment for cryptocurrency. Despite this regulatory milestone and the subsequent election of a pro-crypto presidential administration, the cryptocurrency asset class has experienced significant underperformance, particularly from 2025 onward. Using a comprehensive dataset including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Dogecoin, the Official Trump (TRUMP) memecoin, AI-focused equity ETFs, gold, real estate, and a 70/30 passive portfolio benchmark, this study quantifies the shift in capital allocation away from digital assets toward AI infrastructure investments. The findings indicate that the crypto trade has largely collapsed in 2025-2026, with the TRUMP token emerging as the worst-performing asset, declining approximately 96% from its peak. Risk-adjusted return analysis confirms that cryptocurrencies exhibit persistently high volatility with increasingly unfavorable Sharpe ratios, while AI equities have delivered superior returns with comparatively moderate risk profiles.

title: Corporate Governance and Financial Distress Risk: The Dynamics of Structural Fragility
affiliations: University of Wollongong, Wollongong NSW Australia, University of Wollongong, School of Business and University of Wollongong - School of Accounting Economics and Finance

detail.title: Corporate Governance and Financial Distress Risk: The Dynamics of Structural Fragility
detail.abstract: Why does corporate governance retain predictive information about financial distress after contemporaneous financial ratios lose signal? Using Chinese A-share firms from 2007-2023, we show that structural governance decays more slowly than financial health and remains informative at longer forecast horizons. Financial-only AUC falls from 0.880 to 0.617 between one-and five-year horizons, while governance-only AUC falls from 0.750 to 0.654. Governance also predicts distress among financially healthy firms. Mechanism tests show that stronger governance predicts lower tunneling exposure, while persistent tunneling exposure predicts future distress and partially accounts for the governance-distress association.

title: How to Buy a Trade Surplus
affiliations: Peterson Institute and Peterson Institute for International Economics

detail.title: How to Buy a Trade Surplus

publicationDetails.detailsText: Peterson Institute for International Economics Working Paper No. 26-13
publicationDetails.journalName: Peterson Institute for International Economics (PIIE) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper shows that fiscal policy and net official financial flows, including foreign exchange intervention, are important drivers of trade (current account) imbalances. Each $1 that a government devotes to a fiscal surplus invested in foreign-currency assets raises a country's current account balance by about $0.80. Other factors also matter, including trend growth rates, per capita income, stocks of foreign assets, and aging populations. The paper extends previous research (Gagnon and Sarsenbayev 2021) by six years and roughly 1,000 observations. The results are broadly similar to those previously obtained.

reference: Cornell Legal Studies Research Paper No. 26-09
title: Measuring What Matters: Investigating the Hidden Costs of Legal Search Methods
affiliations: , , University of Georgia and

detail.title: Measuring What Matters: Investigating the Hidden Costs of Legal Search Methods

publicationDetails.detailsText: Cornell Legal Studies Research Paper No. 26-09
publicationDetails.journalName: Cornell Law School Legal Studies Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
This paper asks a practical question: when lawyers, students, or institutions choose between different legal search techniques, such as print/index research, Boolean search, natural-language search, and generative-AI search, what are the real costs and benefits of that choice – not just money, but in terms of time, accuracy, research-skill development, information preservation, bias, professional responsibility, and environmental impact? The analysis rests on two foundational premises: first, that effective legal research involves learning that develops from the iterative research journey itself. The process of discovering, analyzing, and synthesizing legal authorities is not merely instrumental but constitutes a core component of legal reasoning and professional development. Second, that the legal profession’s highest calling lies in its creativity and analytical sophistication; the ability to construct novel arguments, identify unexpected connections between legal principles, and develop innovative solutions to complex problems.

The paper’s core argument is that generative AI may save time, but its value in legal research cannot be assessed responsibly unless we also account for verification burdens, hallucination risk, loss of deep research process, client- facing harms, and other hidden costs. When AI tools reduce associate lawyers to cite-checking and verification roles rather than engaging in substantive legal analysis, this represents a fundamental shift that undermines both individual professional development and the profession’s broader intellectual capacity. The research process itself, not just its outputs, serves essential functions in developing legal judgment, fostering creative problem-solving, and maintaining the analytical rigor that distinguishes legal practice from mere information retrieval.

title: Selected Evidence, Omitted Information, and Belief Updating in Large Language Model Decision Support
affiliations: Nanyang Technological University (NTU) and

detail.title: Selected Evidence, Omitted Information, and Belief Updating in Large Language Model Decision Support
detail.abstract: AI advisors often receive selected rather than complete evidence. A prompt may include the favorable parts of a hiring file, the regulatory checks in a due-diligence screen, or a procurement dashboard that omits conflict-of-interest information. We test whether large language models use the selection process to infer what the prompt leaves out. The design adapts Enke's WYSIATI task: an initial signal induces a High/Low assessment, later evidence is selected conditional on that assessment, and final estimates are compared with Bayesian and visible-sample benchmarks. Study 1 provides the diagnostic benchmark and reanalyzes Enke's human microdata. Humans and several models move toward visible-sample updating, while GPT-5.5 largely corrects the numeric contrast. Rationale outputs provide diagnostic evidence rather than hidden chain-of-thought traces: many responses echo the selection rule, but Bayesian correction is more closely associated with explicit hidden-expectation reasoning. Study 2 embeds the same structure in domain-framed numerical tasks for financial due diligence, hiring, and procurement. Selected is compared with a posterior-equivalent coarse-placeholder Control that shows the same selected ratings and makes the omitted-side midpoint explicit. The contrast remains after Full-arm arithmetic checks. A later visible-only instruction moves estimates further toward the displayed sample. The results identify a specific failure in numerical updating from selected evidence.

title: Functional-Form Misspecification in Earnings Management Models: Evidence from Nonlinear Structure
affiliations: University of Wollongong, Wollongong NSW Australia, University of Wollongong, School of Business and University of Wollongong - School of Accounting Economics and Finance

detail.title: Functional-Form Misspecification in Earnings Management Models: Evidence from Nonlinear Structure
detail.abstract: This study evaluates whether commonly used additive logistic specifications provide an adequate representation of proxy-based earnings management outcomes. Rather than treating predictive performance as an end in itself, we adopt a specification-testing framework and interpret performance differentials across models as evidence on the validity of functional-form assumptions. Using a comprehensive sample of Chinese listed firms between 2008-2023 and a strict walk-forward temporal validation design, we compare baseline logistic regression, augmented parametric specifications, and flexible nonlinear estimators. We document three main findings. First, augmented logistic models deliver statistically significant improvements over baseline specifications for accrual-based proxies, indicating that additive linear assumptions are empirically restrictive. Second, flexible nonlinear estimators generate substantial additional gains for both accrual-and real activity-based proxies, suggesting that low-dimensional parametric extensions are insufficient to approximate the underlying conditional structure. Third, diagnostic analysis reveals that misclassification under linear specifications is systematic rather than random and is concentrated in regions characterized by joint configurations of firm characteristics. These results provide evidence of functional-form misspecification in proxy-based settings and suggest that commonly used specifications may impose restrictive assumptions that affect empirical inference.

title: Financial Resilience and Firm Valuation: Empirical Evidence from Indonesian FMCG Sector (2019-2026)

detail.title: Financial Resilience and Firm Valuation: Empirical Evidence from Indonesian FMCG Sector (2019-2026)
