declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve any human participants, patients, or animal subjects. The research is based entirely on publicly available corporate financial data and secondary data resources, and therefore, formal ethical approval was not required.

detail.abstract: This study examines the determinants of financial resilience and its subsequent impact on firm valuation within Indonesia's vital Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) and consumer related sectors amidst prolonged global economic volatility. Employing a panel data analysis, this paper investigates the empirical effects of profitability, proxied by Return on Assets (ROA), and capital structure, measured via the Debt-to-Equity Ratio (DER), on firm value, proxied by the Price to Book Ratio (PBV). The dataset comprises 17 prominent consumer related companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) spanning the period from 2019 to 2026. The descriptive results reveal that Indonesian FMCG firms maintain a remarkably conservative capital structure alongside robust operational profitability, serving as a critical internal shield against external macroeconomic disruptions. The findings provide strategic insights for corporate treasurers, portfolio managers, and policymakers in designing forward-looking financial frameworks that secure supply chain sustainability and domestic economic resilience during systemic crises.

title: Designing Feedback for Psychological Safety: Balancing Openness and Individual Comfort through the Context-Format-Readiness Model

detail.title: Designing Feedback for Psychological Safety: Balancing Openness and Individual Comfort through the Context-Format-Readiness Model

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have influenced the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This paper is based on a conceptual literature review and an anonymous practice-based case analysis. No personal data were collected, and no human subjects research requiring formal ethics approval was conducted.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding and was conducted independently as part of the author's doctoral studies.

detail.abstract: This paper explores how feedback can be effectively designed in coaching contexts to support psychological safety while still enabling honest and meaningful feedback. It argues that although feedback is essential for learning, it can also create discomfort and reduce openness if not carefully structured. Drawing on existing research and a practical case analysis, the paper highlights that the way feedback is organized-not just what is said or how it is delivered-plays a critical role in how it is experienced. The case analysis illustrates how structured group feedback formats can produce different reactions, with some individuals engaging openly while others experience discomfort and withdraw. To better understand and handle these dynamics, the paper introduces the Context-Format-Readiness (CFR) model. The model focuses on three interrelated dimensions-context, feedback format, and individual readiness-and describes how their interaction shapes the experience and effectiveness of feedback in coaching settings. It also outlines an iterative approach in which psychological safety is assessed, feedback practices are introduced in gradual ways, and are adapted over time to align with these dimensions. By reframing feedback as a design challenge rather than a fixed method, the paper offers a perspective that invites readers to rethink how feedback can better support both development and psychological safety in coaching-oriented environments.

title: The Duty of Disclosure in International Arbitration: Transparency, Apparent Bias and the Structural Limits of Impartiality

detail.title: The Duty of Disclosure in International Arbitration: Transparency, Apparent Bias and the Structural Limits of Impartiality
detail.abstract: This paper examines the duty of disclosure in arbitration through comparing between English Arbitration Law and the broader international commercial arbitration framework. It discusses how both systems despite being founded on the need to preserve arbitrator independence, impartiality and party confidence, yet they differ in structure, predictability and practical application. English law offers a more defined framework for disclosure and apparent bias, especially following Halliburton and the 2025 amendments to the Arbitration Act 1996. The wider international framework, by contrast, relies on a combination of the UNCITRAL Model Law, institutional rules and soft law instruments including the IBA Guidelines, thereby producing more flexibility but also more uncertainty. The paper further argues that disclosure, despite being essential, cannot act as a complete safeguard. It operates at the level of transparency, yet it does not fully address structural pressures such as repeat appointments, professional networks and market incentives. The paper concludes that disclosure remains central to arbitral legitimacy, but must be understood as part of a wider framework of procedural integrity.

title: How Do Money and Tax Illusion Impact Long-Term Investments? An Experiment
affiliations: Leibniz  Universität Hannover, Leibniz University Hannover, Leibniz Universität Hannover - Faculty of Economics and Management and Leibniz  Universität Hannover - Institute for Risk and Insurance

detail.title: How Do Money and Tax Illusion Impact Long-Term Investments? An Experiment
detail.abstract: The wealth effects of inflation and taxes on long-term savings, such as retirement investments, can be substantial. Nonetheless, individuals misperceive the impact of both taxes and inflation. Based on a unified theoretical framework, we distinguish between potential cognitive mechanisms underlying tax and inflation misperceptions and derive their implications for investment behavior. Using an incentivized, pre-registered online experiment, we test how these misperceptions influence individual investment decisions. In our baseline setting, inflation and taxation affect investment outcomes equivalently in real or after-tax terms. The results show that-even though all participants were informed about the effects of inflation and taxes on investment returns-investment distortions remain significant in both settings. Distortions driven by money illusion clearly exceed those caused by tax illusion. We find that both rational inattention and anchoring contribute to these distortions, with anchoring appearing more persistent in the inflation setting. Money illusion is therefore not only larger than tax illusion but also harder to undo. Money and tax illusion become more pronounced when future tax and inflation rates are uncertain. We then test the effectiveness of different communication strategies in this setting. Additional tabular information, visualizations, and attention nudges do not systematically reduce money or tax illusion. We show that requiring participants to view real or after-tax consequences before decision making is the most effective intervention; voluntary access has weaker effects, and later display does not systematically reduce the distortions.

title: Strategic Bargaining in Multi-Buyer Markets: Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards for LLM Negotiations
affiliations: , , California Institute of Technology (Caltech), Georgia Institute of Technology - H. Milton Stewart School of Industrial and Systems Engineering and Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - School of Engineering

detail.title: Strategic Bargaining in Multi-Buyer Markets: Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards for LLM Negotiations
detail.abstract:
Negotiation is a fundamental strategic interaction in management science, characterized by agents attempting to reach agreements while protecting private information, such as reservation costs and hidden valuations. A prevalent yet complex scenario involves a single seller negotiating concurrently with multiple buyers, each possessing heterogeneous, private budgets. In such settings, constrained by a limited number of communication turns, the seller must balance exploring the broader market to discover the highest valuation with concentrating sufficient turns on a single target buyer to secure the best possible outcome. Our analysis reveals a significant gap in standard Large Language Models (LLMs): while these models are linguistically proficient, they fail to act as effective economic decision-makers. Specifically, they exhibit a failure to explore the buyer pool, often fixating on the current highest bid rather than strategically investigating the market to discover latent high valuations. 

In this paper, we propose a specialized training recipe using Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards (RLVR). By anchoring the reward function to objective economic outcomes, the strategic balance between market discovery and surplus extraction emerges natively through the learning process. Our results demonstrate that the trained seller undergoes a multi-stage strategic evolution, learning to leverage price anchoring and strategic probing to identify more profitable counterparties. The agent extracts substantially higher surplus than frontier models by both improving its persuasive bargaining skills and consistently closing deals with high-value buyers. Finally, we show that our seller strategies generalize robustly to unseen buyer negotiation styles and budget distributions.

title: Who Trains the Next Senior? Managing Software Engineering When AI Makes Code Cheap
affiliations: and

detail.title: Who Trains the Next Senior? Managing Software Engineering When AI Makes Code Cheap
detail.abstract: Generative and agentic AI have made the routine work of software engineering nearly free, and the first casualty is the junior engineer. Engineering leaders now face a choice most are making by default. Cheap machine-made code commoditizes breadth, the plausible and conventional, while raising the value of two things humans still supply and machines do not: depth, the judgment of which answer is right in this system, and divergence, the perspective from outside the consensus that a senior-plus-AI team structurally lacks. Left to inertia, organizations slide into substitution, replacing juniors and letting review, apprenticeship, and the diversity of what they build hollow out. The alternative, complementarity, is a set of concrete moves: shrink the unit of review, tier scrutiny by consequence, measure verified outcomes rather than raw output, and rebuild the apprenticeship on purpose. We show why the choice is real, what each path costs, and what to do about it now.

title: Privacy That Protects and Privacy That Launders: zk-Mixers, Private Swaps, and Systemic Contagion in Decentralized Finance

detail.title: Privacy That Protects and Privacy That Launders: zk-Mixers, Private Swaps, and Systemic Contagion in Decentralized Finance

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there is no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study did not involve human participants or animal subjects.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Zero-knowledge privacy protocols let users hide transaction details on public blockchains. Systems like Tornado Cash, FixedFloat, and the Houdini Private Swap feature recently added to Jumper rely on cryptographic techniques that unlink sender and receiver addresses. These constructions give legitimate users meaningful protection for their financial activity. They also create a straightforward dual-use dilemma. The February 2025 Bybit incident supplies a clear example. Thieves stole $1.5 billion in ETH, the largest cryptocurrency theft on record. The FBI linked the attack to North Korea's Lazarus Group. The stolen funds moved quickly through Tornado Cash. The resulting lack of transparency triggered a wave of customer withdrawals. Bybit responded by securing loans of several hundred million dollars from other institutions to keep its operations running. Cases like this demonstrate that zk-based privacy tools, when used at large scale for illicit purposes, can accelerate liquidity crises and place costs on market participants who had no involvement in the original theft. The real problem is not the underlying mathematics that delivers privacy. It lies in the missing mechanisms that could impose accountability on criminal actors while leaving the privacy protections for everyone else intact.

title: Here Today, Gone Today: First Evidence on European Zero-Day Options
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Here Today, Gone Today: First Evidence on European Zero-Day Options
detail.abstract: This paper provides the first systematic empirical analysis of zero-days-to-expiry options on the EURO STOXX 50 and the DAX. Since their introduction on the Eurex in 2023, daily-expiry index options have grown rapidly, yet their European pricing and trading costs remain undocumented. Using intraday order-book data, four results emerge. Put-call parity holds tightly at quoted mid-prices, with cross-strike dispersion of the implied forward around a tenth of an index point for the EURO STOXX 50 and half a point for the DAX. This efficiency is, however, largely an artefact of mid-quote measurement: once the spread is crossed, the round-trip cost of a synthetic position is roughly fifteen to twenty times larger, near 10% and 13% of the at-the-money straddle premium, respectively. The proportional cost rises sharply into expiry, reaching roughly 40% and 70% of the straddle value in the final half-hour. Costs peak at the money, where the premium is thinnest relative to the spread, and are consistent across both indices. The market is thus priced most precisely where it can least be traded, with trading costs concentrated in the final, thinnest-liquidity minutes of the session.

title: Periodic Investment under Capital Injections with Stochastic Drift and Multi-Asset Jump Risk
affiliations: Soochow University, Soochow University, Soochow University and Soochow University

detail.title: Periodic Investment under Capital Injections with Stochastic Drift and Multi-Asset Jump Risk
detail.abstract: In this paper, we study a multi-asset periodic investment problem under capital injections, stochastic drift, jump risk, cash-flow costs, and weighted intertemporal downside-risk constraints. Unlike a selffinancing portfolio, a periodic investment account is affected by the timing of capital injections, the net investable amount, and the remaining investment horizon of each injected cash flow. We model risky assets by a multi-asset Merton jump-diffusion process with stochastic drift, where Brownian motions describe continuous market fluctuations, common jumps capture systematic shocks, and idiosyncratic jumps capture asset-specific shocks. Cash-flow costs account for the gap between gross capital injections and net investable cash flows, while the traditional terminal downside-risk constraint is extended to a weighted intertemporal form. To handle the distributional and tail-risk difficulties caused by the accumulation of dependent wealth components, we use a comonotonic approximation and reformulate the downside-risk constraint through the Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) of the corresponding loss variable. Compared with the existing stochastic-drift periodic investment framework, we derive a sharper CVaR upper bound for the stochastic drift component by refining the treatment of the positive-part expectation. This yields a less conservative risk amplification coefficient. We then derive a fractional Kelly strategy within the constant mix strategy class and further develop a rolling-horizon fractional Kelly strategy, in which portfolio allocations are updated using rolling parameter estimates and current account wealth. We conduct numerical experiments using daily data for five representative A-share stocks. The model comparison shows that the proposed return model, which incorporates stochastic drift together with systematic and idiosyncratic jump risks, achieves better empirical fit than benchmark models that omit either stochastic drift or jump risk, as measured by the AIC and BIC criteria. Strategy comparisons under realized price paths show that the rolling-horizon strategy achieves higher terminal wealth and a higher return per unit of gross risky exposure, although it also involves larger risky exposure and higher turnover. Sensitivity analyses further indicate that the monitoring frequency, cash-flow costs, rebalancing costs, the safety-level coefficient, the tail probability, and the specification of the risk amplification coefficient all affect portfolio exposure and wealth performance. These results suggest that the proposed framework provides a flexible approach to dynamic asset allocation under long-term capital injections and downside-risk control.

title: Towards Proactive Hybrid Management (PHM): A Conceptual Framework for Human-AI-Algorithmic Integration in Decision-Making

detail.title: Towards Proactive Hybrid Management (PHM): A Conceptual Framework for Human-AI-Algorithmic Integration in Decision-Making

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest

detail.abstract: This paper presents Proactive Hybrid Management (PHM) as a conceptual management framework that reorganizes the relationship between human judgment, artificial intelligence, and algorithmic logic within a proactively aware temporal context. PHM addresses a persistent gap in contemporary management: the disconnect between the abundance of analytical tools and the quality and timing of decisions. Unlike existing frameworks such as Decision Support Systems, Algorithmic Management, and Human-in-the-Loop models — which treat these three elements separately — PHM integrates them within a single coherent framework that explicitly separates analytical responsibility from decision responsibility, while preserving human accountability as non-transferable. The paper draws on a partial applied case from a property management context to illustrate how the absence of methodological maturity leads to automation failure. PHM is positioned not as a replacement for existing frameworks, but as a unifying approach that assigns time its natural place within the decision cycle.

title: Similarity-Based Expectations and Mutual Fund Performance: Evidence from Chinese Mutual Funds
affiliations: Southwestern University of Finance and Economics (SWUFE) - China Center for Behavior Economics and Finance, Southwestern University of Finance and Economics, Southwestern University of Finance and Economics and

detail.title: Similarity-Based Expectations and Mutual Fund Performance: Evidence from Chinese Mutual Funds
detail.abstract: We examine whether similarity-based expectations are related to mutual fund performance in China. Using open-end equity funds from 2005 to 2025, we construct a fund-level similarity-based return expectation measure (SBE) that weights past fund-months by their similarity to the current state and uses the returns that followed those states as a proxy for investors' expectations. We find that SBE positively predicts future fund returns, and the result is robust to alternative similarity windows, performance measures, and model specifications. The predictive relation is stronger for funds with low institutional ownership, in high-sentiment periods, and among funds with low historical maximum returns. We further provide mechanism evidence on investor flows, price pressure, and strategic catering by fund managers. Our findings extend the similarity-based framework from stock market to delegated portfolio management and document that investors' reliance on similar past states is related to capital allocation and subsequent mutual fund performance.

title: A Tonnage Tax Regime for Venezuelan Maritime Hydrocarbon Transport: The Special Regime of Energy Maritime Tonnage (RETME) Denominated in Special Drawing Rights

detail.title: A Tonnage Tax Regime for Venezuelan Maritime Hydrocarbon Transport: The Special Regime of Energy Maritime Tonnage (RETME) Denominated in Special Drawing Rights

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that he has no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this study because it does not involve human participants, patients, clinical data, or animal subjects. The paper is based on legal, fiscal, policy, and publicly available documentary sources.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: This paper proposes a Special Regime of Energy Maritime Tonnage (Régimen Especial de Tonelaje Marítimo Energético, RETME) for Venezuelan hydrocarbon maritime transport, replacing ordinary corporate income taxation for qualifying shipping activity with an objective daily levy based on a vessel’s net tonnage. The paper reviews five comparative tonnage tax regimes (the general European Union framework, and the British, Spanish, Dutch, and Greek models), proposes a hybrid Venezuelan design combining the Spanish technical base, British training obligations, Dutch maritime-cluster logic, and Greek flexibility on flag requirements, and develops an original quantitative model expressing tax liability in International Monetary Fund Special Drawing Rights (SDR/XDR) rather than a depreciating national currency. Using a reference export volume of 1.25 million barrels per day (Reuters, 2026) and standard Aframax-class vessel parameters, the model estimates annual per-vessel liability of 47,997.50 SDR and presents three operating-cycle scenarios yielding estimated annual direct collection between approximately 2.0 million and 5.6 million SDR, depending on route length. The paper argues that fiscal reform is the necessary starting point for Venezuelan maritime modernization, and that tax incentives must be conditioned on verifiable investment, employment, and transparency commitments rather than granted unconditionally.

title: An Analysis of the 2026 EU Avoidance Rules and an Evaluation against the UNCITRAL Legislative Guide on Insolvency
affiliations: University of Leeds

detail.title: An Analysis of the 2026 EU Avoidance Rules and an Evaluation against the UNCITRAL Legislative Guide on Insolvency

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. The author has no personal, professional, or financial relationships that could be perceived to have influenced the research, analysis, or conclusions presented in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this research. The study is based exclusively on doctrinal legal analysis of legislation, case law, and academic literature and did not involve human participants, personal data, or animal subjects.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant, funding, or financial support from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract:
This article provides the first systematic, principle-based evaluation of the European Union's 2026 Directive harmonising transaction avoidance rules, using the UNCITRAL Legislative Guide on Insolvency as an external normative benchmark. It argues that the Directive embodies a structurally unstable model of minimum harmonisation, which simultaneously proclaims convergence while entrenching doctrinal divergence through indeterminate concepts, excessive reliance on subjective criteria, and weak coordination with the EU's cross-border insolvency framework. Methodologically, the article develops a replicable framework for assessing EU insolvency harmonisation against internationally recognised principles, demonstrating how principle-based soft-law instruments can serve as functional benchmarks for testing legislative coherence. Substantively, it shows that although the Directive reinforces core distributive values such as creditor equality and estate preservation, it fails to secure legal certainty, procedural efficiency, and cross-border predictability, thereby undermining its own internal market objectives. The article advances a set of doctrinal and institutional reforms, including the reintroduction of constructive knowledge, the development of structured evidentiary presumptions, and the adoption of empirically grounded suspect periods. More broadly, it argues that effective harmonisation in EU insolvency law requires a shift from formal convergence to precise functional equivalence informed by empirical and comparative evidence. The findings have implications not only for the implementation of the Directive but also for the future design of EU insolvency law within the Capital Markets Union.

IMPORTANT: This version is a working paper and has not been peer reviewed. This paper has been submitted to the European Business Organisation Law Review and is currently under review.

title: How Clubs Evaluate Sporting Directors: Evidence from Executive Turnover in English Professional Football
affiliations: University of Lausanne

detail.title: How Clubs Evaluate Sporting Directors: Evidence from Executive Turnover in English Professional Football
detail.abstract: Professional football clubs have increasingly separated recruitment and squad building from coaching by creating the sporting director role, yet dismissal risk still concentrates on the coach rather than the executive who holds many of these decision rights. Using a counting process survival dataset of sporting director tenures in English professional football, we test whether dismissal is predicted by team results, measured as deviation from expected league position, or by value creation through recruitment, measured as squad market value change attributable to the sporting director. Team results predict dismissal hazard consistently across every specification. Value creation predicts it under exactly one of three operationalizations: squad value growth measured against the club's own wage bill growth, associated with substantially lower hazard. Squad value growth measured against peers, and that same measure corrected for the season's transfer trading, show no relationship, even though the corrected measure was built specifically to fix the standard measure's clearest flaw. The three measures are largely uncorrelated with each other, so the pattern reflects what a club's own reporting can construct rather than sample composition or measurement accuracy. Boards appear to reward what they can already measure from their own records, not what the role was created to deliver: reallocating decision rights to a new executive role does not automatically move accountability with it.

title: Science-Based Grounds of Environmental Litigation for Air Pollution
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Science-Based Grounds of Environmental Litigation for Air Pollution

declarations.declarationOfInterest: There are no conflicts of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: not applicable
declarations.funderStatement: No funding received.

detail.abstract:
Following initial overview sections on Polluters Pay Principle and Environmental Law, Environmental Litigation is explored in depth. Both academic research and recent news articles in a rapidly-changing field were studied. Scientific evidence of grounds for litigation is explored including right to a sustainable environment, toxic co-pollutants, attribution science, deception, externalized costs, and affordability. Criminal, civil, and combined trials of pollution cases are explored. Strategies for improving outcomes of litigation are proposed. Google Scholar, SSRN, and the media were searched from January 2020 to June 2026.
This article focuses almost entirely on air pollution including Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions that cause climate change and toxic airborne co-pollutants from combustion of fossil fuels. Effective means for cleaning up the atmosphere have not been discovered. Inventions have been made to clear the air of GHGs and toxics, but these are either ineffective or increase air pollution.1,2,3 The Social Cost of Carbon (SCC), our best quantitative estimate of comprehensive damages, is applied to analyses of policies, fines, judgments, and penalties.

title: Should the ECB Incorporate Home Values into its Target Price Index? The Challenge of Cross-Country Heterogeneity
affiliations: Wichita State University - W. Frank Barton School of Business

detail.title: Should the ECB Incorporate Home Values into its Target Price Index? The Challenge of Cross-Country Heterogeneity
detail.abstract: Unlike most central banks, the ECB does not include a measure of owner-occupied housing (OOH) in its target price index. There have been calls to add such a measure to the target, with advocates arguing that including OOH would increase the central banks' credibility and allow the ECB to lean against housing bubbles. There are several technical issues regarding how an OOH can be added to the target price index. One key issue that has not been thoroughly examined is the dispersion of prices across euro countries. An "optimal currency area" would ideally have highly cohesive inflation across the different countries in the monetary union. If, instead, inflation is highly variable across countries, the ECB will face a difficult policy challenge. If inflation is rising in some nations, but below target in others, the appropriate (loose) policy for the low inflation countries will exacerbate price instability in the higher inflation countries. Indeed, even without an OOH, this geographic dispersion has been a challenge for the euro. Any OOH added to the ECBs' target will be a function of house prices. Using a set of house price indices developed with the intent of fostering crosscountry comparability, we compare the geographic variability in these house prices with that of the current ECB target, the Harmonized Index of Consumer Prices (HICP). Using a variety of measures we find individual country deviations of house prices from their sample-wide means tend to be much more geographically heterogeneous than those of the HICP index. Moreover, such deviations tend to be much more persistent through time than those of the HICP. Other measures indicate greater cyclical cohesion for the HICP than house prices across euro countries. While these results do not definitively prove it would be a mistake for the ECB to adopt an OOH in its target index, they do fit into a new literature which indicates it is optimal for central banks to ignore house prices when conducting monetary policy.

title: Neuroanthropological Economics: The Political Economy of Black South African Unemployment, Economic Exclusion, and Xenophobia Through the Nae Lens

detail.title: Neuroanthropological Economics: The Political Economy of Black South African Unemployment, Economic Exclusion, and Xenophobia Through the Nae Lens
detail.abstract:
Thirty years after the formal end of apartheid, Black South Africans face an unemployment rate of 35.8% — more than five times the 6.7% rate for white South Africans — and the country has become a recurring site of xenophobic violence against African migrants. Standard political economy explanations attribute these phenomena to structural inequality, labour market failures, and elite capture of redistributive policies. These explanations are accurate but incomplete. They describe the political and economic architecture of exclusion without explaining why Black South Africans, despite high motivation and survival intelligence, consistently fail to convert available economic opportunities into sustained enterprise; why three decades of Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment (BBBEE) have enriched a narrow political elite while leaving the majority economically immobile; and why economic frustration is displaced onto African migrants rather than channelled into collective political and economic action.
This article applies Neuroanthropological Economics (NAE) to close this explanatory gap. NAE's central claim — that economic behaviour is the simultaneous product of neurobiological substrates, culturally-specific practices, and historically-embodied trauma — generates a more complete account of Black South African economic exclusion than political economy or behavioural economics alone can provide. We argue that: (1) the chronic cortisol load produced by apartheid-era institutional violence and sustained by post-apartheid poverty creates a neuro cultural trap in which Black South Africans are neurobiologically predisposed toward short-term economic decisions, undermining enterprise formation; (2) BBBEE's failure reflects a structural mismatch between the Ubuntu-rooted collective economic logic of the Black majority and the individualistic, financialised architecture of empowerment policy; (3) xenophobia is not a cultural pathology but a predictable product of cortisol-driven amygdala hyperreactivity under conditions of chronic scarcity and institutional betrayal — a frustration-aggression-displacement circuit activated when economic failure cannot be attributed to its structural causes. NAE proposes that resolving these interlocked crises requires not merely redistributive policy, but neuro-culturally aligned economic institutions that reduce chronic cortisol, activate oxytocin-mediated collective trust, and replace BBBEE's elite-capture architecture with cooperative frameworks scoring ≥80% on the Cultural Appropriateness Score.
The article also provides an empirical corrective to the migration-blame narrative underlying movements such as Operation Dudula: migrants contribute an estimated 9% of South African GDP against a 5.1% population share, while the country’s own growth has averaged 1.1% since 2008 against a 4.2% African continental average in 2025 — a gap substantially explained by domestic infrastructure failure (Eskom load-shedding) rather than migration. It traces a compounding educational attainment gap from schooling through postgraduate and doctoral level, examines the limits of South Africa’s own crime and incarceration data for adjudicating scapegoating narratives, and proposes a Cultural-Appropriateness-Score-aligned rural cooperative programme (beef, aquaculture, diversified agriculture) as a constructive policy alternative. Twenty-two data tables, drawn from Statistics South Africa, the African Development Bank, the World Bank, the OECD/ILO, the Department of Higher Education and Training, and the Department of Correctional Services, support the analysis throughout.

title: Beyond Markowitz: Can Network Theory Improve Portfolio Diversification? A Correlation-Network and Mean-Variance Portfolio Experiment
affiliations: Instituto Tecnológico Autónomo de México (ITAM)

detail.title: Beyond Markowitz: Can Network Theory Improve Portfolio Diversification? A Correlation-Network and Mean-Variance Portfolio Experiment
detail.abstract: This paper studies whether a simple financial-network layer can complement traditional mean-variance portfolio optimization. Modern Portfolio Theory formalizes diversification through the covariance matrix: a portfolio is attractive when it improves expected return per unit of variance. Yet covariance matrices estimated from financial returns are noisy, unstable, and difficult to interpret economically. Network methods offer an alternative representation of the same correlation structure. By transforming pairwise correlations into distances and extracting a minimum spanning tree, the investor can see which assets are central, peripheral, or redundant in the portfolio's dependence structure. Using daily U.S. equity prices from an open public dataset covering Apple, Microsoft, IBM, Starbucks, and the S&P 500 benchmark from 2007 to 2016, I compare equal-weight, inverse-volatility, minimum-variance, maximum-Sharpe, and network-peripheral portfolios. The empirical exercise is deliberately framed as a methodological prototype rather than a final investment recommendation. In the out-of-sample backtest, the maximum-Sharpe portfolio delivers the highest annualized return and Sharpe ratio, while the network-peripheral portfolio produces competitive returns and a higher Sharpe ratio than the equal-weight benchmark, but with higher volatility and drawdown. The results suggest that network methods are most useful not as a replacement for Markowitz optimization, but as a diagnostic and selection layer: they reveal dependence concentration, identify structurally central assets, and create an interpretable bridge between diversification as a mathematical concept and diversification as an economic intuition.

title: Worst-of Autocallable Notes from the Investor's Perspective: Analytical Results and the Structural Drag of the Worst-of Payoff *

detail.title: Worst-of Autocallable Notes from the Investor's Perspective: Analytical Results and the Structural Drag of the Worst-of Payoff *

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Nobody and nothing has influenced this study.
declarations.funderStatement: I funded the research myself.

detail.abstract: Worst-of autocallable notes are among the most widely distributed retail structured products, yet the academic literature has focused almost exclusively on their valuation and hedging under the risk-neutral measure. This paper studies the product under the physical measure, from the perspective of the investor who holds it. Contrary to the folklore that worst-of autocallables admit no analytical treatment, we derive a hierarchy of exact and semi-analytical results under correlated geometric Brownian motion. The centerpiece is a closed-form expression for the expected worst-of log performance, which decomposes into the single-asset drift and a structural drag equal to σ p (1 − ρ)T en, where en is the expected maximum of n independent standard normals: proportional to volatility, decreasing in correlation like √ 1 − ρ, growing in basket size like √ 2 ln n, and identical under both measures. We obtain the exact worst-of distribution as a one-dimensional integral, prove first-order stochastic dominance monotonicity in correlation and basket size, solve the discretely observed autocallable exactly for one underlying, and reduce the full worst-of autocallable to low-dimensional quadrature. We then calibrate the coupon of a canonical three-year note to price at par under the riskneutral measure across a grid of volatilities, correlations, and basket sizes, and evaluate the resulting notes under the physical measure. The central finding is that the product’s quality is not a number but a mapping from preferences. Under expected utility the assessment is negative: the fair coupon is an almost perfect inverse statistic for expected-utility quality (rank correlation of −0.999 with the probability of beating the risk-free rate across the grid), and certainty equivalents for a moderately risk-averse investor are negative wherever volatility reaches 25%. But the same engineering is close to optimal for goal-reaching investors who maximize the probability of clearing a return hurdle by a horizon—the objective for which digital payoffs are theoretically optimal. Correctly selected, the note raises the probability of achieving an 8% annual target from 42% (best long basket) to 90%, and at a 12% target the worst-of feature becomes indispensable: no singleasset structure or long portfolio on the menu comes close. We derive a one-line selection rule—buy the lowest-coupon note whose slowest redemption still clears the hurdle—and show that cumulative prospect theory at standard parameters does not rationalize the product, sharpening the demand question. The worst-of autocallable emerges as a specialized but legitimate instrument: a probabilitymanufacturing technology, correctly priced for investors with threshold objectives and systematically mis-sold to wealth accumulators.

title:
The Impact of Conditional Cash Transfers on Female Postgraduate Attainment: A Difference-in-Differences Analysis
of West Bengal’s Kanyashree Prakalpa

detail.title:
The Impact of Conditional Cash Transfers on Female Postgraduate Attainment: A Difference-in-Differences Analysis
of West Bengal’s Kanyashree Prakalpa

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no personal or financial relationships with people or organizations that could have influenced this study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study relies exclusively on secondary, publicly available data from the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Government of India. As it does not involve the collection of primary data from human subjects, formal ethics committee approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: The Government of India, in the last decade, has implemented policies aimed at female empowerment and educational attainment to tackle early marriages and autonomy restrictions faced by women. This study presents the impact of one such policy, Kanyashree Prakalpa, on Female postgraduate students. While existing research has extensively evaluated its impact on schooling outcomes, the programme's impact on Tertiary education remains underresearched. This study evaluates this by using two identification strategies: a cross-state comparison using Uttarakhand as the control group, and a within-state gender comparison using West Bengal men as the control group. The cross-state difference-indifferences (DiD) yields a positive but insignificant result, and the gender DiD finds a significant positive effect. Results indicate that K3 narrowed the gender gap in postgraduate attainment within West Bengal by 4.5 percentage points. A complementary analysis finds that K1 and K2 narrowed the gender gap in undergraduate attainment by 9.6 percentage points. Robustness checks, including a placebo test, parallel trends test, and alternative control group, support the validity of the identification strategy.

title: Evolution and Future of Mission-Oriented Innovation Policy
affiliations: University of Cambridge and University of Cambridge - Institute for Manufacturing

detail.title: Evolution and Future of Mission-Oriented Innovation Policy

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no competing interests.
declarations.funderStatement: M.H. and E.O. are supported by the Gatsby Charitable Foundation research grant GAT4039.

detail.abstract: Mission-oriented innovation policy (MOIP), grand challenges, and big science have become central to contemporary industrial strategy, yet these concepts are often used interchangeably despite addressing distinct coordination problems. As innovation systems face AI-driven, fiscal, geopolitical, and technological shifts, we synthesise the evolution of these traditions and reinterpret them through a contemporary lens. We distinguish the respective roles of grand challenges, big science, and MOIP, identify the conditions under which mission-oriented innovation policy is an appropriate policy instrument, and examine how changing innovation systems reshape mission design. Beyond clarifying the conceptual foundations of MOIP, the paper offers a structured framework that helps policymakers and practitioners diagnose when mission-oriented coordination is warranted, challenge classical assumptions about mission design, and navigate alternative institutional approaches for future technologies.

title: Empires in the Mirror of Time A Hybrid Short Story on Empire Cycles and Actionable Lessons for Modern Governance
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Empires in the Mirror of Time A Hybrid Short Story on Empire Cycles and Actionable Lessons for Modern Governance
detail.abstract: Why do large-scale political systems repeatedly experience cycles of expansion, strain, and reconfiguration? Empires rarely collapse suddenly; they fail when routine pressures—fiscal strain, legitimacy loss, distorted information, and overextended commitments—interact faster than institutions can adapt. This book examines a millennium of large-scale governance systems to identify recurring failure modes and the conditions under which decline can be slowed, managed, or redirected. Blending historically grounded narrative scenes with a practical governance playbook, it introduces a Five Machines framework—governance, fiscal systems, security, information, and legitimacy—that allows leaders to diagnose institutional stress before crisis becomes unavoidable. Drawing lessons from medieval federations, industrial empires, Cold War superpowers, and today’s networked world, the book translates historical patterns into stress tests, early-warning indicators, and reform roadmaps applicable to modern states, alliances, platforms, and critical infrastructure systems. Its goal is prevention: improving institutional resilience without requiring catastrophe to justify reform.

title: Inter-Cohort Migration Competition: Effects on the Labor Market and Political Attitudes at the Regional EU Level

detail.title: Inter-Cohort Migration Competition: Effects on the Labor Market and Political Attitudes at the Regional EU Level

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This was my Bachelor's Thesis which I completed at Bocconi University during the course of my International Economics course, under the supervision of Professor Tito Boeri.
declarations.funderStatement: There was no funding.

detail.abstract: This thesis investigates whether immigration creates competition not only between migrants and natives, but also among migrants who have arrived at different points in time, and whether this is also mirrored in changes in political attitudes over the duration of stay in the host country. This complementary analysis is performed using panel data from Eurostat and two survey rounds from the European Social Survey (ESS), in the European Union (EU), at regional and national level respectively. For the first part, concerning labor market outcomes, over the period 2000-2024, contemporaneous shares of migrants present on the labor market are not significant. However, lagged shares are, highlighting the delayed competition effect that requires time to adjust through various channels. A 10-percentage-point increase in the oneyear lagged migrant share is associated with a decline of roughly 2.95 percentage points in the employment rate of foreign citizens, while the corresponding two-year lag implies a decline of about 3.53 percentage points. When controlling for skill heterogeneity, the effects appear stronger for the lower and medium segments of the education distribution. Robustness and endogeneity checks broadly confirm these results. For the second part, concerning changes in political attitudes according to duration of stay, which uses the ESS, the framing of the question is key: when inquiring about immigration along the economic dimension, migrants that have been in the host country for shorter periods of time seem to be more open than those who are or have been settled for longer. Concerning cultural impact and general openness, results are similar, but statistically weaker. Finally, a bridge exercise is conducted, which links the lagged migrant pressure to migrants' political attitudes. While this yields weaker results statistically, it is nevertheless helpful thanks to its informative nature, as it suggests that the labor market effect and the attitudinal evidence work in compatible and similar directions. Overall, this thesis contributes to assessing the impact of inter-migrant competition, both from an economic and social perspective, which should allow for better policymaking outcomes when deliberating on the impact of immigration for EU states.

title: Interchange Fees in Payment Networks: Implications for Prices, Profits, and Welfare
affiliations: Consumer Finance Institute, Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia, Drexel University and Bates White, LLC

detail.title: Interchange Fees in Payment Networks: Implications for Prices, Profits, and Welfare
detail.abstract: We study a two-sided payment card market with elastic demand, merchant market power, ad valorem fees and rewards, and cash. Interchange fees, rewards, and credit card adoption generate tax wedges between consumer and merchant prices, with different incidence for cash and card users. Contrary to conventional wisdom, a modest interchange fee cap raises rewards when demand is relatively inelastic and lowers them when demand is relatively elastic. Under constant elasticity, the cap lowers prices for both consumer groups, benefits merchants, and reduces network profits. With linear demand, credit card users still gain, but cash users can lose through cross subsidization and imperfect pass-through.

title: Exploring Pockets of Predictability in Islamic Capital Markets: The Roles of Energy Commodities and Systematic Uncertainty
affiliations: University of Malaya (UM)

detail.title: Exploring Pockets of Predictability in Islamic Capital Markets: The Roles of Energy Commodities and Systematic Uncertainty
detail.abstract:
This paper investigates the time-varying, episodic predictability of Shariah-compliant (SC) stock premiums across six major global Islamic Capital Markets (ICMs) (Malaysia, Indonesia, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Qatar, and the United Arab Emirates (UAE)). Moving beyond static, constant-coefficient regressions that analyze predictability on average, we draw on macro-behavioral foundations of information rigidity and sticky expectations to examine localized dynamic stock market states. Methodologically, we implement the nonparametric, time-varying parameter kernel regression framework of Farmer, Schmidt, and Timmermann (2024), regularized via Zellner's G-prior Bayesian shrinkage and a strict minimum-duration validator to isolate out-of-sample predictability pockets ex-ante. The predictor matrix decomposes performance across traditional macroeconomic proxies and alternative shifters, evaluating active market-timing allocations across unrestricted and constrained forecasting regimes. Furthermore, we deploy local projections to structurally trace the lifespan of post-shock informational drifts. 
Our empirical results reveal a stark structural divergence across the analyzed indices: global uncertainty indices (the VIX) require flexible, unrestricted mandates to capture market-timing premiums during systemic contagion shocks, whereas real-sector commodity proxies (WTI, Brent Crude, and LNG) operate as robust, restriction-invariant shifters heavily bound to corporate cashflows. Imposing economic sign boundaries systematically regularizes energy and currency signals, muting out-of-pocket variance inflation while concentrating annualized alphas within in-pocket windows. These findings demonstrate that because SC stocks are disconnected from conventional credit cycles and speculative leverage, their premiums act as direct conduits to the physical economy. Ultimately, the paper provides a predictability framework for investors interested in the ICM, showing that active regime awareness secures both Shariah mandate integrity and superior out-of-sample risk-adjusted returns.

title: Why Do Exchange Rate Movements Often Fail to Generate Trade Adjustment? Geopolitical Risk, Exchange Rate Persistence, and the Limits of Price-Based Trade Adjustment

detail.title: Why Do Exchange Rate Movements Often Fail to Generate Trade Adjustment? Geopolitical Risk, Exchange Rate Persistence, and the Limits of Price-Based Trade Adjustment
detail.abstract: Why do exchange rate movements often fail to generate trade adjustment? Using a structural gravity model estimated by Poisson pseudomaximum-likelihood on a bilateral panel of G10 and euro-area economies over 1994-2025, with one-year lagged exchange rate components as the preferred specification, I find: first-and most robustly-that persistent exchange rate movements have no detectable effect on bilateral exports, a null result confirmed across Christiano-Fitzgerald, Hodrick-Prescott, and Hamilton decompositions, all country-exclusion exercises, and all crisis-period subsamples, consistent with the hysteresis literature on trade inertia in advanced economies; second, that transitory exchange rate movements show a positive contemporaneous association with trade that disappears once lagged, most plausibly reflecting common macroeconomic shocks; and third, that geopolitical risk appears to condition the exchange rate-trade relationship-the interaction between the persistent exchange rate component and the Caldara-Iacoviello GPR index is positive and significant, with evidence that the sign of the exchange rate effect reverses at high GPR, as appreciation rather than depreciation becomes associated with higher exports during periods of geopolitical stress. Economic magnitudes remain modest throughout (below 2% for a one-standard-deviation movement). These findings suggest that exchange rate flexibility is an unreliable trade-adjustment mechanism in advanced economies. The paper identifies the existence of a geopolitical conditioning effect but not the precise mechanism through which it operates.

title: The Conflicting Relation between Militarism and Transparency in Brazil: Analysis of Freedom of Information Requests and Declassification of Documents
affiliations: and Universidade Federal de Pernambuco - Faculdade de Direito do Recife

detail.title: The Conflicting Relation between Militarism and Transparency in Brazil: Analysis of Freedom of Information Requests and Declassification of Documents
detail.abstract: How military institutions in Brazil deal with transparency duties and what does this represent from the militarism ethos and its relation with democracy, state and society? This research aims to answer this problem, so as to describe how military institutions in Brazil deal with transparency duties and what does this represent from the militarism ethos and its relation with democracy, the state and society. Historically, militaries have had a complex relation with society and the state in Brazil, often seeking to control power dynamics. Most recently, democratic controls have been strengthened, but militaries still perpetuate practices of closing. The research shows that the armed forces and the Ministry of Defense still try to fit in the current legal order a vision in which militaries legitimize themselves and are different from other public agents, without the same accountability duties. This is reinforced by the lack of action from control bodies, opening the way to opportunistic usage of restrictions of private information and of risk to national security in public interest documents.

title: Artificial Intelligence, Warfare, and the Transformation of Global Security
affiliations: and Nigerian Army University Biu,  Borno, Nigeria

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence, Warfare, and the Transformation of Global Security
detail.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into military and security domains represents one of the most consequential transformations in the character of contemporary warfare with significant import in the transformation of global security. This paper critically examined AI's impact on global security and conflict resolution, interrogating both its operational efficiencies and its systemic risks to international order. AI-enabled technologies, including autonomous weapons systems, predictive analytics, and cyber-defence algorithms, are fundamentally reconfiguring the dynamics of deterrence, escalation, and peacekeeping. Drawing on evidence from recent conflict case studies and a review of contemporary literature, this paper foregrounds the dual-use dilemma at the heart of military AI: while precision targeting, accelerated decision-making, and enhanced surveillance offer measurable tactical advantages, they simultaneously introduce risks of algorithmic bias, cyber vulnerability, and uncontrolled escalation. This is compounded by the progressive erosion of meaningful human oversight. Current projections indicate that within the next decade, over 60 per cent of major military powers will have embedded AI within their command-and-control systems, raising urgent questions of compliance with international humanitarian law and the ethical limits of lethal autonomy. The paper further examines AI's constructive potential in conflict resolution, particularly through predictive peacekeeping frameworks and automated early-warning systems that may strengthen diplomatic and crisismanagement architectures. The study ultimately argues that AI's trajectory in warfare is neither inherently destabilising nor inevitably violent. Its strategic consequences are determined by the governance frameworks, deployment decisions, and international cooperative arrangements within which it operates. Effective regulation sustained human control, and equitable access between technologically advanced and developing states remains the decisive variable.

title: Youth Unemployment and Political Instability in Nigeria: Electoral Violence, Government Legitimacy, and Lessons for Emerging Economies
affiliations: Institute of Management and Technology (IMT), Enugu

detail.title: Youth Unemployment and Political Instability in Nigeria: Electoral Violence, Government Legitimacy, and Lessons for Emerging Economies

declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is based entirely on secondary data obtained from publicly available and credible sources, including World Bank, National Bureau of Statistics, published academic articles, etc.. No human participants or personally identifiable information were involved in the research. As such, ethical approval and informed consent were not required.
declarations.funderStatement: Self

detail.abstract: This study examined the relationship between youth unemployment and political instability in Nigeria, focusing on electoral violence and government legitimacy between 2015 and 2025. The study adopted a qualitative research design and employed thematic analysis of secondary data obtained from National Bureau of Statistics reports, government publications, scholarly literature, and reports of national and international development organizations while a PESTEL analysis was utilized to provide broader insight into the political, economic, social, technological, environmental, and legal factors shaping youth unemployment and political instability in Nigeria. Findings revealed that persistent youth unemployment contributed significantly to electoral violence by increasing the vulnerability of youths to political manipulation, thuggery, and electionrelated unrest. The study concludes that the inability of the economic system to generate adequate employment opportunities for young people poses a serious threat to democratic governance and social cohesion. The study recommends the adoption of sustainable job creation strategies, expansion of skills acquisition, entrepreneurship programmes, increased youth inclusion in governance and decision-making processes to strengthen political stability and enhance public confidence in government. The findings provide valuable lessons for other emerging economies facing similar youth unemployment and governance challenges.

title: The Competence Gap: Civil Rights Literacy as a Professional Duty

detail.title: The Competence Gap: Civil Rights Literacy as a Professional Duty

keywords: Enyart V. National Conference of Bar Examiners

detail.abstract:
More than one in four American adults reports a disability, and every major civil rights statute adds further protected classes, so the probability that any given client falls within a protected class is a substantial share of every practice. Yet legal education and bar licensure do not require civil rights or disability law, and the duty of competence has never been read to demand it. This Essay argues that the omission is not a gap in an individual lawyer's education but a structural competence failure of the profession, and that it falls hardest on the clients least able to absorb it. The duty of competence already reaches civil rights literacy. Model Rule 1.1 requires the preparation reasonably necessary for the representation, the profession expanded that baseline to relevant technology in 2012 through commentary alone, and the doctrine that shields a lawyer's informed strategic choices does not shield a choice never made, because ignorance of a materially stronger remedy is not a strategy. The individual failure has an upstream source in accreditation and the bar examination, which set the competence baseline and omit the body of law most relevant to the most vulnerable clients. 
The contribution is a remedy located at the three points that set that baseline: the duty of competence, accreditation and bar content, and mandatory continuing education. The remedy is professional regulation, not litigation.

title: Uniform-in-τ Convergence Rates for Generative Bayesian Computation
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business and George Mason University

detail.title: Uniform-in-τ Convergence Rates for Generative Bayesian Computation
detail.abstract: Generative Bayesian Computation (GBC) recasts posterior simulation as supervised learning: a quantile neural network is trained by check-loss regression on simulated parameterdata pairs, and posterior draws are produced by pushing a uniform base variate through the learned quantile map. The sampler therefore relies on the accuracy of the estimated quantile function uniformly across quantile levels τ ∈ (0, 1), not at any single level. We show that the deep-quantile estimator at the heart of GBC inherits the minimax rates of Padilla, Tansey & Chen (2022), and we upgrade their xed-τ guarantee to a uniform-in-τ statement on a nite grid, with a constant whose growth we track explicitly to the posterior tails. Our main consequence is an amortized Wasserstein guarantee: using the one-dimensional optimal-transport identity, the GBC grid sampler attains the bound matching the deep-quantile rate up to a tail-dependent constant, without requiring control of the estimator's modulus of continuity in τ. We isolate that missing modulus as the one obstruction to the same guarantee for the fully implicit (continuous-τ) sampler, and pose it as the central open problem for GBC theory. The rate is in the simulation budget n, which the analyst controls.

title: Economic and Legal Limits on the Calculation Of Illegal Benefit in Environmental Fines: The OEFA Methodology and a Correction on Detection Probability

detail.title: Economic and Legal Limits on the Calculation Of Illegal Benefit in Environmental Fines: The OEFA Methodology and a Correction on Detection Probability

No client, company, public agency, or third party funded, commissioned, reviewed, or approved this paper. The views expressed are solely those of the author and do not necessarily represent the views of any institution, client, or employer.
