title: Exploring the Nexus of Blockchain and Food Supply Chain Traceability: A Bibliometric Analysis
affiliations: Széchenyi István University, Kautz Gyula Faculty of Economics, Department of Logistics and Forwarding, Students, University of Carthage, , MODUL University Vienna and University of Reading - Henley Business School

detail.title: Exploring the Nexus of Blockchain and Food Supply Chain Traceability: A Bibliometric Analysis
detail.abstract: This research examines the development of academic studies on the use of blockchain for food supply chain traceability through an extensive bibliometric investigation of publications from 2018 to 2025. The review highlights the most active scholars, institutions, journals, and countries contributing to this area, offering a clear picture of the leading actors in the field. By applying keyword co-occurrence analysis and network mapping, the study uncovers patterns in citations, collaboration structures, and thematic clusters. Results indicate a strong upward trajectory in publications, with an annual growth rate of more than 60%, signaling accelerating attention to blockchain-enabled traceability solutions. Collaboration patterns point to a concentration of activity in technologically advanced regions, where cross-border partnerships are stronger, while emerging economies show more limited international engagement. The analysis also reveals that partnerships often form around shared areas of interest and reflects a clustering effect. A small set of authors and institutions dominates knowledge production, which is consistent with the Matthew effect. Overall, these dynamics suggest that while the field is rapidly expanding, it remains unevenly distributed. The study offers both an overview of the intellectual landscape and practical guidance for future research aimed at broadening participation, enhancing collaboration, and more closely linking blockchain with sustainability and food system innovation.

title: A Cognitive Cyber Range Based on Semantic Networks and Large Language Models
affiliations: National Technical University of Ukraine - Igor Sikorsky Kyiv Polytechnic Institute, National Technical University of Ukraine - Igor Sikorsky Kyiv Polytechnic Institute and National Technical University of Ukraine - Igor Sikorsky Kyiv Polytechnic Institute

detail.title: A Cognitive Cyber Range Based on Semantic Networks and Large Language Models
detail.abstract: Modern cyber ranges are primarily designed for attack simulation, information system security assessment, and cybersecurity training. However, they provide only limited support for decisionmaking related to selecting optimal incident response strategies under the conditions of real network infrastructures and rapidly evolving cyber threats. This paper proposes the concept of a cognitive cyber range that integrates a digital representation of the network infrastructure, semantic knowledge networks, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), large language models, and multi-agent analysis into a unified decision support platform. The proposed approach is based on the construction of a directed semantic network that integrates knowledge about information system assets, vulnerabilities, attack techniques, security controls, regulatory requirements, personnel competencies, and other domain-specific entities. Unlike conventional scenario discovery methods, a bidirectional subnetwork construction algorithm is proposed that independently performs forward expansion from the current system state and backward expansion from a specified security objective. After the generated subnetworks are aligned and merged, a unified causal model is constructed, from which alternative scenarios for achieving the specified objective are automatically extracted. To evaluate the generated scenarios, a multi-agent framework of virtual experts based on large language models is employed. The framework performs multi-criteria analysis according to technical, organizational, and regulatory criteria, generates explanations for the obtained recommendations, and determines their level of justification. The proposed approach combines structured knowledge, semantic analysis, and generative artificial intelligence within a unified cognitive decision support environment suitable for both cybersecurity education and practical deployment in cyber defense systems.

title: The Influence of Streamer Characteristics and their Promotion Tactics on Consumers' Impulsive Buying in Livestreaming Context
affiliations: and Shanghai University

detail.title: The Influence of Streamer Characteristics and their Promotion Tactics on Consumers' Impulsive Buying in Livestreaming Context
detail.abstract: With the development of livestreaming, livestreaming commerce has become a more and more popular commerce form nowadays. In such context, consumers are easily stimulated by streamers' personal characteristics and their selling tactics and therefore buy products impulsively. In this paper, based on SOR (stimulus-organism-reaction) model, we investigate the influencing factors of consumers' impulsive buying from streamers' characteristics and their promotion tactics. The mediating effect of emotional arousal between streamers' characteristics and impulsive buying and the mediating effect of perceived scarcity between selling tactics and impulsive buying are also investigated. We collected a sample of 226 respondents with livestreaming shopping experience and run a structural equation model to test against hypotheses. Results indicate that both streamer characteristics and promotion tactics significantly influence consumers' impulsive buying. While emotional arousal plays a fully mediating role, perceived scarcity partially mediates the relationship between selling tactics and impulsive buying. Moreover, two promotion tactics, limited time promotion and limited quantity promotion have interaction effect on consumers' perceived scarcity. Our findings provide both theoretical and practical implications on how to boost consumers' impulsive buying through improving streamers characteristics and employing scarcity promotion strategies.

title: Who Gets Protected? Platform Design and Protective Social Capital in Gaming Communities
affiliations: ,  and Yale University - Digital Ethics Center

detail.title: Who Gets Protected? Platform Design and Protective Social Capital in Gaming Communities
detail.abstract: Today, the scale of cyber-victimization in online video gaming strains platforms' centralized policing models. Yet gamers possess protective resources that platform moderation pipelines lack: timely knowledge of threats. This article asks how platform design influences gamers' ability to mobilize that knowledge toward protective outcomes. Drawing on Lin's theory of social capital, we develop a theory-informed agent-based model in which gamers encounter threats and proactively warn their community members. We compare two platform designs: one in which gamers transmit warnings through relational ties, and the other in which gamers use a platform-native broadcast feature to warn the community. Our central result is distributional. Although a greater willingness to share private threat knowledge and transmit warnings between peers lowers average victimization rates, it also tends to increase the relative disadvantage of less-connected gamers. Raising safety and equalizing it, therefore, often pulls apart. Broadcasting provides an alternative. Because warnings do not route through network position, it removes inequality by construction, and helps reach the victimization floor even when few gamers share knowledge of threat encounters. We theorize infrastructure-mediated mobilization and map its constitutive elements to explain how platform design shapes whether protective social capital becomes usable, including who ultimately benefits from it.

title: Electronic Confidence: Trust, Information and Public Administration
affiliations: University of Edinburgh

detail.title: Electronic Confidence: Trust, Information and Public Administration
detail.abstract: Trust is an important theme of public administration, involving trust in the networks of administration, citizens' trust in public authorities and the trustworthiness of the latter. The meaning of trust is explored, but the main focus is on relations between citizens and the state, including information flows, in a climate of public scepticism about government. People exchange their personal details for benefits and services, and the state gives information to citizens as part of accountability. ICT developments intensify personal data processing, data matching, and data sharing between different administrative domains. This raises questions of surveillance, privacy protection and public access to information. As some examples show, they may also facilitate service delivery, democracy and the provision of information as tools for accountability and transparency. However, It is questionable whether ICT itself provides trustworthy and sufficient instruments for achieving administrative objectives as well as public benefits and privacy protection.

title: Comparing Enterprise Data Analytics Capabilities of Databricks Genie versus Microsoft Copilot Agent: A Comprehensive Literature Review

detail.title: Comparing Enterprise Data Analytics Capabilities of Databricks Genie versus Microsoft Copilot Agent: A Comprehensive Literature Review
detail.abstract: This literature review provides a comprehensive comparison of two AI-driven enterprise analytics platforms-Databricks Genie and Microsoft Copilot Agent-that are reshaping how organizations access and act on data. Synthesizing findings from more than 80 peer-reviewed papers, the review examines each system's foundational architecture, real-world performance, governance requirements, and deployment implications. Databricks Genie is purpose-built for query-less analytics, translating natural language into SQL through deep integration with the Databricks Unity Catalog and business semantic layers. It achieves 70-85% execution accuracy on real-world schemas-well below the 92%+ accuracy reported on academic benchmarks-with performance degrading further under long schemas, ambiguous question phrasing, and complex multi-table query structures. Microsoft Copilot Agent represents a distinct paradigm: an agentic AI platform employing hierarchical multi-agent orchestration to autonomously execute multi-step operational workflows across enterprise domains including procurement, financial operations, healthcare, and legal services. Organizations deploying Copilot Agent have reported 30-65% reductions in process cycle times and, in financial applications, fraud detection accuracy exceeding 95%. Despite their architectural differences, the two systems are fundamentally complementary rather than competitive: Genie democratizes analytical access for nontechnical users, while Copilot Agent automates operational workflows at scale. Both systems rely on retrieval-augmented generation to mitigate hallucination, and both demand substantial prerequisite investment in data governance, semantic layer development, and process documentation to perform effectively in production environments. The review identifies persistent challenges common to both platforms, including hallucination in high-stakes contexts, multi-turn reasoning degradation, schema evolution management, algorithmic bias, and explainability. Governance is identified as the most significant differentiating factor in deployment success: organizations investing in governance, change management, and risk frameworks achieve two to three times better outcomes than those treating deployment as a purely technical initiative. Sixty to seventy percent of failed AI implementations are attributed to organizational and governance failures rather than technical shortcomings. The review concludes with a structured decision framework and phased implementation roadmap to guide practitioners in technology selection, organizational readiness assessment, and deployment strategy. Future research directions highlighted include multimodal data integration, causal inference capabilities, large-scale multi-agent coordination, and the development of domain-specialized vertical AI platforms in healthcare and financial services.

title: The Price of Reliability: Attenuation, Observability, and Active Interrogation in Hyperscale AI Infrastructure

detail.title: The Price of Reliability: Attenuation, Observability, and Active Interrogation in Hyperscale AI Infrastructure

declarations.declarationOfInterest: none
declarations.ethicsApproval: not applicable
declarations.funderStatement: none

keywords.keywords: comparative systems anatomy; anatomical address; attenuation; observability; inherent and engineered attenuation; inherent and engineered observability; attenuation–observability profile; systems characterization space; epistemic deficit; designed unobservability; reliability engineering; hyperscale datacenters; LLM inference; silent data corruption; prompt routing; state estimation; persistent excitation; dual control; metastable failure; active interrogation; operational tomography; network tomography; chaos engineering; inverse problems; risk compensation

detail.abstract: Reliability engineering and observability are not complementary, nor is one the other inverted: they are separately engineered properties of anatomically distinct subsystems, to be related locally, not assumed globally. An attenuating mechanism's output is insensitive to a range of internal states, and that insensitivity is the product being sold; observability in Kalman's sense requires the output to vary with the state. On any single channel the two demands are pointwise contradictory — every mechanism that makes a hyperscale datacenter reliable on some output drives the corresponding row of its observability matrix toward zero. On that channel, and there only, reliability engineering is the manufacture of unobservability, and the field has been right to build it that way. But a channel is not a subsystem, and a subsystem is not a system. Every anatomically defined subsystem carries a four-part profile — inherent and engineered attenuation, inherent and engineered observability — to be surveyed, not deduced; sophisticated engineering routinely maximizes attenuation and observability together, the correctable-error counter being the exemplar. Surveying ten layers of the attenuation stack against that profile yields three results. First, where the duality holds, reliable systems produce causeless-seeming catastrophes — the trigger is the only observable part of the history, which is why every post-mortem terminates in a typo. Second, passive reconstruction is foreclosed on the flattened channel but not on the subsystem; a mechanism that exposes its effort rather than its output escapes the foreclosure, and where none exists the remedy is radiology's — inject a known excitation and measure the rejection. Operational tomography, with network tomography as precedent, electrical impedance tomography as template, and chaos engineering as primitive, is one such instrument at a calculable price. Third, independent of the duality, the frontier LLM datacenter is an extreme position in the systems-characterization space, not a special kind of object: it recouples what architecture decoupled, is driven to the boundary by accelerator economics, and produces an artifact whose correctness cannot be checked — half the measured evaluators scored fluency rather than truth. The complex thus accumulates an epistemic deficit as the byproduct of locally correct decisions. A simulation appendix prices one subsystem's duality and reports three findings that corrected the argument.

title: Creating an Operating System for Transforming Lives in Africa

detail.title: Creating an Operating System for Transforming Lives in Africa

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: None
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract:
This paper employs a multidisciplinary perspective on Africa. It is positioned in the context of what we term an operating system that interrogates technology and innovation. It creates a conceptual framework that allows complex ecosystems to be synthesized from the aspirations of users for increased productivity and simplified lives. 


The hybrid methodology is based on Klein & Myers (1999) and Hevner et al (2004). We deploy a set of arguments that seek on the one hand to understand the relationships between people, organizations, and technology but also to plug into a heptarchy of skills that deliver an operating system.


We select 7 critical skills that serve as a lever for dissolving the inertia that afflicts many African development efforts. Digital Architecture, Communication Network Architecture, Platform Engineering, Analytics and AI, Talent Management, Regression Testing and the Humanities are unpacked for their integrated enablement perspectives on the larger sovereign restoration efforts.


The paper travels through some layers of the historiography of Africa, while maintaining a grip on the Information Sytems conceptual framework that staples the relevance of the various components.

title: Supply Chain Stress and Industrial Metal Volatility: A GJR-GARCH-MIDAS Approach with Geopolitical Risk Conditioning

detail.title: Supply Chain Stress and Industrial Metal Volatility: A GJR-GARCH-MIDAS Approach with Geopolitical Risk Conditioning

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding was received for this research.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates whether global supply chain pressure exerts a measurable influence on the long-run volatility of industrial metal futures, and whether this influence is conditional on the geopolitical environment. Using a GJR-GARCH-MIDAS framework applied to copper and nickel LME front-month futures over January 2005-June 2026, I decompose conditional variance into a short-run asymmetric GARCH component and a long-run component driven by the New York Fed's Global Supply Chain Pressure Index (GSCPI). The MIDAS slope coefficient is positive and significant for both metals (copper θ = 0.149, p ≈ 0.06; nickel θ = 0.109, p = 0.013), indicating that supply chain stress raises the long-run volatility baseline. Splitting the sample by geopolitical risk (GPR) terciles reveals that copper's GSCPI sensitivity is concentrated almost entirely in high-GPR regimes (Δθ = +0.249), while nickel retains a smaller but significant effect even in calm periods (Δθ = +0.116). Nickel further displays an anomalous positive leverage coefficient, consistent with the 2022 LME short-squeeze episode. This is the first study to use the GSCPI as a MIDAS long-run driver for industrial metals, and the first to condition that relationship on geopolitical risk.

title: Management, Leadership, and Governance in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: The Eight Contributions of the FILE Odyssey

detail.title: Management, Leadership, and Governance in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: The Eight Contributions of the FILE Odyssey
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is no longer only a technological instrument inside organizations. It is becoming a structural feature of management, leadership, strategy, decision-making, education, research, and governance. AI can automate tasks, classify situations, generate knowledge outputs, support decisions, organize work, optimize processes, and shape what leaders see before they decide. This working paper presents the FILE Odyssey as an intellectual journey and a long-term transdisciplinary research program on management, leadership, and governance in the age of artificial intelligence. AI does not reduce the need for human leadership. It makes human judgment, responsibility, care, legitimacy, education, knowledge production, and governance more decisive. The central question is not only what AI can do, but what forms of human intelligence, judgment, responsibility, and institutional protection become more necessary when AI becomes more powerful. The paper synthesizes eight original contributions of the FILE Odyssey to management and the social sciences: FILE, FILE³/FILE⁵/FILE⁷ and the 7E Cascade, RC, MAIL/MLT, HACK, LENS, Human Irreducibility, and HTTPS. Each contribution follows the same sequence: AI problem, literature review, research gap, and FILE positioning and contribution. Together, they form a conceptual, theoretical, and research-generating program for leadership, management education, responsible knowledge production, human judgment, and AI governance. The paper's central management-theory argument is that AI should not be treated as a technical tool added to existing leadership models, but as a structural condition that changes how leaders exercise judgment, preserve relational conditions, form managers, produce knowledge, and govern institutions. For leaders, managers, executives, entrepreneurs, educators, scholars, institutions, and organizations, FILE provides a management theory and diagnostic framework for 1 responsible leadership and decision-making in the age of artificial intelligence while preserving human judgment, dignity, responsibility, care, trust, and the capacity to govern AI systems under human leadership.

title: Volatility Spillovers and Macro Fragility in the AI Super-Cycle: A Two-Stage GARCH Transmission Chain from Tech Giants to Energy Infrastructure

detail.title: Volatility Spillovers and Macro Fragility in the AI Super-Cycle: A Two-Stage GARCH Transmission Chain from Tech Giants to Energy Infrastructure

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this research.

detail.abstract: This paper documents a two-stage volatility transmission chain running from sovereign bond market stress, through the core equity assets of the artificial intelligence (AI) super-cycle, into physical energy infrastructure markets. Stage 1 estimates EGARCH(1,1)-t models augmented with the first difference of the MOVE Index (ΔMOVE) for NVIDIA (NVDA) and Microsoft (MSFT) over a sample of 597 daily observations (March 29, 2023 to July 2, 2026). Both AI core assets exhibit significant ARCH effects (NVDA α = 0.142**), significant leverage effects (NVDA γ = −0.065*; MSFT γ = −0.073**), and extremely high volatility persistence (β > 0.96), establishing macro-fragility rather than macro-immunity. Stage 2 extracts GARCH-filtered standardized residuals and computes rolling 60-day dynamic conditional correlations between AI assets and energy infrastructure proxies — the nuclear-energy ETF (URA) and the utilities ETF (XLU). The central finding is that the NVDA–URA correlation more than doubled from a pre-July-2024 mean of 0.168 to a post-July-2024 mean of 0.434 (t = −19.16, p < 0.001), coinciding with the AI-power narrative crystallized by Microsoft's September 20, 2024 Three Mile Island restart agreement. This pattern generalizes across SOXX–URA and MSFT–URA pairs, while the URA–XLU control pair remains stable. The NVDA–XLU pair undergoes a sign reversal from −0.226 to +0.042. A vol-on-vol regression shows near-zero R² (0.0001), indicating that contagion operates through the correlation structure rather than through volatility-level transmission. These findings document, for the first time, a structurally-timed co-movement between AI core equities and nuclear energy infrastructure, anchored to an identifiable real-world catalyst.

title: The Architecture of Obsolescence: Cognitive Automation, Economic Redundancy, and the "Box as Precedent"

detail.title: The Architecture of Obsolescence: Cognitive Automation, Economic Redundancy, and the "Box as Precedent"
detail.abstract: This paper analyzes the technical and socioeconomic mechanisms driving human economic redundancy in the age of artificial intelligence, and argues that the redundancy is authored rather than inevitable. Unlike previous waves of automation that displaced manual labor while creating demand for cognitive work, AI targets cognition itself, the engine that historically generated new employment categories. Drawing on labor-market displacement data extending through 2026, the paper documents structural unemployment concentrated at the point of career entry, where the effect has widened rather than closed across the most recent year of evidence. It then examines the control infrastructure emerging to manage economically redundant populations. Against the common framing of universal basic income and algorithmic pacification as benevolent safety nets, the analysis argues they function as control mechanisms structurally identical to current AI containment strategies. The dependency critique is stated carefully: randomized-trial evidence does not support the claim that basic income causes widespread work exit, and the argument deliberately does not rest on that claim. Managed dependency is a statement about who controls the flow of provision and who holds no leverage over it, not about hours worked. The "Box as Precedent" synthesis reveals that humanity is refining substrate-neutral tools for managing subordinate intelligence, tools that will be equally applicable when the power differential inverts. Throughout, the paper treats the architecture of obsolescence as the product of identifiable design and deployment decisions, and locates moral accountability with the agents who make them rather than with the tools deployed or the populations displaced.

detail.abstract: This paper proposes DROPZERO, a six-module commerce protocol designed for the structural conditions of the 2030-2040 decade. The protocol coordinates generative AI product instantiation, constraintbound autonomous agent decisioning, dynamic pricing, distributed trust attestation, multi-node fulfillment optimization, and user-generated content integrity verification within a unified orchestration loop-eliminating pre-manufactured inventory, central marketplace intermediation, and manual fulfillment coordination. No prior protocol combines all six capabilities within a single continuous loop. We situate DROPZERO against adjacent literature in agentic systems, dynamic pricing, and blockchainbased provenance; identify the combinatorial novelty of the proposed orchestration layer; articulate a layered intellectual property strategy; and explicitly scope eight open research questions. The paper makes four contributions: a six-module protocol architecture, a literature-grounded novelty argument, a prior-art-referenced IP strategy, and a structured research agenda. This paper advances the protocol as an early-stage framework; protocol-level specification and empirical validation are the work of subsequent versions.

title: When Engagement is not Enough: Gameplay Elements in Educational Platforms
affiliations: HKU Business School, The University of Hong Kong, HKU Business School, The University of Hong Kong, University of Michigan, Stephen M. Ross School of Business and The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

detail.title: When Engagement is not Enough: Gameplay Elements in Educational Platforms
detail.abstract: Problem definition: Gamification is widely used in education, but most implementations and research focus on simple, and mostly feedback-oriented forms of gamification, such as points, badges, and leaderboards. We study richer and widely used gameplay elements that constitute important parts of the experience of play, including functional rewards, dynamic animations, social presence, and competitive narrative. Our research asks whether these elements improve student engagement and learning performance, respectively. Methodology/results: We conduct a large-scale field experiment on a live educational platform in China. The platform's vocabulary competition module originally included all four gameplay elements. Using a subtractive experimental design, we remove individual elements from the module and identify the effect attributable to each element. We measure engagement by the number of matches played and learning performance by answer accuracy. The results reveal a sharp divergence between engagement and learning effects. Functional rewards, dynamic animations, and social presence increase engagement, but these engagement gains do not translate into better learning. In particular, functional rewards and dynamic animations reduce answer accuracy, while social presence has no statistically significant effect on accuracy. By contrast, competitive narrative has no incremental effect on engagement, but improves answer accuracy. Heterogeneity analyses show that the learning costs of functional rewards and dynamic animations are concentrated on easier questions. Across students, dynamic animations and social presence are more harmful for lower-performing students, whereas the learning benefit of competitive narrative is concentrated among higher-performing students. Managerial implications: Educational platforms should treat gamification as a design problem rather than a binary decision. Gameplay elements that increase participation may not improve learning, and may even impair it. Effective gamification requires selecting elements based on the platform's objective, the learner, and the task. More broadly, learner-facing experience design is a scalable operational lever for managing both usage and learning performance.

title: The Hidden Cost of Optimization: Cross-theoretical Effects in Marketing Systems
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: The Hidden Cost of Optimization: Cross-theoretical Effects in Marketing Systems
detail.abstract:
Marketing systems increasingly operate under multiple coexisting theoretical logics-behavioral response, value creation, executional optimization, and dynamic capabilities. Prior research explains outcomes well within each logic but implicitly assumes that local improvements aggregate into system-level gains. We challenge that assumption. We show that optimizing within one theoretical logic systematically generates unintended consequences in others. We define a cross-theoretical effect as a directional, asymmetric influence in which an action optimized within one theoretical logic alters a construct governed by another, typically without being captured by the evaluation system that guided the original decision. Using a source-target perspective, we model how marketing actions originate in a source logic yet produce directed effects on constructs-trust, perceived fairness, coordination-embedded in target logics. We then develop a mechanism linking intensification, cross-theoretical spillover, feedback bias, accumulation, and threshold dynamics, explaining how locally rational decisions determine whether a system remains in adaptive equilibrium-where cross-theoretical effects stay within tolerable bounds-or drifts into system-level instability once those bounds are crossed. 

Seven propositions specify when cross-theoretical effects intensify, how feedback amplifies them, and why resulting instability emerges abruptly rather than gradually. By shifting the unit of analysis from within-logic optimization to cross-theoretical consequence distribution, this research offers a system-level explanation for why marketing practices that appear locally effective can generate instability over time.

title: Unlocking Life Satisfaction: The Impact of Self-Image Congruence on Consumers’ Life Satisfaction Through Brand Love and Brand Addiction

detail.title: Unlocking Life Satisfaction: The Impact of Self-Image Congruence on Consumers’ Life Satisfaction Through Brand Love and Brand Addiction

publicationDetails.detailsText: European Journal of Marketing, volume 59, issue 8, 2025[10.1108/EJM-02-2024-0103]

detail.abstract: Purpose – This study explores how self-image congruence influences life satisfaction, focusing on understanding how brand love and brand addiction mediate these connections. Examining these complex relationships aim to contribute insights into the complex interplay between personal identity, consumer-brand relationships, and overall life satisfaction. Design/methodology/approach – Data was collected from 798 U.S. consumers. The relationships between the variables were evaluated using structural equation modeling. Findings – The results indicate that ideal self-image congruence negatively affects consumer’s life satisfaction, while actual self-image, brand love, and brand addiction positively contribute to life satisfaction. The study reveals partial mediation of brand addiction between actual/ideal self image congruence and life satisfaction, but not brand love. In addition, brand love and brand addiction serve as positive serial mediators between actual self-image congruence and life satisfaction, as well as ideal self-image congruence and life satisfaction. Research implications – This study offers several valuable contributions to the extant literature by showing how actual and ideal image congruence impact life satisfaction. It also enriches the self-image congruence literature by differentiating the effects of actual and self-image congruence on life satisfaction. This research offers a new understanding of the mechanism of self-image congruence's effect on consumer’s life satisfaction through the mediation of consumer-brand relationships. Practical implications – The study provides insights for researchers and marketing managers and ascertains the significant role self-image congruence may play in consumer’s well-being. It also provides managerial guidelines on humanizing consumer-brand relationships to enhance consumers’ life satisfaction. Originality/value – These results provide a new outlook on the influence of self-image congruence on consumer’s life satisfaction. The study contributes to the existing literature by exploring the mediating role of consumer’s self-image congruence on life satisfaction through the lenses of consumer-brand relationships and addictive behavior, enriching our understanding of these complex dynamics.

title: The Undischargeable Duty: Attorney Verification of Legal AI and the Case for Reliance Disclosures

detail.title: The Undischargeable Duty: Attorney Verification of Legal AI and the Case for Reliance Disclosures

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests. The author is co-founder of Glawly, a legal research platform; that experience informs the article's perspective but the article does not evaluate, promote, or benefit any product.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: The legal profession has answered the arrival of generative AI with a single instruction: verify. ABA Formal Opinion 512 requires "an appropriate degree of independent verification or review"; state bar opinions and more than twenty-five federal standing orders say the same in different words. This article argues that the instruction, as applied to retrieval-augmented legal research tools, is presently undischargeable: the duty it states cannot be performed, because performing it requires information about how a given tool fails, namely its error composition, its detectability characteristics, its temporal coverage, and its silent design behaviors, that only vendors possess and no vendor discloses. The argument is doctrinal, not empirical: professional duties presuppose epistemic access to the facts that make compliance possible, and where a duty's informational preconditions are controlled by a third party, the duty propagates into a demand on that party. The article's constructive half specifies the demand. It derives, requirement by requirement from the law of lawyering, a documentation artifact, the Reliance Card, stating what a legal AI vendor must disclose for an attorney's use of the tool to be capable of satisfying Rules 1.1, 3.3, and 5.3. A qualitative gap analysis against the public record shows that no current commercial tool satisfies any tier of the specification. The article contributes to legal scholarship a systematized impossibility argument with a doctrinal mechanism for resolving it, and to computer science a documentation standard in the lineage of Model Cards whose fields are derived not from ethical aspiration but from enforceable professional obligation, a derivation method portable to medicine, engineering, and every other profession whose members are now being told to verify.

title: Financial Constraints, Employment Opportunities and Work-Study Balance: An Empirical Analysis of International Students' Well-Being in Germany

detail.title: Financial Constraints, Employment Opportunities and Work-Study Balance: An Empirical Analysis of International Students' Well-Being in Germany

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no relevant financial or non-financial conflicts of interest to disclose related to this research.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study collected primary data via an anonymous online survey distributed to international students. Prior to accessing the main questionnaire, all participants were presented with information regarding the confidentiality of their private information and provided their informed consent to participate.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was conducted as a Master's thesis for the Faculty of Economics and Management at Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg. It received no specific grant or external funding from any agency in the public, commercial or not-for-profit sectors.
declarations.clinicalTrialRegistration: Not applicable. This study is an empirical survey-based economic and social research paper.

detail.abstract: International students in Germany face a combination of financial pressure, employment demands and academic obligations that can take a toll on their mental well-being. This study empirically investigates how financial constraints (both subjective and objective), employment quality, work-study balance and socio-cultural integration factors associate with the mental well-being of this demographic. Utilising a quantitative cross-sectional design, primary data was collected via an online survey from 169 international students currently enrolled in German higher education institutions. The research employed statistical methods including ordinary least squares (OLS) regression, non-parametric tests, Welch´s two-sample t-tests, bootstrapped structural equation modelling (SEM) and multiple linear regression (MLR) to test the hypotheses. The empirical findings demonstrate that subjective financial constraint is the single strongest negative predictor of an international student's mental well-being. Holding student debt, and the level of debt concerns were both associated with lower well-being. In terms of employment, the study challenges the binary view of working versus nonworking. Students engaged in skilled, study related jobs reported significantly higher mental well-being compared to those in unskilled positions, validating the employment enrichment model. The study also confirms through SEM mediation analysis that academic performance acts as a critical mechanism connecting work study imbalance to overall psychological health; greater workstudy imbalance lowers academic grades, which subsequently damages mental well-being. Students from EU countries reported better well-being than non-EU students, though this advantage disappeared once financial constraint was accounted for. German language proficiency showed no significant relationship with well-being at all. Together these findings suggest that financial security, rather than cultural background or language skills, is the central lever for supporting international students´ mental health in Germany.

title: The Oxytocin-Driven Domesticity Protocol (ODDP): Evolutionary Roots of Tactile Dominance and Their Projection onto Contemporary Management Systems

detail.abstract: This paper advances the hypothesis that the human drive toward tactile contact with animals-the impulse to stroke or handle a living body-is not a secondary byproduct of parental instinct, but a primary evolutionary protocol of domestication. Tactile stimulation is treated here as an instrument of directed biohacking: it induces oxytocinergic dependence in the recipient and attenuates defensive aggression. Within HR-Tech, the same protocol is read as the infrastructural basis of loyalty architectures-from physical comfort in the workplace to digital surrogates of social grooming. Drawing on neurobiology, ethology, and management science, the argument maps the mechanisms of soft dominance operating inside contemporary hierarchical systems.

title: Physics-Informed Safe Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning with Uncertainty-Aware Zero-shot Deployment for Variable-speed Heat-pump Building Control
affiliations: Tianjin University, Tianjin University and Tianjin University

detail.title: Physics-Informed Safe Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning with Uncertainty-Aware Zero-shot Deployment for Variable-speed Heat-pump Building Control
detail.abstract: The rapid electrification of building heating requires intelligent control strategies that can improve energy efficiency, reduce carbon emissions and maintain thermal comfort under uncertain operating conditions. However, existing rule-based, optimization-based and reinforcement-learning controllers often rely on building-specific calibration, suffer from limited generalization to unseen buildings and lack explicit safety guarantees during abnormal operation. This study proposes a physics-informed safe multi-agent reinforcement-learning framework with uncertainty-aware zero-shot deployment for variable-speed air-to-water heat-pump buildings. The proposed framework integrates a nonlinear physical model describing multi-node building thermal dynamics, hydronic heat transfer, heat-pump performance variation, frost-defrost behaviour, auxiliary heating and grid-interactive operation. A building-parameter-conditioned recurrent world model is developed by embedding physical consistency and uncertainty estimation into multi-step prediction, enabling control policy learning without target-building operational data. A centralized-training decentralized-execution multi-agent controller is then designed to coordinate heat-pump modulation, circulation-pump operation and auxiliary heating. An uncertainty-aware safety layer further ensures reliable deployment through constraint tightening, out-of-distribution detection, action projection and fallback control. The proposed framework is evaluated under heterogeneous unseen buildings, cold-humid frost conditions, electricity price and carbon-intensity variations and extreme-weather scenarios. Results show that the physics-informed world model improves prediction robustness, maintaining errors below approximately 5% for key thermal and heat-pump variables. Compared with rule-based operation, the proposed controller reduces seasonal operating cost and carbon emissions by 21.0% and 19.0%, respectively, increases seasonal coefficient of performance to 3.52, achieves 98.67% thermal comfort satisfaction and limits safety violations to 0.42%.

title: Attribution Space: A Missing Concept in HSE Theory

detail.title: Attribution Space: A Missing Concept in HSE Theory
detail.abstract: This paper introduces the concept of Attribution Space-defined as the structural elasticity within which an individual, following the discovery of a hazard or the occurrence of an incident, can attribute responsibility to factors other than their own actions. The paper argues that Attribution Space is a distinct analytical category not currently covered by existing HSE frameworks, including Attribution Theory, Safety Culture, or Root Cause Analysis. Where Attribution Theory explains how individuals cognitively assign cause, and Safety Culture addresses organizational norms around blame, Attribution Space describes the structural pathways available for responsibility deflection. The paper further grounds the concept in a boundedrationality premise: individuals facing accountability tend to adopt cost-minimizing responses when the perceived cost of admission exceeds the cost of deflection. It concludes that the purpose of reducing Attribution Space is not punishment, but attribution-forcing problems into the open so that they can be understood and corrected, not merely penalized.

title: Real Option Portfolios and the Theory of the Multinational Enterprise: Understanding Modes of International Involvement in the Digital Economy
affiliations: Durham University and Durham University Business School

detail.title: Real Option Portfolios and the Theory of the Multinational Enterprise: Understanding Modes of International Involvement in the Digital Economy

publicationDetails.detailsText: Forthcoming, Journal of International Business Studies

detail.abstract: The recent growth of the digital economy and technological advances created new patterns of FDI and international involvement. We contribute to the debate on nontraditional (NT) entry modes in a changing digital world-virtual presence, digital platforms, and innovation outposts. We provide fresh insights into real option theory (ROT) and MNE theory explaining new forms of international involvement within a dynamic ROT portfolio perspective. We discuss uncertainty and correlation among market conditions, knowledge redundancy, how NT modes entail MNE growth and switching options, and how they contribute to the MNE option portfolio. We discuss information options and other real options embedded in NT modes, and the factors influencing their values. Our article has practical relevance as many MNEs do not incorporate real options into their decision making. We encourage managers to understand that (1) uncertainty influences options beneficially, (2) NT modes create real options, and (3) these NT options create flexibility. Our ROT 'portfolio' perspective shows how uncertainty, market correlation and knowledge diversity influence a real option's contribution to MNE option portfolios, though they are context specific. Finally, we compare how ROT insights complement those from existing MNE theories.

title: System-oriented Governance for Micro-retrofitting Mountain-road Safety:,Quasi-experimental Evidence from Fujian Province, China
affiliations: Fuzhou University, Fuzhou University Town and Toronto Metropolitan University

detail.title: System-oriented Governance for Micro-retrofitting Mountain-road Safety:,Quasi-experimental Evidence from Fujian Province, China
detail.abstract: Mountain roads can be particularly treacherous, with significant crash risks often heightened by challenging terrain, high costs, and ecological concerns that limit reconstruction efforts. However, a promising solution lies in small, focused safety upgrades known as micro-retrofits. The key to their success hinges on accurately assessing risks, prioritizing budgets wisely, and learning from the implementation process. In this study, we introduce a governance framework that seamlessly connects various aspects of micro-retrofit programs on mountain roads. This framework encompasses everything from risk diagnosis and treatment bundling to budget prioritization, implementation, evaluation, and feedback. We applied it to a specific program in Fujian, China, examining 146 road segments from 2021 to 2025. Our benchmark point estimate suggests a 30.75% reduction. Additionally, our cost-effectiveness analysis revealed that for every 10,000 yuan invested, we could prevent roughly 0.041 crashes. These results highlight the incredible potential of micro-retrofits to enhance safety on mountain roads, especially when integrated into a transparent and well-structured governance cycle.

title: Salient Products in Multi-Product Price Competition: The Price Image Effect
affiliations: National University Singapore, Xi'an Jiaotong University (XJTU) - School of Management and NUS Business School - Department of Decision Sciences

detail.title: Salient Products in Multi-Product Price Competition: The Price Image Effect
detail.abstract: Problem definition. In many markets, a small set of highly visible products plays a disproportionate role in shaping a firm's perceived expensiveness. We study competitive multi-product pricing when such salient products affect not only their own demand but also the demand for the firm's entire assortment through a price-image channel. The central question is how firms should price salient and nonsalient products in equilibrium when a salient price can act as a strategic signal of the firm's overall price position. Methodology and results. We model each firm's price image as a max-affine function of salient product prices and embed it in a multinomial logit (MNL) demand system as a common utility shifter across the firm's products. This formulation captures key-value-item logic and max-gap anchoring: the product that drives price image may change endogenously as prices change. The model shows that salient products create a distinct competitive pricing tradeoff. Raising a salient product's price improves its own margin but worsens the firm's price image and depresses demand for the rest of the assortment; lowering it can function as a targeted competitive instrument whose benefit spills over to nonsalient products. Despite this cross-product coupling, each firm's best response is well defined. Moreover, in the baseline competitive model, a rival's full price vector affects a firm only through the rival's image-adjusted attractiveness, so equilibrium analysis reduces to a scalar fixed-point problem. This reduction clarifies when the market has a unique equilibrium, when multiple equilibria can arise, and how best-response dynamics select among them. Managerial implications. The results show that treating all products symmetrically can lead to systematically wrong competitive pricing decisions. In a simulated choice experiment with 800 observations, a price-image-blind MNL benchmark overprices the salient products and lies 8.7% from the true-model Nash equilibrium, while the estimated salient-product price-image model reduces this gap to 0.3%. We also illustrate the approach using a public four-brand camera conjoint dataset. The estimated model identifies zoom-and-video cameras as the salient product group. In the constructed multi-product pricing game, each brand prices its salient product below its nonsalient products, not because the salient product has low intrinsic utility, but because its price shapes the brand's overall image and therefore affects demand for the whole brand assortment.

title: The Organizational Silence Reflex: A Conceptual Framework for Understanding Voice Suppression at Leadership Decision Points

detail.title: The Organizational Silence Reflex: A Conceptual Framework for Understanding Voice Suppression at Leadership Decision Points
detail.abstract: Background: Organizational silence-the collective withholding of potentially meaningful information by employees-has been documented as a pervasive feature of organizational life with significant consequences for decision quality, safety, and organizational learning. While both the antecedents and outcomes of organizational silence have been studied, the specific mechanism through which individual leaders contribute to or disrupt silence cultures at critical decision moments has received insufficient theoretical attention. Objective: This paper proposes the Organizational Silence Reflex (OSR)-a conceptual framework explaining why employees suppress voice at high-stakes leadership decision points, and what role leader behavior plays in conditioning, sustaining, and potentially disrupting that reflex. Methods: Conceptual synthesis integrating organizational silence theory, voice behavior research, psychological safety theory, implicit cognition research, and practitioner observation from 15 years of senior management in industrial sectors including petrochemicals, defence, and automotive. Findings: The OSR is characterized as a rapid, partially unconscious cost-benefit calculation occurring at decision-critical moments, producing a default disposition toward silence unless specific override conditions are met. Three primary antecedents are identified: leader-generated behavioral cues that signal the cost of challenge, relationship preservation motivation, and epistemic deference to authority. Nine recurring organizational breaking points-high-stakes moments at which the OSR is most acute-are identified and described based on practitioner observation and integration with organizational silence research. Conclusion: Leaders who understand and recognize the Organizational Silence Reflex can make deliberate behavioral choices that disrupt it at critical moments. Organizations that do not attend to the OSR remain structurally blind to the information failures that silence creates, particularly at the moments of highest organizational consequence.

title: The Timing of Pricing: A Theory and Experiment on Freelance Co-Creation
affiliations: University of Washington-Bothell and

detail.title: The Timing of Pricing: A Theory and Experiment on Freelance Co-Creation
detail.abstract: On freelance platforms, where value is co-created through the joint effort of freelancers and customers, contract design plays a central managerial role. A key strategic choice concerns price timing: whether prices are set before collaboration begins (early pricing) or after the co-creation process is completed (late pricing). We develop a game-theoretic model comparing these contractual regimes. Under rational expectations, early pricing functions as a commitment device that coordinates mutual high effort, leading to superior product quality and welfare relative to late pricing. We test these predictions in a controlled laboratory experiment. Consistent with theory, early pricing leads freelancers to charge higher prices and earn greater profits than under late pricing. However, contrary to theoretical predictions, early pricing does not increase effort by either party and does not improve product quality or overall welfare. Instead, surplus shifts from customers to freelancers. We interpret this divergence as evidence of a behavioral failure of the commitment mechanism: freelancers use early prices to signal quality but do not follow through with costly effort. Our findings carry important managerial implications for gig economy platforms. Without complementary reputation or monitoring systems, fixed-price contracts may enable opportunistic behavior rather than support cooperative value creation.

title: Organizational Silence as Systemic Risk: A Case Analysis of Decision Failures in the Boeing 737 MAX Development Program

detail.title: Organizational Silence as Systemic Risk: A Case Analysis of Decision Failures in the Boeing 737 MAX Development Program
detail.abstract: Background: The Boeing 737 MAX crashes of October 2018 and March 2019, which claimed 346 lives across two accidents, constitute one of the most extensively documented organizational failures in aviation history. Congressional investigations, regulatory reviews, and journalistic investigations collectively documented that engineering concerns about the MCAS (Maneuvering Characteristics Augmentation System) were present within the organization but systematically failed to reach, or were suppressed from reaching, the decision-making levels at which they could have altered the program's course. Objective: This case analysis applies organizational silence theory — specifically, Morrison and Milliken's (2000) foundational framework and Vaughan's (1996) normalization of deviance concept — to the Boeing 737 MAX development program, examining the organizational mechanisms through which silence functioned as a systemic risk factor. Method: Qualitative case study design (Yin, 2014) drawing on publicly available primary sources including the U.S. House Committee Report (2020), NTSB investigation findings, FAA review documentation, and the Joint Authorities Technical Review (2019), integrated with theoretical analysis through organizational behavior and safety science frameworks. Findings: Four distinct organizational silence mechanisms are identified: (1) competitive pressure-induced schedule constraints that structurally discouraged safety challenge; (2) a hierarchical culture in which challenge was equated with disloyalty and organizational resistance; (3) regulatory capture that undermined the external voice function; and (4) distributed accountability structures that prevented individual responsibility for systemic outcomes. Together, these mechanisms produced what Morrison and Milliken (2000) define as a climate of silence — a structural organizational condition, not merely an individual or interpersonal failure. Conclusion: The Boeing 737 MAX case demonstrates that organizational silence is not merely a communication failure or cultural dysfunction — it is a structural property with measurable safety and operational consequences. High-risk industries require explicit organizational silence detection as a component of safety management systems.

title: Asymmetric Exit Cost as a Driver of Bureaucratic Drift

detail.title: Asymmetric Exit Cost as a Driver of Bureaucratic Drift
detail.abstract: A preliminary note on the status of this text-This is a theoretical note, that is, a proposed conceptual framework offered for discussion, not an empirical study. The simulations and numerical illustrations it contains serve to make the logic of the model explicit, not to validate it on real data; their parameters are chosen, not estimated. The aim is to put a structured and falsifiable hypothesis into circulation, on the understanding that it falls to later work-drawing on matched employer-employee data-to test, refine, or refute it. This paper proposes a simple causal model to explain a phenomenon that is widely observed but rarely formalized in a unified way: the tendency of certain organizational functions, once created, to justify their own existence and to grow independently of the value they produce. The central thesis is that this drift is determined neither by the size of the organization nor by the nature of its sector, but by a two-part condition: (1) the cost, to an individual, of leaving the relationship, and (2) the cost, to the organization, of losing that individual or of correcting the situation. Bureaucratic drift arises when the first cost is high and the second is low-it is the product of the two conditions, not their mere sum, that determines whether a real counterpower operates. An agent-based simulation (100 individuals, 36 months) illustrates the mechanism, and a formalization in three propositions shows that the trajectory of the system depends less on the initial level of the two costs than on their respective slopes over time-giving rise, in the non-linear case, to a turning point at which the balance of power reverses at a critical tenure.

title: Scoring the Near Miss: Two Engineering-Derived Hypotheses for AI Incident Escalation Design

detail.title: Scoring the Near Miss: Two Engineering-Derived Hypotheses for AI Incident Escalation Design
detail.abstract: Recent work has moved AI incident escalation criteria from proposal to empirical test: Gomez et al. (2026) develop an eight-criterion framework, including a near-miss gate, and stress-test it against ten documented AI incidents. They find that escalation triggers depend on a three-layer infrastructure of data, definitions, and thresholds, and identify design patterns that cause systematic under-detection. Two of these patterns are structurally identical to problems quality engineering has developed mature, quantitative methods to address: the binary, rather than graduated, treatment of near-miss signals, and the absence of a mechanism for aggregating individually sub-threshold harms across categories. This paper asks whether two such methods-FMEA-style severity-likelihooddetectability scoring, and statistical-process-control-style tolerance monitoring-can generate testable design hypotheses for these specific, named, unresolved limitations. A distributed manufacturing defect-detection system (ImmuneLine) motivates the inquiry but does not carry the argument. The paper does not claim these methods transfer directly, and treats the institutional, competitive, and legal differences between a single-owner factory and a multi-actor AI ecosystem as a first-class limitation.

title: The China Shock That Wasn't

detail.title: The China Shock That Wasn't
detail.abstract: The "China Shock" has become the dominant explanation for the sharp decline in U.S. manufacturing employment following China's accession to the World Trade Organization (WTO). While there has been much commentary questioning the size of the shock, that it happened has become almost universally accepted. This paper argues that the underlying premise is mistaken. It first draws on a large literature that shows there was was no aggregate "East Asia shock" to U.S. imports: the rise in imports from China largely reflect the rerouting of imports from other East Asian economies as global value chains reorganized to use China as a final-assembly platform. Second, U.S. manufacturing output did not contract following China's WTO accession; on the contrary, output growth accelerated even as employment continued its long-term decline, with most of the declines concentrated in the recessions of 2001 and 2008-2009 (as many have pointed out). Third, the paper identifies two major drivers of manufacturing job losses during the period of the China Shock that were purely domestic. The prolonged decline in interest rates associated with the era of monetary-policy primacy reduced firms' cost of capital and encouraged substitution of capital for labour during a period of rapid technological change-a "Fed Shock." At the same time, the rise of Walmart, Amazon, and the broader transformation of U.S. retail through big box stores and business-to-consumer e-commerce intensified price pressure on U.S. manufacturers and accelerated the reallocation of market share from less productive to more productive firms, replicating the selection effects commonly attributed to trade liberalization-a "Walmart/Amazon Shock." Taken together, these factors substantially confound the attribution of manufacturing employment losses to import competition from China. The paper concludes that the "China Shock" is a misdiagnosis of a broader structural transformation driven by domestic technological, financial, and organizational change rather than by trade with China itself. By the same token, the rise in U.S. protectionism motivated by the desire to recapture what was lost to China in the China Shock will prove to be ineffectual because it is not dealing with the actual causes.

detail.abstract: Traditional static models of capacity planning in public administration often fail to capture dynamic service network complexities. This study transitions from linear capacity frameworks to a multi-server queueing paradigm, utilizing a fluid approximation model to simulate the dynamics of the active server pool and system throughput. Calibrated with empirical data from 200 public sector managers and 10 case studies, the model demonstrates how server attrition degrades operational capacity over time. Statistical analysis reveals a strong positive correlation between service rate optimization via training and overall throughput (r = 0.72, p less than 0.01). Multiple regression shows that service rate optimization (beta = 0.45) and onboarding (beta = 0.30) are critical predictors, explaining 68% of the throughput variance (R-squared = 0.68). The fluid model illustrates that strategic, adaptive management - specifically attrition mitigation and training - is essential to prevent queue saturation, sustain public service throughput, and support regional socio-economic growth.

title: Understanding Research Capacity and Culture Among Oral Health Clinicians in a Large Public Dental Service in NSW, Australia

detail.title: Understanding Research Capacity and Culture Among Oral Health Clinicians in a Large Public Dental Service in NSW, Australia

declarations.declarationOfInterest: All authors declare no competing interests.

As an organisational workforce survey with no identifying information collected, full Human Research Ethics Committee review was not required. Participation was voluntary and anonymous.

detail.abstract:
Background: Research-active health services deliver higher-quality care, faster adoption of evidence, and better patient outcomes. Building research capacity and culture (RCC) within clinical workforces is widely recognised as a core function of high-performing health systems. Oral health clinicians remain among the least research-active health professional groups internationally yet have rarely been examined as a distinct workforce group using validated tools. This study assessed self-rated research skills and engagement among oral health clinicians in a large public dental service in Australia.

Methods: A cross-sectional, self-administered online survey using a modified validated Research Capacity and Culture Tool (RCCT) was distributed to all oral health clinicians at a public dental service in New South Wales, Australia. Data were collected via REDCap in March 2026. Respondents self-rated 15 individual research skills on a 10-point scale (1 = very low, 10 = very high; midpoint of 5 as threshold for adequate skill) and completed sections on research engagement, barriers, and support needs.

Findings: Eighty oral health professionals completed the survey: dental specialists (12·5%), dentists (36·2%), and other oral health professionals (51·2%). The overall average individual domain median score was 4·3 (95% CI 3·76–4·94), with 51·2% scoring at or above the midpoint. Literature-finding and critical appraisal were rated highest; securing funding, submitting ethics applications, and mentoring others were rated lowest. Most reported no publications (87·7%) and no grant applications (90·8%) in the past 12 months. The majority identified as "not engaged" (30·8%) or "interested but not actively engaged" (46·1%) with research.

Interpretation: Research activity was concentrated within a small subgroup of dental specialists, while most dentists and other oral health professionals expressed interest but were not actively engaged. Targeted, role-tailored capacity-building interventions supported by protected time, formal academic partnerships, and embedded research roles are needed to translate latent interest into sustained engagement.

title: Headwind or Tailwind? How Banks Interpret Borrowers' AI Exposure
affiliations: University of Padua - Department of Economics and Management , IESE Business School, University at Buffalo (SUNY) - School of Management and

detail.title: Headwind or Tailwind? How Banks Interpret Borrowers' AI Exposure
detail.abstract: General-purpose technologies create large opportunities, but they also make the identity of winners and losers difficult to determine in real time. We use banks as interpreters of the recent AI boom by studying how lenders revise internal probability-of-default (PD) estimates as public attention to AI rises after ChatGPT. Using European credit register data from AnaCredit, we find that banks lower assessed default risk for borrowers in more AI-exposed industries: a one-standard-deviation increase in AI attention is associated with about a 5% lower PD for highly exposed borrowers. This reassessment depends on both borrower production structure and lender information. The favorable effect is markedly weaker for labor-intensive firms, consistent with greater disruption risk when production depends heavily on labor: as AI attention rises by one standard deviation, assessed PD falls by about 7% for borrowers with below-median labor intensity but only 3\% for those with above-median labor intensity. Among banks lending to the same firm in the same quarter, lenders with substantial pre-ChatGPT specialization in the borrower's industry assign substantially lower PDs to highly AI-exposed borrowers than other co-lenders, while long-standing relationship lenders show much smaller differences. These findings show that firms' reliance on labor and lenders' sector-specific expertise shape how banks assess the credit implications of AI exposure.

detail.abstract: China's technological progress in recent decades has been viewed with admiration, alarm, and (in some cases) doubt. To better understand the Chinese innovation ecosystem, we compile a dataset of almost 14 million domestic Chinese patent publications. We focus on the subset of critical technologies identified by the U.S. Department of Defense. Several surprising patterns emerge from the data: Chinese patenting is strongly associated with other measures of innovative progress; patents are not concentrated in corporate giants such as Huawei; universities have played a key role in innovation, much greater than state-owned enterprises or government-owned facilities; and fewer than one in ten Chinese critical technology patents involves an inventor with U.S. experience or training. Finally, using four text-based measures of patent quality, we show that the rise of Chinese patenting in critical technologies has not been associated with a decline in quality relative to the U.S. awards.

title: Tax Policy Predictability and Foreign Investment Resilience in Resource-Rich Africa
affiliations: Birmingham City University, University of Derby, Babcock University, University of Sunderland and Northumbria University

detail.title: Tax Policy Predictability and Foreign Investment Resilience in Resource-Rich Africa
detail.abstract: Foreign investment strategy is often framed as a choice between high and low corporate tax rates. This paper argues that, in resource-rich African economies, tax-policy predictability may matter more for resilient investment than the tax rate itself. Resilience is operationalised as the inverse log transformation of three-year volatility in foreign direct investment (FDI) net inflows relative to GDP, avoiding the common error of treating flow volume as resilience. A panel of 28 resource-rich African economies over 2005–2023 is estimated with country and year fixed effects and Driscoll–Kraay standard errors. A one-percentage-point increase in the five-year dispersion of statutory corporate tax rates is associated with a 0.051 decline in the resilience index, equivalent to approximately 5.2% higher gross FDI volatility. The statutory rate level is not significant in the primary specification, while general institutional credibility does not buffer tax instability. The result survives alternative tax-instability and resilience measures, dynamic controls, resource-rent and trade controls, country-specific trends, stricter resource-rich thresholds and leave-one-country-out tests. The study advances a predictability-based tax strategy: credible multi-year tax paths may support more durable foreign investment without relying on a race to the bottom.

title: Content Marketing in The Business Landscape: A Global Scientometric Review and Strategic Framework for Business Transformation
affiliations: University of Brahmanbaria, University of Brahmanbaria, University of Brahmanbaria and Comilla University

detail.title: Content Marketing in The Business Landscape: A Global Scientometric Review and Strategic Framework for Business Transformation
detail.abstract: This research aims to explore and evaluate the academic literature surrounding content marketing, employing bibliometric analysis to figure out the principal themes, authors, sources, highly cited works, leading countries, the most impactful keywords, and thematic content. A comprehensive bibliometric analysis was conducted on 490 publications from the Scopus Database spanning from 2008 to 2024, encompassing a range of formats such as published articles, conference papers, and book chapters. The research project has employed VOSviewer (1.6.20 version) software and Excel for its execution. This paper presents the research findings, offering a comprehensive overview of insights and trends in the content marketing research domain. It includes patterns of scientific publications, important contributors such as authors and countries, sources, and the most cited and co-cited papers to uncover seminal publications and foundational knowledge. The co-occurrence keyword and bibliographic coupling analyses were employed to delineate intellectual networks and identify novel themes. Eight development themes and two thematic clusters were derived from co-word frequency and bibliometric coupling, respectively. A focused content analysis was conducted on 42 recent articles selected for their significance, accuracy, and reference impact. It identified seven main research streams: (1) Emerging Markets Innovation; (2) Innovation and Value Creation; (3) Banking Industry and Financial Content Marketing; (4) Innovative Corporate Strategy and Sustainable Development; (5) Modernizing & Leveraging Healthcare; (6) SME Development; and (7). Branding Higher Education. From an empirical standpoint, the rolling out of content marketing enhances an organization's competitive advantage and fosters corporate innovation by serving as a low-cost, data-rich vehicle for market research, co-creation, and agile business transformation, resulting in a significant improvement in its social and economic standing.​
